## Round 420: S5f-10b, second half, part 1 — counting the translates in a ball, and the Schur bound (`src/KubotaBallCount.lean`)

**What it is.** The seventh step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation". Round 419's next step planned `T_R` on the quotient, beginning with the counting function and the Schur bound. This round proves both, for any subgroup `Γ` of `SL_2(ℤ[ω])` and any partition of unity `ρ` for it, with `ν = ρ dμ`:

- `γq ∈ B_R(p)` exactly when `γ⁻¹p ∈ B_R(q)`, for `p, q` in upper half-space (`Eis.mem_hball_slAct_iff`);
- `N(p, q) = #{γ ∈ Γ : γq ∈ B_R(p)}`, a sum in `[0, ∞]`, has `∫ρ(q)N(p, q) dμ(q) = μ(B_R(p))` (`Eis.lintegral_cntB`) and `N(p, q) = N(q, p)` on upper half-space (`Eis.cntB_comm`);
- `μ(B_R(p)) = μ(B_R(0, 1)) = V_R` for `p` in upper half-space, and `V_R < ∞` for `R ≥ 0` (`Eis.uhsMeasure_hball` and `Eis.uhsMeasure_hball_lt_top`);
- the Schur bound `∫∫N(p, q)a(p)b(q) dν(q) dν(p) ≤ V_R·(∫a² dν)^{1/2}(∫b² dν)^{1/2}` for measurable `a, b ≥ 0` (`Eis.lintegral_cntB_mul_le`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaBallCount.lean`, 280 lines, 17 theorems, 3 definitions and 1 instance; each of its 17 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The invariant under `SL_2(ℤ[ω])`** (**`mem_hball_slAct_iff`**, with `ppi_slAct`, `ppi_comm` and `measurable_ppi₂`).
- **The counting function** (`cntB`, a definition; **`lintegral_cntB`** and **`cntB_comm`**, with `measurable_hball_ind`, `measurable_hball_ind_left`, `measurable_cntB`, `measurable_cntB_left` and `measurable_cntB_right`).
- **The volume of a ball** (`VB`, a definition; **`uhsMeasure_hball`** and **`uhsMeasure_hball_lt_top`**).
- **The Schur bound** (`muR`, a definition, and the instance `sFinite_muR`; **`lintegral_cntB_mul_le`**, with `ae_muR_UHS`, `lintegral_cntB_muR` and `lintegral_cntB_muR'`).

**The proof.**

- **The invariant.** Round 418's `pinv_actP` for `γ⁻¹` gives `ppi(γ⁻¹p, q) = ppi(p, γq)`, and `ppi` is symmetric.
- **Unfolding.** Round 386's `lintegral_unfold` with `Φ_γ(q) = 1_{B_R(p)}(γq)` and `Ψ = 1_{B_R(p)}` gives `∫ρ(q)Σ_γ1_{B_R(p)}(γq) dμ(q) = ∫1_{B_R(p)} dμ`.
- **Symmetry.** Reindexing `γ ↦ γ⁻¹` and the invariant.
- **The volume.** `g = (1, z; 0, 1)(√v, 0; 0, 1/√v)` maps `(0, 1)` to `p = (z, v)` and preserves `μ` (round 383's `measurePreserving_actP`). It maps `B_R(0, 1)` onto `B_R(p)` off the null set `v ≤ 0` (round 418's `mem_hball_actP`). On `B_R(0, 1)`, `v ≥ 1/(R + 2)` (round 418's `hball_one_subset`), so the density `v⁻³` is at most `(R + 2)³` there.
- **The Schur bound.** On `ν ⊗ ν` with density `N`, Hölder's inequality with exponents `2, 2` (Mathlib's `ENNReal.lintegral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq`) bounds `∫a(p)b(q)` by the product of the square roots of `∫N(p, q)a(p)²` and `∫N(p, q)b(q)²`. By Tonelli and the unfolding, these are `V_R∫a² dν` and, with the symmetry, `V_R∫b² dν`.

**Against the plan.** Round 419's next step listed:

- "the counting function `N(p, q) = #{γ : ppi(p, γq) ≤ R}`, with `∫ρ(q)N(p, q) dμ(q) = μ(B_R(p))` by round 386's `lintegral_unfold`, and `N(p, q) = N(q, p)`";
- "the Schur bound by the volume of a ball".

Both landed as listed. The counting function is not proved finite at every pair. The Schur bound uses only its integrals, and it is finite for `ν ⊗ ν`-almost every pair. The operator, its self-adjointness and its action on automorphic functions remain.

**The next step.** S5f-10b, second half, part 2. Take a unitary character `χ` on `Γ` and the sesquilinear form `B(f, g) = Σ_γ conj χ(γ)·∫∫1_{B_R(p)}(γq)·conj f(q)·g(p) dν(q) dν(p)` on `L²(ν)`, with `|B(f, g)| ≤ V_R‖f‖‖g‖` from this round's Schur bound. The plan:

- the operator `K` with `⟪Kf, g⟫ = B(f, g)` (Mathlib's `InnerProductSpace.continuousLinearMapOfBilin`);
- `K` self-adjoint, from `χ(γ⁻¹) = conj χ(γ)`, this round's `mem_hball_slAct_iff` and the swap of the two integrals;
- for automorphic `u` with `∫ρ|u|² < ∞`, `K` applied to `u` is `T_Ru` almost everywhere.

*(Round 421: the first two items landed, `Eis.inner_ballOp` and `Eis.isSelfAdjoint_ballOp`; the third is round 421's next step. See round 421.)*

## Round 421: S5f-10b, second half, part 2 — the ball average as a self-adjoint operator (`src/KubotaBallOp.lean`)

**What it is.** The eighth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation". Round 420's next step planned the ball operator on `L²(ν)`, `ν = ρ dμ`, from a sesquilinear form, and its self-adjointness. This round proves both, for any subgroup `Γ` of `SL_2(ℤ[ω])`, any unitary character `χ` on `Γ` and any partition of unity `ρ` for `Γ`:

- `χ(γ⁻¹) = conj χ(γ)` for `γ ∈ Γ` (`Eis.IsUChar.map_inv`);
- the kernel `k(p, q) = Σ_γ χ(γ)·1_{B_R(p)}(γq)` has `|k(p, q)| ≤ N(p, q)` (`Eis.enorm_bker_le`) and `k(q, p) = conj k(p, q)` on upper half-space (`Eis.bker_swap`);
- the form `B(f, g) = ∫conj k(p, q)·conj f(q)·g(p) d(ν ⊗ ν)` has `|B(f, g)| ≤ V_R‖f‖‖g‖` for `R ≥ 0` (`Eis.norm_bform_le`);
- the operator `K = ballOp` with `⟪Kf, g⟫ = B(f, g)` (`Eis.inner_ballOp`) is self-adjoint (`Eis.isSelfAdjoint_ballOp`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaBallOp.lean`, 337 lines, 23 theorems and 6 definitions, one of them the structure `IsUChar`; each of its 23 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **Unitary characters** (`IsUChar`, a structure; `IsUChar.map_one` and **`IsUChar.map_inv`**).
- **The kernel** (`bker`, a definition; **`enorm_bker_le`** and **`bker_swap`**, with `measurable_hball_indC` and `measurable_bker`).
- **The form** (`bformF` and `bform`, definitions; **`norm_bform_le`**, with `lintegral_enorm_sq_rpow`, `measurable_bformF`, `lintegral_bformF_le` and `integrable_bformF`).
- **The operator** (`bformCLM` and `ballOp`, definitions; **`inner_ballOp`**, with `ae_snd_add`, `ae_fst_add`, `ae_snd_smul`, `ae_fst_smul`, `bform_add_left`, `bform_smul_left`, `bform_add_right` and `bform_smul_right`).
- **Self-adjointness** (**`isSelfAdjoint_ballOp`**, with `ae_prod_UHS` and `bform_eq_conj`).

**The proof.**

- **The kernel.** `k` is a sum over the countable group `Γ` of measurable functions, measurable by Mathlib's `Measurable.tsum`. Mathlib's `enorm_tsum_le_tsum_enorm` bounds `|k|` by `Σ_γ|χ(γ)|·1 = N` with no summability hypothesis. For the symmetry, `conj` passes through the sum (Mathlib's `Complex.conj_tsum`), the sum is reindexed by `γ ↦ γ⁻¹`, `χ(γ⁻¹) = conj χ(γ)`, and round 420's `mem_hball_slAct_iff` exchanges `1_{B_R(q)}(γ⁻¹p)` with `1_{B_R(p)}(γq)`.
- **The form.** `|conj k·conj f(q)·g(p)| ≤ N(p, q)|g(p)||f(q)|`, and round 420's Schur bound gives `∫ ≤ V_R‖g‖₂‖f‖₂`, finite for `R ≥ 0` (round 420's `uhsMeasure_hball_lt_top`). So the integrand is integrable, and `|B(f, g)| ≤ V_R‖f‖‖g‖`.
- **Linearity.** The representatives of `f₁ + f₂` and `cf` agree with `f₁ + f₂` and `cf` almost everywhere, and the two projections of `ν ⊗ ν` carry this to the product (Mathlib's `Measure.QuasiMeasurePreserving.ae_eq_comp`). Mathlib's `LinearMap.mk₂'ₛₗ` and `LinearMap.mkContinuous₂` give a bounded sesquilinear map, and `InnerProductSpace.continuousLinearMapOfBilin` gives `K`.
- **Self-adjointness.** `conj B(g, f)` is the integral of `k(p, q)·g(q)·conj f(p)`. Swapping the coordinates of `ν ⊗ ν` (Mathlib's `integral_prod_swap`) and `k(q, p) = conj k(p, q)` almost everywhere turn it into `B(f, g)`. Mathlib's `ContinuousLinearMap.eq_adjoint_iff` then gives `K† = K`.

**Against the plan.** Round 420's next step listed "the operator `K` with `⟪Kf, g⟫ = B(f, g)` (Mathlib's `InnerProductSpace.continuousLinearMapOfBilin`)" and "`K` self-adjoint, from `χ(γ⁻¹) = conj χ(γ)`, this round's `mem_hball_slAct_iff` and the swap of the two integrals". Both landed as listed. Round 420 wrote the form as a sum over `γ` of integrals. This round writes it with the kernel `k` inside one integral on `ν ⊗ ν`, so that linearity and the swap each concern one integral. The third item, `K` on automorphic functions, remains.

**The next step.** S5f-10b, second half, part 3: the kernel representation and automorphic functions. The plan:

- `(Kf)(p) = ∫k(p, q)f(q) dν(q)` for `ν`-almost every `p`, with the Schur bound in its `L²` form;
- for `u` with `u(γq) = χ(γ)u(q)` and `∫ρ|u|² < ∞`, `∫k(p, q)u(q) dν(q) = ∫_{B_R(p)} u dμ`, by unfolding with round 386's `IsPU.tsum_inv`, so `Ku = T_Ru` almost everywhere. *(Round 422: landed as planned, `Eis.ballOp_ae_eq_kfun` and `Eis.ballOp_toLp_ae_eq_bavg`. See round 422.)*

## Round 422: S5f-10b, second half, part 3 — the ball operator through its kernel, and on automorphic functions (`src/KubotaBallKernel.lean`)

**What it is.** The ninth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the last part of S5f-10b. Round 421 built the self-adjoint ball operator `K` on `L²(ν)`, `ν = ρ dμ`, from a sesquilinear form. Round 421's next step planned its kernel representation and its action on automorphic functions. This round proves both:

- `∫(∫N(p, q)b(q) dν(q))² dν(p) ≤ V_R²∫b² dν` for measurable `b ≥ 0` (`Eis.lintegral_sq_cntB_le`);
- `Kf = ∫k(·, q)f(q) dν(q)` almost everywhere, for `f` in `L²(ν)` and `R ≥ 0` (`Eis.ballOp_ae_eq_kfun`);
- for `u` with `u(γq) = χ(γ)u(q)` (`Eis.IsAut`), `∫k(p, q)u(q) dν(q) = ∫_{B_R(p)} u dμ` whenever `∫N(p, q)|u(q)| dν(q) < ∞` (`Eis.kfun_eq_bavg`);
- for such `u`, measurable and in `L²(ν)`, `Ku = T_Ru` almost everywhere, with `T_Ru(p) = ∫_{B_R(p)} u dμ` round 418's `bavg` (`Eis.ballOp_toLp_ae_eq_bavg`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaBallKernel.lean`, 358 lines, 17 theorems and 2 definitions; each of its 17 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The Schur bound in its `L²` form** (**`lintegral_sq_cntB_le`**, with `sq_lintegral_cntB_le`).
- **The kernel representation** (`kfun`, a definition; **`ballOp_ae_eq_kfun`**, with `lintegral_enorm_sq_lt_top`, `aestronglyMeasurable_kfun`, `enorm_kfun_le`, `memLp_kfun`, `inner_toLp_kfun` and `ballOp_eq_toLp_kfun`).
- **Automorphic functions** (`IsAut`, a definition; **`kfun_eq_bavg`** and **`ballOp_toLp_ae_eq_bavg`**, with `IsPU.le_one`, `tsum_toReal_rho_inv`, `IsAut.enorm`, `lintegral_hball_enorm`, `conj_mul_self_of_uchar` and `lintegral_enorm_sq_lt_top_of_memLp`).

**The proof.**

- **The `L²` Schur bound.** For `p` in upper half-space, Hölder's inequality for the measure `N(p, q) dν(q)` gives `(∫N(p, q)b(q) dν)² ≤ (∫N(p, q) dν)(∫N(p, q)b(q)² dν)`, and round 420's `lintegral_cntB_muR` makes the first factor `V_R`. Tonelli and round 420's `lintegral_cntB_muR'` finish.
- **The kernel representation.** `|∫k(p, q)f(q) dν(q)| ≤ ∫N(p, q)|f(q)| dν(q)` by round 421's `enorm_bker_le`, so the `L²` Schur bound puts the kernel function in `L²(ν)`. Its inner product with `g` is `∫conj(∫k(p, q)f(q) dν(q))·g(p) dν(p)`, which Fubini (Mathlib's `integral_prod`) turns into round 421's form `B(f, g)`. So it has the same inner products as `Kf`, and is `Kf`.
- **Automorphic functions.** `∫k(p, q)u(q) dν(q) = Σ_γ χ(γ)∫1_{B_R(p)}(γq)u(q)ρ(q) dμ(q)` (Mathlib's `integral_tsum`; the sum of the integrals of the absolute values is `∫N(p, q)|u(q)| dν(q)`). Moving each term by `γ⁻¹` (round 383's `integral_actP`) and using `u(γ⁻¹q) = conj χ(γ)·u(q)` gives `∫ρ(γ⁻¹q)·1_{B_R(p)}(q)u(q) dμ(q)`. Summing back over `γ`, `Σ_γρ(γ⁻¹q) = 1` (round 386's `IsPU.tsum_inv`, with `ρ ≤ 1` on upper half-space) leaves `∫_{B_R(p)} u dμ`. The second interchange needs `∫_{B_R(p)}|u| dμ < ∞`, which round 386's `lintegral_unfold` turns into `∫N(p, q)|u(q)| dν(q)` (`lintegral_hball_enorm`).
- **On `L²(ν)`.** The `L²` Schur bound makes `∫N(p, q)|u(q)| dν(q)` finite for `ν`-almost every `p`.

**Against the plan.** Round 421's next step listed "`(Kf)(p) = ∫k(p, q)f(q) dν(q)` for `ν`-almost every `p`, with the Schur bound in its `L²` form" and "for `u` with `u(γq) = χ(γ)u(q)` and `∫ρ|u|² < ∞`, `∫k(p, q)u(q) dν(q) = ∫_{B_R(p)} u dμ`, by unfolding with round 386's `IsPU.tsum_inv`, so `Ku = T_Ru` almost everywhere". Both landed as listed; the second also needs `u` measurable. S5f-10b is complete. Round 418's plan for S5f-10 continues with the Eisenstein series.

**The next step.** S5f-10c, the truncated Eisenstein series. For `Γ = Γ_1(3)` with Kubota's character (round 361's `kub`, a unitary character on `Γ_1(3)` by round 387's `norm_kub` and round 382's `kub_mul`), the plan is:

- a truncation `h_s`, round 387's series restricted to `v(γw) ≥ Y` in each term, for `Y` large;
- `E_s − h_s` measurable, automorphic and in `L²(ν)` for `Re s > 2` (round 388's growth bound);
- `T_R E_s = ĥ(s)E_s` for `Re s > 2`, from round 418's `bavg_cpow` summed over the series;
- `g_s = (K − ĥ(s))(E_s − h_s)` computed as an explicit function supported in the shells `Ye^{−r} ≤ v(γw) ≤ Ye^r`. *(Round 423: all four landed, `Eis.memLp_eisLow`, `Eis.bavg_eis1` and `Eis.ballOp_eisLow_sub`, with `Y ≥ 0` in place of `Y` large; the support is proved in the wider shells `Y/(R + 2) ≤ v(γw) < (R + 2)Y`. See round 423.)*

## Round 423: S5f-10c — the truncated Eisenstein series, and `g_s` (`src/KubotaEisTrunc.lean`)

**What it is.** The tenth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and S5f-10c. Round 422's next step planned the truncated Eisenstein series for `Γ_1(3)` with Kubota's character. This round proves it through pseudo-Eisenstein series of a general profile, with `ν = ρ_G dμ` for a partition of unity `ρ_G` of `Γ_1(3)` and `K` round 421's ball operator:

- the pseudo-Eisenstein series `E(f)(w) = Σ_{(c, d)} (c/d)₃·f(v(γw))` is automorphic for every `f` (`Eis.isAut_pseis`), and in `L²(ν)` for `f` measurable and bounded on `(0, ∞)` with `|f(v)| ≤ C·v^τ` there, `C ≥ 0`, `τ > 2` (`Eis.memLp_pseis`);
- `T_R E(f) = E(Bf)` with `Bf(v) = ∫_{B_R(0, v)} f(v′) dμ` (`Eis.bavg_pseis`), so `T_R E_s = ĥ(s)·E_s` for `Re s > 2` (`Eis.bavg_eis1`);
- with `h_s = E(1[v ≥ Y]v^s)`, `E_s − h_s = E(1[v < Y]v^s)` is in `L²(ν)` for `Re s > 2` and `Y ≥ 0` (`Eis.memLp_eisLow`);
- `(K − ĥ(s))(E_s − h_s) = g_s` in `L²(ν)` for `Re s > 2` (`Eis.ballOp_eisLow_sub`), where `g_s = E(G_s)` with `G_s(v) = B(1[v′ < Y]v′^s)(v) − ĥ(s)·1[v < Y]v^s`; `G_s(v) = 0` unless `Y/(R + 2) ≤ v < (R + 2)Y` (`Eis.gProf_eq_zero_of_lt` and `Eis.gProf_eq_zero_of_ge`), and `g_s` is in `L²(ν)` for every `s` with `Re s ≥ 0` (`Eis.memLp_gfun`). *(Round 516: `memLp_gfun` is removed; round 424's `memLp_gfun_all` proves this for every `s`.)*

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaEisTrunc.lean`, 784 lines, 53 theorems, 10 definitions and 4 instances; each of its 53 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **`Γ_1(3)` with Kubota's character** (`rhoG`, a definition, and the instances `finite_quot_three`, `finiteIndex_Gam3` and `finite_quot_Gam3`; `isUChar_kub` and `isPU_rhoG`).
- **Pseudo-Eisenstein series** (`psTerm` and `pseis`, definitions; **`isAut_pseis`**, **`measurable_pseis`** and **`summable_psTerm`**, with `eisTerm_eq_psTerm`, `eis1_eq_pseis`, `psTerm_of_not_bRow`, `psTerm_add`, `psTerm_const_mul`, `psTerm_congr`, `pseis_congr`, `psTerm_rowMul`, `measurable_height`, `measurable_psTerm`, `norm_psTerm_le`, `pseis_add`, `pseis_const_mul` and `pseis_sub`). *(Round 516: `eisTerm_eq_psTerm`, which no proof used, is removed.)*
- **Growth at the cusps, and `L²`** (**`norm_pseis_slAct_sub_le`**, **`lintegral_puLe_top_mul_lt_top`** and **`memLp_pseis`**, with `height_slAct_of_fst` and `memLp_two_of_lintegral`).
- **The ball average** (`bTrans`, a definition; **`bavg_pseis`** and **`bavg_eis1`**, with `le_snd_of_mem_hball`, `snd_le_of_mem_hball`, `height_le_of_mem_hball`, `bavg_snd_eq`, `psTerm_eq_of_row` and `bavg_psTerm`).
- **The truncation** (`lowF`, `highF`, `eisLow` and `eisHigh`, definitions; **`eis1_eq_eisLow_add_eisHigh`** and **`memLp_eisLow`**, with `measurable_lowF`, `measurable_highF`, `norm_lowF_le`, `norm_lowF_le_Y`, `norm_highF_le`, `isAut_eisLow` and `measurable_eisLow`). *(Round 516: `measurable_highF`, which no proof used, is removed.)*
- **`g_s`** (`gProf` and `gfun`, definitions, and the instance `sFinite_uhsMeasure`; **`ballOp_eisLow_sub`**, **`gProf_eq_zero_of_lt`**, **`gProf_eq_zero_of_ge`** and **`memLp_gfun`**, with `uhsMeasure_hball_lt_top_of_mem`, `norm_bTrans_le_const`, `norm_bTrans_le`, `bavg_eisLow_sub`, `measurable_bTrans`, `measurable_gProf`, `norm_gProf_le` and `norm_gProf_le_pow`). *(Round 516: `memLp_gfun` is removed, as above.)*

**The proof.**

- **`Γ_1(3)`.** `κ` is a unitary character on `Γ_1(3)` by round 382's `kub_mul_Gam3` and round 387's `norm_kub`. `Γ_1(3)` is the kernel of reduction modulo `3` (round 382), and `ℤ[ω]/3` is finite by round 389's `finite_quot_three_mul`, so `Γ_1(3)` has finite index. Round 386's `isPU_puLe_top` gives `ρ_G`.
- **Pseudo-Eisenstein series.** Round 387's proof of automorphy, through the bijection `(c, d) ↦ (c, d)g⁻¹` with round 387's `height_rowMul` and `cub_rowMul`, holds with `f(v(γw))` in place of `v(γw)^s`. Round 387's series is `E(v^s)` by definition (`eis1_eq_pseis` is `rfl`).
- **At the cusps.** At `g·w`, the bottom rows with `(c, d)g = (0, e)` have height `v`, since `e` is a unit (round 388's `isUnit_rowMul_snd`), and together they give `a_g·f(v)`. The other rows are bounded by `C` times round 388's sum, `summable_height_ne`.
- **`L²`.** `∫ρ_G F dμ` is a sum over the finitely many cosets `q` of `∫ρ(q·p)F(p) dμ(p)`. Moving each term by `q⁻¹` (round 386's `lintegral_slAct`) gives `∫ρ(p)F(q⁻¹·p) dμ(p)`. `ρ` vanishes off the Siegel set (round 385's `rhoK_le`), where `F(q⁻¹·)` is bounded, and `∫ρ dμ < ∞` (round 385's `lintegral_rhoK_lt_top`). For `F = |E(f)|²` the bound at the cusps gives `|E(f)(g·w)| ≤ |a_g|·D + C·cuspC(τ)·2^{τ−2}` on the Siegel set.
- **The ball average.** On `B_R(p)`, `(v − v′)² ≤ Rvv′`, so `v/(R + 2) ≤ v′ ≤ (R + 2)v`. Each term of `E(f)` on the ball is therefore at most `C(R + 2)^τ` times the majorant at `p`, the sum of the integrals is finite, and Mathlib's `integral_tsum` exchanges sum and integral. Each term is moved by an element of `Γ_1(3)` with bottom row `(c, d)` (round 387's `exists_Gam3_of_BRow`, round 418's `bavg_comp_actP`) and then by the translation to `(0, v)`, which leaves a function of the height unchanged. For `f = v^s`, round 418's `bavg_cpow` gives `Bf = ĥ(s)v^s`.
- **`g_s`.** `T_R(E_s − h_s) − ĥ(s)(E_s − h_s) = E(B(1[v < Y]v^s)) − E(ĥ(s)·1[v < Y]v^s)` pointwise, and round 422's `ballOp_toLp_ae_eq_bavg` makes it the identity in `L²(ν)`. For `(R + 2)v < Y`, the ball `B_R(0, v)` lies below height `Y`, where `B(1[v′ < Y]v′^s) = B(v′^s) = ĥ(s)v^s`. For `v ≥ (R + 2)Y`, it lies at height `Y` or above, where `1[v′ < Y]v′^s` vanishes. So `G_s` is bounded by `(V_R + |ĥ(s)|)Y^σ` and vanishes below `Y/(R + 2)`, which gives `|G_s(v)| ≤ M((R + 2)/Y)³v³`, and `memLp_pseis` applies with `τ = 3`. The ball transform is measurable by Mathlib's `StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right'`, applied to the indicator of `{(v, q) : q ∈ B_R(0, v)}`.

**Against the plan.** Round 422's next step listed:

- "a truncation `h_s`, round 387's series restricted to `v(γw) ≥ Y` in each term, for `Y` large";
- "`E_s − h_s` measurable, automorphic and in `L²(ν)` for `Re s > 2` (round 388's growth bound)";

All four landed, as statements about pseudo-Eisenstein series of a general profile. `Y ≥ 0` suffices (`Y > 0` for `g_s` in `L²(ν)`). The support of `G_s` is proved in the shells `Y/(R + 2) ≤ v < (R + 2)Y`. For `R = 2cosh r − 2` these contain the planned shells, since `R + 2 = 2cosh r > e^r`; the planned ones would need the exact range of heights on a ball. This round also proves `g_s` in `L²(ν)` for every `s` with `Re s ≥ 0`, which the plan had not listed.

## Round 424: S5f-10d — `s ↦ g_s` is holomorphic into `L²`, and the resolvent applied to it (`src/KubotaGHolo.lean`)

**What it is.** The eleventh step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and S5f-10d. Round 423 wrote `g_s = (K − ĥ(s))(E_s − h_s)` as the pseudo-Eisenstein series `E(G_s)` of a profile vanishing outside the shells `Y/(R + 2) ≤ v < (R + 2)Y`. This round proves, with `ν = ρ_G dμ` as in round 423:

- for `f` measurable, vanishing on `(0, a)` and bounded by `D` on `(0, ∞)`, `‖E(f)‖₂ ≤ psC(a)^{1/2}·D` with a constant depending only on `a` (`Eis.eLpNorm_pseis_le`);
- `G_s(v) = ∫_{B_R(0, v)} (1[v′ < Y] − 1[v < Y])·v′^s dμ` (`Eis.gProf_eq_gInt`), and Taylor's bound for it in `s`, uniform in `v` (`Eis.gInt_taylor`);
- `g_s` is in `L²(ν)` for every `s`, and `s ↦ g_s` is complex-differentiable into `L²(ν)` at every `s`, with derivative `E(G′_s)` (`Eis.memLp_gfun_all`, `Eis.hasDerivAt_gL`), for `R ≥ 0` and `Y > 0`;
- `ũ_s = −R(ĥ(s))g_s` equals `E_s − h_s` in `L²(ν)` for `Re s > 2` with `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0` (`Eis.uL_eq_eisLow`), and for `R = 2cosh r − 2`, `s ↦ ũ_s` and `s ↦ ⟨y, ũ_s⟩` are complex-differentiable wherever `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0` (`Eis.differentiableAt_uL`, `Eis.differentiableAt_inner_uL`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaGHolo.lean`, 746 lines, 42 theorems and 9 definitions; each of its 42 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **A quantitative `L²` bound** (`psC`, a definition; **`lintegral_puLe_top_mul_le`** and **`eLpNorm_pseis_le`**, with `psC_lt_top`, `norm_le_pow_of_vanish`, `lintegral_pseis_sq_le` and `memLp_pseis_of_vanish`).
- **`G_s` as one integral** (`gWt`, `gInt` and `gDer`, definitions; **`gProf_eq_gInt`**, with `norm_gWt_le`, `measurable_gWt`, `gWt_eq_zero`, `snd_mem_Icc_of_mem_hball`, `rpow_le_add_of_mem_Icc`, `abs_log_le_of_mem_Icc`, `integrableOn_hball_of_le`, `measurable_ballInt`, `measurable_gInt`, `measurable_gDer`, `integrableOn_gWt`, `ballInt_gWt_eq_zero`, `snd_mem_shell` and `norm_ballInt_gWt_le`).
- **Taylor's bound, uniform in `v`** (`shM` and `shL`, definitions; **`norm_cpow_taylor_le`** and **`gInt_taylor`**, with `shM_nonneg`, `shL_nonneg`, `norm_cpow_le_shM`, `abs_log_le_shL`, `gInt_eq_zero_of_lt`, `gDer_eq_zero_of_lt`, `norm_gInt_le` and `norm_gDer_le`).
- **`s ↦ g_s` is holomorphic** (`gL` and `gL'`, definitions; **`memLp_gfun_all`** and **`hasDerivAt_gL`**, with `memLp_pseis_gDer`, `shell_lt_of_lt_div`, `differentiable_gL` and `continuous_gL`).
- **The resolvent** (`uL`, a definition; **`uL_eq_eisLow`** and **`differentiableAt_uL`**, with `ballOp_toLp_eisLow_sub`, `cosh_sub_nonneg` and `differentiableAt_inner_uL`).

**The proof.**

- **The `L²` bound.** Round 423's `lintegral_puLe_top_mul_lt_top` is made quantitative: moving each coset `q` by `q⁻¹` and bounding `F` on the Siegel set gives `∫ρ_G F dμ ≤ Σ_q C(q⁻¹)·∫ρ dμ` over the finitely many cosets. A profile vanishing on `(0, a)` and bounded by `D` satisfies `|f(v)| ≤ D·a⁻³·v³`, so round 423's `norm_pseis_slAct_sub_le` with `τ = 3` bounds `|E(f)|` on the Siegel set at `g·∞` by `(|a_g| + 2a⁻³·cuspC(3))·D`.
- **`G_s` as one integral.** Round 418's `bavg_cpow` at `(0, v)` gives `ĥ(s)v^s = ∫_{B_R(0, v)} v′^s dμ`, so round 423's `G_s = B(1[v′ < Y]v′^s) − ĥ(s)·1[v < Y]v^s` is the integral of `(1[v′ < Y] − 1[v < Y])·v′^s` over the ball. On the ball `v/(R + 2) ≤ v′ ≤ (R + 2)v` (round 423), so the weight vanishes there off the shells, and for `v` in the shells `v′` lies in `[Y/(R + 2)², (R + 2)²Y]`.
- **Taylor's bound.** `x^{s+h} − x^s − h·log x·x^s = x^s(e^{h log x} − 1 − h log x)`, and Mathlib's `Complex.norm_exp_sub_one_sub_id_le` bounds the bracket by `|h log x|²` for `|h log x| ≤ 1`. Integrating against the weight over the ball, whose measure is `V_R`, gives `|G_{s+h}(v) − G_s(v) − h·G′_s(v)| ≤ V_R·M_s·(|h|L)²` for every `v > 0`, with `M_s` and `L` the bounds for `x^σ` and `|log x|` on the shells' heights.
- **Holomorphy.** `g_{s+h} − g_s − h·E(G′_s) = E(G_{s+h} − G_s − h·G′_s)` on upper half-space (round 423's `pseis_sub` and `pseis_const_mul`), so the `L²` bound gives `‖g_{s+h} − g_s − h·E(G′_s)‖₂ ≤ psC(a)^{1/2}·V_R·M_s·(|h|L)²`, which is `o(|h|)` (Mathlib's `hasDerivAt_iff_isLittleO`).
- **The resolvent.** Round 423's `ballOp_eisLow_sub` is an identity of elements of `L²(ν)` (`Lp.ext`). So `(ĥ(s) − K)(E_s − h_s) = −g_s`, and round 419's `resolvent_sub_apply` inverts it where `ĥ(s)` is in the resolvent set, which holds for `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0` (round 419's `mem_resolventSet_of_im_ne_zero`). The derivative of `s ↦ R(ĥ(s))` is round 419's `hasDerivAt_resolvent_of_im_ne_zero` composed with round 418's `differentiable_hhat`. Mathlib's `HasDerivAt.clm_apply` then differentiates `R(ĥ(s))g_s`.

**Against the plan.** Round 423's next step listed:

- "`G_s(v)` and its derivative in `s` bounded uniformly in `v`, for `s` in compact sets, by differentiating under round 418's ball integral";
- "the number of bottom rows whose heights at `w` lie in the shells, bounded on the Siegel set at every cusp, so that `s ↦ g_s` is continuous into `L²(ν)` and `s ↦ ⟨y, g_s⟩` is holomorphic for every `y` in `L²(ν)`";
- "`ũ_s = −R(ĥ(s))g_s` where `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0` (round 419's resolvent bound), equal to `E_s − h_s` for `Re s > 2` by this round's `ballOp_eisLow_sub`, with `s ↦ ⟨y, ũ_s⟩` holomorphic there".

The third landed as listed. The first two landed in a stronger form, by a different route. In place of a derivative bound and a count of rows, round 423's bound at the cusps is made quantitative: `‖E(f)‖₂` is at most a constant times the supremum of the profile. With Taylor's bound for `x^s`, uniform in `v`, this makes `s ↦ g_s` complex-differentiable into `L²(ν)` itself, not only weakly, and at every `s`. No differentiation under the integral is needed: the derivative profile `G′_s` is written down, and the remainder is bounded directly.

**The next step.** S5f-10e, the residue θ, with `R = 2cosh r − 2` for `r > 0`. The plan:

Unfolding over `Γ_∞\Γ_1(3)` (round 386's `lintegral_unfold_cosets` and `rhoInf`, in a complex form) and round 389's constant term give `φ(s)` times `∫ψ̄(v)v^{2−s} dv/v³` and the area of a period parallelogram.
- The identity theorem, on the convex set `{Re s > 1, 0 < Im s < π/r}` (round 418's `im_hhat_pos`), carries the identity to `s = 4/3 + iε`. There `(s − 4/3)φ(s)` tends to round 417's residue, which is nonzero, so `⟨E(ψ), θ⟩ ≠ 0` and θ ≠ 0. *(Round 425: the first two items landed, with the lemma localised to small `ε`, `Eis.tendsto_uL_thetaL` and `Eis.ballOp_thetaL`, and an automorphic representative of θ, `Eis.thetaL_ae_eq_thetaF`; the pairing and θ ≠ 0 are round 425's next step. ## Round 425: S5f-10e, part 1 — the residue θ (`src/KubotaResidue.lean`)

**What it is.** The twelfth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the first part of S5f-10e. Round 424 set `ũ_s = −R(ĥ(s))g_s`, equal to `E_s − h_s` for `Re s > 2` and complex-differentiable wherever `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0`. This round takes its residue at `s = 4/3`, with `R = 2cosh r − 2` for `r > 0`, `Y > 0`, and `ν = ρ_G dμ` as in round 423:

- `ĥ′(σ)` is real for real `σ`, and `ĥ′(σ) ≥ K(r, σ) > 0` for `σ > 1` (`Eis.deriv_hhat_im`, `Eis.imK_le_deriv_hhat`);
- `θ = −ĥ′(4/3)⁻¹·P g_{4/3}`, with `P` the orthogonal projection onto the kernel of `K − ĥ(4/3)`, is the limit in `L²(ν)` of `(s − 4/3)·ũ_s` along `s = 4/3 + iε` as `ε → 0⁺` (`Eis.tendsto_uL_thetaL`);
- `Kθ = ĥ(4/3)·θ` (`Eis.ballOp_thetaL`);
- every kernel integral `∫k(·, q)f(q) dν(q)` is automorphic with the character (`Eis.isAut_kfun`), so θ is almost everywhere the automorphic function `θ̃ = ĥ(4/3)⁻¹·∫k(·, q)θ(q) dν(q)` (`Eis.isAut_thetaF`, `Eis.thetaL_ae_eq_thetaF`).

This round does not prove θ ≠ 0. That is the next step.

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaResidue.lean`, 286 lines, 10 theorems and 2 definitions; each of its 10 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The resolvent along a curve, near `0` only** (**`tendsto_resolvent_curve_ev`**).
- **`ĥ` near `4/3`** (**`deriv_hhat_im`** and **`imK_le_deriv_hhat`**, with `hasDerivAt_hhat_vert`).
- **The residue** (`thetaL`, a definition; **`tendsto_uL_thetaL`** and **`ballOp_thetaL`**).
- **An automorphic representative** (`thetaF`, a definition; **`isAut_kfun`**, **`isAut_thetaF`** and **`thetaL_ae_eq_thetaF`**, with `bker_slAct`).

**The proof.**

- **Near `0` only.** Round 419's `tendsto_resolvent_curve` asks for `c·ε ≤ Im ℓ(ε)` at every `ε > 0`. Replacing `ℓ(ε)` by `l + iεc` where the bound fails changes `ℓ` only away from `0⁺`, where neither the hypothesis on `ℓ` nor the conclusion looks.
- **`ĥ′` real.** On the real axis `ĥ` is real (round 418's `hhat_real_pos`). So `y ↦ ĥ(y)` and `y ↦ Re ĥ(y)` agree on `ℝ`, and their derivatives at `σ`, `ĥ′(σ)` and its real part (Mathlib's `HasDerivAt.real_of_complex`), agree.
- **`ĥ′` positive.** `ε ↦ ĥ(σ + iε)` has derivative `iĥ′(σ)` at `0`. Taking imaginary parts of its slopes, `Im ĥ(σ + iε)/ε → Re ĥ′(σ)`, and round 418's `im_hhat_ge` bounds the quotient below by `K(r, σ)` for `0 < ε ≤ π/(2r)`; round 418's `imK_pos` makes `K(r, 4/3) > 0`.
- **θ.** With `l = ĥ(4/3)`, `d = ĥ′(4/3)` and `c = K(r, 4/3)`, the slope gives `(ĥ(4/3 + iε) − (l + iεd))/ε → 0`, round 418's `im_hhat_ge` gives `c·ε ≤ Im ĥ(4/3 + iε)` near `0⁺`, and round 424's `continuous_gL` gives `g_{4/3+iε} → g_{4/3}`. The localized `tendsto_resolvent_curve` then gives `iε·R(ĥ(4/3 + iε))g_{4/3+iε} → d⁻¹·P g_{4/3}`, and `ũ_s = −R(ĥ(s))g_s`.
- **The eigenvalue.** `P g_{4/3}` lies in the kernel of `K − ĥ(4/3)` (Mathlib's `Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem`).
- **Automorphy.** `k(g·p, q) = Σ_γ χ(γ)·1_{B_R(g·p)}(γq)`. Reindexing `γ = gγ′` and moving the ball by `g⁻¹` (round 418's `mem_hball_actP`) gives `χ(g)·k(p, q)`, so the kernel integral is automorphic in `p`. Since `ĥ(4/3) > 0` (round 418's `hhat_real_pos`), `θ = ĥ(4/3)⁻¹·Kθ`, and round 422's `ballOp_ae_eq_kfun` writes `Kθ` as the kernel integral almost everywhere.

**Against the plan.** Round 424's next step listed:

- "`ĥ(σ)` is real for real `σ` (round 418's `hhat_real_pos`), so `ĥ′(4/3)` is real. It is positive, since `ĥ(σ) = ∫_{−r}^{r} 2π(cosh r − cosh u)e^{(σ−1)u} du` (round 418's `hhat_eq_interval`) is increasing for `σ > 1`.";
- "Round 419's `tendsto_resolvent_curve`, with this round's `continuous_gL`, gives θ as the limit of `iε·ũ_{4/3+iε}`, namely `−ĥ′(4/3)⁻¹·P g_{4/3}` with `P` the projection onto the kernel of `K − ĥ(4/3)`. That lemma asks for `c·ε ≤ Im ĥ(4/3 + iε)` at every `ε > 0`, while round 418's `im_hhat_ge` gives it for `ε·r ≤ π/2`. So the curve is to be capped, or the lemma localised to small `ε`.";

and then the pairing with pseudo-Eisenstein series and the identity theorem. The first two landed: the lemma is localised (`tendsto_resolvent_curve_ev`). The positivity of `ĥ′(4/3)` comes from the lower bound for `Im ĥ`, not from monotonicity on the real axis, from which a positive derivative would not follow. The automorphic representative was not planned; it is added because θ is an element of `L²(ν)`, a space of functions on all of upper half-space, and the later steps need θ as an automorphic function. The pairing and θ ≠ 0 remain.

**The next step.** S5f-10e, part 2: θ ≠ 0. The plan, for a measurable bounded profile `ψ` supported in `[α, β]` with `α > max(Y, 1/Y)`, and `E(ψ)` its pseudo-Eisenstein series, in `L²(ν)` by round 424's `memLp_pseis_of_vanish`:

The bottom rows of `Γ_1(3)` are to be matched with the cosets of `Γ_∞ ∩ Γ_1(3)`, the translations by `3ℤ[ω]` (`(c/d)₃ = conj κ(γ)` by round 387's `kub_eq_conj_cub`), and the folding of round 386's `tsum_fold` is to be redone with complex integrands. *(Round 426: landed, `Eis.integral_conj_pseis_mul` and `Eis.inner_toLp_pseis`, with the absolute convergence of the right side as the hypothesis, and `Γ_1(3)` matched with `ℤ[ω] × (bottom rows)` in place of the cosets. ## Round 426: S5f-10e, part 2 — unfolding pseudo-Eisenstein series (`src/KubotaUnfoldEis.lean`)

**What it is.** The thirteenth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the second part of S5f-10e. Round 425's next step planned the pairing of `ũ_s` with a pseudo-Eisenstein series `E(ψ)`, beginning with an unfolding in complex form. This round proves the unfolding, with `ν = ρ_G dμ` as in round 423 and `3P` round 389's period parallelogram of `3ℤ[ω]`:

- for elements `g_i` of `SL_2(ℤ[ω])` with `Σ_i ρ(g_i⁻¹·q) = ρ′(q)` on upper half-space, `∫ρ(p)·Σ_i F(g_i·p) dμ = ∫ρ′F dμ` for `F` measurable with values in `[0, ∞]` (`Eis.lintegral_unfold_family`), and `∫Σ_i Ψ(g_i·p) dν_ρ(p) = ∫Ψ dν_{ρ′}` for `Ψ` measurable and complex, when `ρ` and `ρ′` are finite on upper half-space and `∫ρ′·|Ψ| dμ < ∞` (`Eis.integral_unfold_family`);
- with one element `γ_{(c, d)}` of `Γ_1(3)` fixed for each bottom row `(c, d)`, `(t, (c, d)) ↦ T_{3t}·γ_{(c, d)}` is a bijection from `ℤ[ω] × (bottom rows)` onto `Γ_1(3)` (`Eis.decGam3`, through `Eis.eq_slT_of_Gam3`);
- `ρ_H(p) = Σ_{(c, d)} ρ_G(γ_{(c, d)}⁻¹·p)` and `ρ_3(z, v) = 1_{3P}(z)` both sum to `1` over the translations by `3ℤ[ω]` (`Eis.tsum_rhoH`, `Eis.tsum_rhoT3`), and `∫Φ dν_{ρ_H} = ∫Φ dν_{ρ_3}` for `Φ` measurable and periodic under `3ℤ[ω]` with `∫ρ_3·|Φ| dμ < ∞` (`Eis.integral_rhoH_eq`);
- for `ψ` and `u` measurable, `u` automorphic with Kubota's character and `∫_{3P×(0,∞)} |ψ(v)·u(z, v)| dz dv/v³ < ∞`, `∫conj E(ψ)·u dν = ∫_{3P×(0,∞)} conj ψ(v)·u(z, v) dz dv/v³` (`Eis.integral_conj_pseis_mul`); when `E(ψ)` and `u` are in `L²(ν)`, the left side is `⟨E(ψ), u⟩` (`Eis.inner_toLp_pseis`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaUnfoldEis.lean`, 456 lines, 25 theorems, 4 definitions and 1 abbreviation; each of its 25 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **Unfolding over a family** (**`lintegral_unfold_family`** and **`integral_unfold_family`**).
- **`Γ_1(3)` as translations times bottom rows** (`BRowT`, an abbreviation, and `gamRow` and `decGam3`, definitions; **`eq_slT_of_Gam3`**, with `gamRow_mem`, `gamRow_10`, `gamRow_11`, `slT_mul_10`, `slT_mul_11`, `slT_mul_slT`, `slT_inv` and `decGam3_apply`).
- **Partitions of unity for the translations** (`rhoH` and `rhoT3`, definitions; **`tsum_rhoH`**, **`lintegral_rhoH_eq`** and **`integral_rhoH_eq`**, with `measurable_rhoH`, `measurable_rhoT3`, `rhoT3_le_one`, `kub_slT`, `rhoH_le_one` and `tsum_rhoT3`).
- **The pairing** (**`integral_conj_pseis_mul`** and **`inner_toLp_pseis`**, with `muR_rhoT3`, `conj_psTerm_mul` and `conj_pseis_mul`).

**The proof.**

- **Unfolding over a family.** Each term `∫ρ(p)F(g_i·p) dμ` is moved by `g_i⁻¹` (round 386's `lintegral_slAct`) to `∫ρ(g_i⁻¹·q)F(q) dμ`, and Mathlib's `lintegral_tsum` exchanges the sums with the integrals. In complex form, Mathlib's `integral_tsum` makes the two exchanges, each justified by the statement in `[0, ∞]` applied to `|Ψ|`. Each term is moved by round 383's `integral_actP`. The weights `ρ(g_i⁻¹·q)` are finite, since they sum to `ρ′(q) < ∞`, so their real parts sum to `ρ′(q)`. Round 422's `kfun_eq_bavg` makes the same exchanges.
- **Translations times bottom rows.** An element of `Γ_1(3)` with bottom row `(0, 1)` has upper-left entry `1` by its determinant, and its upper-right entry is divisible by `3` (round 382's `modThree_iff`), so it is `T_{3t}`. For `γ` in `Γ_1(3)` with bottom row `(c, d)`, `γ·γ_{(c, d)}⁻¹` has bottom row `(0, 1)` (round 387's `rowMul_bottom`), so `γ = T_{3t}·γ_{(c, d)}`. Multiplying by `T_{3t}` on the left does not change the bottom row, so `(t, (c, d))` is unique.
- **`ρ_H`.** `Σ_t ρ_H(T_{3t}·p)` is the sum over `(t, (c, d))` of `ρ_G((T_{−3t}·γ_{(c, d)})⁻¹·p)`. Through `t ↦ −t` and the bijection, it is the sum of `ρ_G(γ⁻¹·p)` over `Γ_1(3)`, which is `1` (round 386's `IsPU.tsum_inv`). For `ρ_3` the sum is round 389's `tsum_fundP3`. Unfolding `ρ_H·Φ` over the translations with the weights `ρ_3` and `1` gives `∫ρ_3(p)·Σ_t ρ_H(T_{3t}·p)Φ(T_{3t}·p) dμ = ∫ρ_H·Φ dμ`, and for `Φ` periodic the inner sum is `Φ(p)`.
- **The pairing.** The term of `E(ψ)` at `(c, d)` is `(c/d)₃·ψ(v(γp))` with `γ = γ_{(c, d)}` (round 423's `psTerm_eq_of_row`). Since `u(γp) = κ(γ)u(p)` and `κ(γ) = conj (c/d)₃` (round 387's `kub_eq_conj_cub`), its conjugate times `u(p)` is `conj ψ(v(γp))·u(γp)`. Unfolding over the family `γ_{(c, d)}` with the weights `ρ_G` and `ρ_H` gives `∫Φ dν_{ρ_H}` with `Φ(z, v) = conj ψ(v)·u(z, v)`, periodic under `3ℤ[ω]` since `κ(T_{3t}) = 1`. Changing the partition to `ρ_3` gives the integral over `3P × (0, ∞)`, since `ν_{ρ_3}` is `dz dv/v³` restricted there (`muR_rhoT3`). Both finiteness hypotheses follow from `∫ρ_3·|Φ| dμ < ∞` through `lintegral_rhoH_eq`.

**Against the plan.** Round 425's next step listed, as its first item:

- "For `u` automorphic in `L²(ν)`, `⟨E(ψ), u⟩ = ∫_{3P×(0,∞)} conj ψ(v)·u(z, v) dz dv/v³`.";
- "The bottom rows of `Γ_1(3)` are to be matched with the cosets of `Γ_∞ ∩ Γ_1(3)`, the translations by `3ℤ[ω]` (`(c/d)₃ = conj κ(γ)` by round 387's `kub_eq_conj_cub`), and the folding of round 386's `tsum_fold` is to be redone with complex integrands."

The identity landed, with two differences. Its hypothesis is the absolute convergence of the right side, which is what the exchange of the sum over the bottom rows with the integral uses. This round does not derive that convergence from `u ∈ L²(ν)`, and the identity does not need `u ∈ L²(ν)`. The bottom rows are not matched with cosets. `Γ_1(3)` is put in bijection with `ℤ[ω] × (bottom rows)` through one fixed element for each bottom row. The folding is a general unfolding over a family of elements of `SL_2(ℤ[ω])`, applied over the fixed elements and over the translations. Round 386's `tsum_fold` is not used.

**The next step.** S5f-10e, part 3: the constant term and θ ≠ 0, for `R = 2cosh r − 2` with `r > 0`, `Y > 0`, and a profile `ψ` that is measurable and bounded, vanishing outside `[α, β]` with `α > max(Y, 1/Y)`:

Round 388's `norm_eis1_slAct_sub_le` then bounds `E_s − h_s` on `3P × [α, β]`, which gives the absolute convergence this round's `inner_toLp_pseis` asks for. Fubini and round 389's `constTerm_eis1` give `⟨E(ψ), ũ_s⟩ = (9√3/2)·φ(s)·∫conj ψ(v)v^{−1−s} dv` for `Re s > 2` with `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0` (round 424's `uL_eq_eisLow`).
- **The identity theorem** on the convex open set `{Re s > 1, 0 < Im s < π/r}` is unchanged from round 425's plan: both sides are holomorphic there (round 424's `differentiableAt_inner_uL` with round 418's `im_hhat_pos`; round 417's `differentiableAt_phiC` with round 416's `eisPhi_eq_phiC`), and they agree where `Re s > 2`. At `s = 4/3 + iε`, multiplying by `iε` and letting `ε → 0⁺` (round 425's `tendsto_uL_thetaL`, round 417's `tendsto_phiC_residue`) gives `⟨E(ψ), θ⟩ = (9√3/2)·Res φ·∫conj ψ(v)v^{−7/3} dv`. For `ψ = 1_{[α, β]}` with `α < β` this is nonzero (round 417's `phiRes_ne_zero`), so θ ≠ 0. *(Round 427: both landed, `Eis.inner_pseis_uL`, `Eis.inner_pseis_thetaL` and `Eis.thetaL_ne_zero`, with the heights `v ≥ Y`, `Yv > 1`, round 388's `norm_eis1_sub_le` for the bound, and `ψ = 1_{[α, α + 1]}`, `α = Y + 1/Y`. ## Round 427: S5f-10e, part 3 — the pairing with pseudo-Eisenstein series, and θ ≠ 0 (`src/KubotaThetaPair.lean`)

**What it is.** The fourteenth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the last part of S5f-10e. Round 426's next step planned the constant term of `E_s − h_s` high in the cusp, the identity theorem, and θ ≠ 0. This round proves all three, for `R = 2cosh r − 2` with `r > 0`, `Y > 0`, `ν = ρ_G dμ` as in round 423, and a profile `ψ` that is measurable and bounded, vanishing outside `[α, β]` with `α ≥ Y` and `Yα > 1`:

- `M_ψ` is entire (`Eis.differentiable_mellinPsi`), and `⟨E(ψ), θ⟩ = (9√3/2)·Res φ·M_ψ(4/3)`, with `Res φ = phiG(4/3)/3`, round 417's residue (`Eis.inner_pseis_thetaL`);
- **θ ≠ 0** (`Eis.thetaL_ne_zero`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaThetaPair.lean`, 576 lines, 19 theorems and 2 definitions; each of its 19 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **High in the cusp** (**`eisHigh_eq`**, **`norm_eisLow_le`** and **`integral_fundP3_eisLow`**, with `height_le_inv`, `eisLow_eq_sub` and `one_lt_of_Y_le`).
- **The pairing for `Re s > 2`** (**`integral_conj_eisLow`** and **`inner_pseis_uL`**, with `cpow_neg_one_sub`, `uhsMeasure_fundP3_Icc_lt_top`, `lintegral_rhoT3_eisLow_ne_top` and `memLp_pseis_Icc`).

- **The identity theorem and the limit** (`domU`, a definition; **`inner_pseis_thetaL`**, with `isOpen_domU` and `convex_domU`).
- **θ ≠ 0** (**`thetaL_ne_zero`**, with `mellinPsi_indicator_ne_zero`).

**The proof.**

- **High in the cusp.** At `(z, v)` the row `(0, 1)` has height `v`. The only bottom row with `c = 0` is `(0, 1)` (round 387's `bRow_zero_iff`). A bottom row with `c ≠ 0` has height `v/(|cz + d|² + |c|²v²) ≤ 1/v`, since `|c| ≥ 1` (round 361's `one_le_norm_σO`). So for `v ≥ Y` with `Yv > 1` the series `h_s` has the single term `v^s`, and `E_s − h_s = E_s − v^s` (round 423's `eis1_eq_eisLow_add_eisHigh`). Round 388's `norm_eis1_sub_le` bounds it, since then `v > 1`. On `3P` it is integrable, and round 389's `constTerm_eis1`, with `|3P| = 9√3/2` (round 389's `volume_fundP3`), gives its integral.
- **The pairing for `Re s > 2`.** The integrand `conj ψ(v)·(E_s − h_s)` vanishes outside `3P × [α, β]` and is bounded there by `M·cuspC(σ)`, since `v ≥ α > 1`. That set has finite measure, so round 426's `inner_toLp_pseis` applies. Its right side is moved to Lebesgue measure on `ℂ × ℝ` with the density `v^{−3}`, and Fubini (Mathlib's `integral_prod_symm`) integrates over `z` first. With `v^{−3}·v^{2−s} = v^{−1−s}` this gives `(9√3/2)·φ(s)·M_ψ(s)`. Round 424's `uL_eq_eisLow` identifies `ũ_s` with `E_s − h_s` when `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0`.
- **`M_ψ` entire.** `M_ψ(s)` is the Mellin transform of `conj ψ` at `−s`. Since `conj ψ` is integrable and vanishes near `0` and near `∞`, Mathlib's `mellin_differentiableAt_of_isBigO_rpow` applies at every point.
- **The identity theorem.** On the convex open set `U = {Re s > 1, 0 < Im s < π/r}`, `Im ĥ(s) > 0` (round 418's `im_hhat_pos`). So `s ↦ ⟨E(ψ), ũ_s⟩` is holomorphic there (round 424's `differentiableAt_inner_uL`). So is `(9√3/2)·φ(s)·M_ψ(s)`, since `s ≠ 4/3` on `U` (round 417's `differentiableAt_phiC`). The two agree on the open set `U ∩ {Re s > 2}` (round 416's `eisPhi_eq_phiC`), hence on `U` (Mathlib's `AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq`).
- **The limit.** `4/3 + iε` lies in `U` for `0 < ε < π/r`. There `iε⟨E(ψ), ũ_s⟩ = ⟨E(ψ), iε·ũ_s⟩ → ⟨E(ψ), θ⟩` (round 425's `tendsto_uL_thetaL`), while `iε·φ(s) = (s − 4/3)φ(s) → Res φ` (round 417's `tendsto_phiC_residue`, since `4/3 + iε ≠ 4/3` for `ε > 0`) and `M_ψ(s) → M_ψ(4/3)`. The two limits agree.
- **θ ≠ 0.** Take `α = Y + 1/Y`, so that `α ≥ Y` and `Yα = Y² + 1 > 1`, and `ψ = 1_{[α, α + 1]}`. Then `M_ψ(4/3) = ∫_α^{α+1} v^{−7/3} dv > 0` (Mathlib's `intervalIntegral_pos_of_pos_on`). Neither `9√3/2` nor `Res φ` is zero (round 417's `phiRes_ne_zero`), so `⟨E(ψ), θ⟩ ≠ 0`.

- "Round 388's `norm_eis1_slAct_sub_le` then bounds `E_s − h_s` on `3P × [α, β]`, which gives the absolute convergence this round's `inner_toLp_pseis` asks for.";
- "Fubini and round 389's `constTerm_eis1` give `⟨E(ψ), ũ_s⟩ = (9√3/2)·φ(s)·∫conj ψ(v)v^{−1−s} dv` for `Re s > 2` with `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0` (round 424's `uL_eq_eisLow`).";
- "For `ψ = 1_{[α, β]}` with `α < β` this is nonzero (round 417's `phiRes_ne_zero`), so θ ≠ 0."

- for `m = δ₃x ≠ 0`, `Re s > 2` and `v > 0`, `∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)E(z, v; s) dz = v^s·∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9) dz + (2π/Γ(s))(2π|m|/9)^{s−1}·v·K_{s−1}(4π|m|v/9)·D_m(s)`, with `D_m(s) = Σ_c S_m(c)N(c)^{−s}` and `S_m(c) = Σ_{d mod 3c} (c/d)₃·ĕ((m/9)(d/c))` (`Eis.integral_ebr_eis1_fundP3`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaEisFourier.lean`, 491 lines, 15 theorems and 2 definitions; each of its 15 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The planar Fourier transform** (`ftInt`, a definition; **`integral_ebr_inv_cpow`**, with `measurable_ebr`, `ebr_neg_mul_exp`, `integral_ebr_gauss`, `cpow_neg_eq_integral`, `ftInt_eq`, `measurable_ftInt`, `norm_ftInt` and `integrable_ftInt`).
- **`K_ν` entire in `ν`** (**`differentiable_besselK`**).
- **One term** (**`integral_ebr_height_cpow`**).
- **The Fourier coefficient** (`cuspSm`, a definition; **`hasSum_integral_ebr_eisTerm_c`** and **`integral_ebr_eis1_fundP3`**, with `ebr_period` and `ebr_neg_mul_add_period`).

**The proof.**

- **The planar Fourier transform.** For `r > 0` and `Re s > 0`, `r^{−s} = Γ(s)⁻¹∫_0^∞ t^{s−1}e^{−rt} dt` (Mathlib's `Complex.integral_cpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_Ioi`), applied to `r = 1 + |z|²`. The double integral converges absolutely for `Re s > 1`: the inner integral of the absolute value over `z` is `πt^{σ−2}e^{−t}` (Mathlib's `integral_rexp_neg_mul_sq_norm`), integrable on `(0, ∞)` (Mathlib's `Real.GammaIntegral_convergent`). After Fubini, the integral over `z` is Mathlib's Gaussian `integral_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm_add`, since `ĕ(−ξz) = e^{−2πi⟨2ξ̄, z⟩}`, and gives `(π/t)e^{−4π²|ξ|²/t}`. The remaining integral `π∫_0^∞ t^{s−2}e^{−t−a²/t} dt`, with `a = 2π|ξ|`, is the Mellin transform of round 361's kernel `e^{−a(u+1/u)}` at `s − 1`, rescaled by `a` (Mathlib's `mellin_comp_mul_left`), which is `2a^{s−1}K_{s−1}(2a)` by round 361's definition of `besselK`.
- **`K_ν` entire.** `K_ν(x)` is half a Mellin transform in `ν`. Its kernel decays like `e^{−xt/2}` at `∞` and faster than every power at `0`, the bounds of round 361's `mellinConvergent_bkK`, so Mathlib's `mellin_differentiableAt_of_isBigO_rpow_exp` applies at every `ν`.
- **One term.** Round 389's `height_cpow_eq` writes the term as `(v/|c|²)^s(|z + d/c|² + v²)^{−s}`. The shift `z ↦ z − d/c` contributes `ĕ(ξd/c)`. The scaling `z ↦ vz` (Mathlib's `integral_comp_smul_of_nonneg`, with Jacobian `v²`) gives `v^{2−2s}` times the planar transform at `ξv`. The powers of `v` combine to `v`.
- **The Fourier coefficient.** `ĕ(σ(δ₃x)σ(3u)/9) = 1` is round 363's `ebr_shift` with `q = 1` and round 304's `ψc_one`. So the character is periodic under `3ℤ[ω]`, and round 389's proof of `hasSum_integral_eisTerm_c` goes through with it: the `d` in a class modulo `3c` are `d_r + 3cu`, the term at `d_r + 3cu` is the term at `d_r` moved by `3σ(u)` (round 389's `eisTerm_add`), and the translates of `3P` tile `ℂ` (round 389's `integral_tile3`). Summing over the classes gives `S_m(c)`. The double sum over `(c, d)` is exchanged with the integral as in round 389's `integral_eis1_fundP3`, the character having modulus `1`. The row `(0, 1)` gives `v^s·∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9) dz`, and the rows `c ≠ 0` give `D_m(s)`.

**Against the plan.** Round 427's next step listed, as its second item:

Its contribution to a pairing with a profile `ψ` of compact support in `(0, ∞)` is that integral times `∫conj ψ(v)v^{s−3} dv`, which is to be shown entire in `s`, so that the residue does not see it. The plan's first item, the series `P_m(ψ)` and its unfolding, was not done; it is the next step. The holomorphy of `K_ν` in `ν` was not listed; the identity theorem with `ψ` will need it.

## Round 429: S5f-10f, part 2 — twisted pseudo-Eisenstein series (`src/KubotaPoincare.lean`)

**What it is.** The sixteenth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the second part of S5f-10f. Round 428's next step planned the series `P_m(ψ)`, its automorphy, its square-integrability and its unfolding. This round proves them, with `γ_{(c, d)}` round 426's element of `Γ_1(3)` with bottom row `(c, d)`, `ν = ρ_G dμ` as in round 423, and frequencies `m = δ₃x`:

- `P_m(ψ)(w) = Σ_{(c, d)} (c/d)₃·ψ(v(γw))·ĕ(m·z(γw)/9)` with `γ = γ_{(c, d)}` satisfies `P_m(ψ)(g·w) = κ(g)·P_m(ψ)(w)` for `g ∈ Γ_1(3)` (`Eis.isAut_pmSer`);
- it is in `L²(ν)` for `ψ` measurable and bounded with `|ψ(v)| ≤ C·v^τ`, `C ≥ 0`, `τ > 2` (`Eis.memLp_pmSer`), in particular for `ψ` bounded and vanishing outside `[α, β]` with `α > 0` (`Eis.memLp_pmSer_Icc`);
- for `ψ` and `u` measurable, `u` automorphic with Kubota's character and `∫_{3P×(0,∞)} |ψ(v)u(z, v)| dz dv/v³ < ∞`, `∫conj P_m(ψ)·u dν = ∫_{3P×(0,∞)} conj(ψ(v)·ĕ(mz/9))·u(z, v) dz dv/v³` (`Eis.integral_conj_pmSer_mul`); in `L²(ν)` the left side is `⟨P_m(ψ), u⟩` (`Eis.inner_toLp_pmSer`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaPoincare.lean`, 351 lines, 16 theorems and 5 definitions; each of its 16 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The series** (`pmTerm` and `pmSer`, definitions).
- **Automorphy** (`rowG` and `rowGEquiv`, definitions; **`isAut_pmSer`**, with `gamRow_mul_eq`, `kub_mul_conj_kub`, `pmTerm_slAct`, `measurable_pmTerm`, `measurable_pmSer` and `norm_pmTerm`).
- **Square-integrability** (`rowsZ`, a definition; **`tsum_enorm_psTerm_slAct_le`**, **`memLp_pmSer`** and **`memLp_pmSer_Icc`**, with `rowsZ_finite` and `tsum_enorm_pmTerm_eq`).
- **Unfolding** (**`integral_conj_pmSer_mul`** and **`inner_toLp_pmSer`**, with `conj_pmTerm_mul` and `conj_pmSer_mul`).

**The proof.**

- **Automorphy.** For `g ∈ Γ_1(3)`, `γ_{(c, d)}·g·γ_{(c, d)g}⁻¹` is in `Γ_1(3)` with bottom row `(0, 1)` (round 387's `rowMul_bottom`), so it is a translation `T_{3t}` (round 426's `eq_slT_of_Gam3`). The translation leaves the height and `ĕ(m·z/9)` unchanged (round 428's `ebr_period`). Round 387's `cub_rowMul` gives `((c, d)g)₃ = (c/d)₃·conj κ(g)`, and `|κ(g)| = 1` (round 387's `norm_kub`), so the term of `(c, d)` at `g·w` is `κ(g)` times the term of `(c, d)g` at `w`. The bottom rows are permuted by `(c, d) ↦ (c, d)g` (round 387's `bRow_rowMul_iff`).
- **The majorant at the cusps.** A term of `P_m(ψ)` has the absolute value of the corresponding term of `E(ψ)` (round 370's `norm_σO_cub`, and `|ĕ| = 1`). At `g·p` with `v(p) ≥ 1/2`, the bottom rows that `g` sends to `(0, *)` are sent to `(0, u)` with `u` a unit (round 388's `isUnit_rowMul_snd`), so they form a finite set, and each of their terms has height `v(p)` (round 423's `height_slAct_of_fst`). The other terms are at most `C` times the heights of the rows `(c, d)g` with `c ≠ 0` to the power `τ` (round 387's `height_rowMul`), whose sum is at most `cuspC(τ)·v^{2−τ}` (round 388's `tsum_height_ne_le`). So `|P_m(ψ)(g·p)| ≤ #(rowsZ g)·D + C·cuspC(τ)·2^{τ−2}` on round 385's Siegel set, and round 423's `lintegral_puLe_top_mul_lt_top` and `memLp_two_of_lintegral` give `L²(ν)`. A profile vanishing outside `[α, β]` satisfies the power bound with `τ = 3` (round 424's `norm_le_pow_of_vanish`).
- **Unfolding.** Since `u(γp) = κ(γ)u(p)` and `κ(γ) = conj (c/d)₃` (round 387's `kub_eq_conj_cub`), `conj P_m(ψ)·u = Σ_{(c, d)} Φ(γ_{(c, d)}p)` with `Φ(z, v) = conj(ψ(v)ĕ(mz/9))·u(z, v)`. `Φ` is periodic under `3ℤ[ω]`, by `ebr_period` and round 426's `kub_slT`. Round 426's `integral_unfold_family` over the family `γ_{(c, d)}` and its `integral_rhoH_eq` then give the integral over `3P × (0, ∞)`, as in round 426's `integral_conj_pseis_mul`.

**Against the plan.** Round 428's next step listed, as its first item:

- "the series `P_m(ψ)(w) = Σ_{(c, d)} (c/d)₃·ψ(v(γw))·ĕ(m·z(γw)/9)` over the bottom rows, with `γ = γ_{(c, d)}` as in round 426, automorphic with Kubota's character (through round 426's `decGam3` and this round's `ebr_period`), in `L²(ν)` for `ψ` bounded with compact support in `(0, ∞)`, and unfolding as in round 426 to `∫_{3P×(0,∞)} conj(ψ(v)ĕ(mz/9))·u dz dv/v³`;"

It landed. The automorphy goes through `eq_slT_of_Gam3`, which `decGam3` also uses, not through `decGam3` itself. `L²(ν)` is proved under the power bound with `τ > 2`, which a bounded profile vanishing below `α > 0` satisfies; a profile vanishing above `β` is not needed for it. The second item, the pairing with `ũ_s`, remains.

**The next step.** S5f-10f, part 3: the pairing of `P_m(ψ)` with `ũ_s` for `Re s > 2`, for `ψ` bounded and vanishing outside `[α, β]`, `α > 0`. The plan:

- a bound for the heights `v/Q_w(c, d)` uniform for `w` in `3P × [α, β]`, through round 387's `height_le_lattice`, so that `E_s` and `h_s` are bounded there and Fubini applies; *(Round 430: landed, `Eis.tsum_height_rpow_le_unif`, `Eis.norm_pseis_le_hBd` and `Eis.integral_fundP3_conj_mul`. See round 430.)*
- on `3P × [α, β]` every height is at most `H₀ = max(β, 1/α)`, so there `h_s = E(f_s)` with `f_s = 1[Y ≤ v ≤ H₀]v^s`; `s ↦ E(f_s)` is complex-differentiable into `L²(ν)` by round 424's method, so `s ↦ ⟨P_m(ψ), E(f_s)⟩` is entire; *(Round 430: landed with `H = Y + β + 1/α` in place of `H₀`, `Eis.eisHigh_eq_band`, `Eis.hasDerivAt_bandL` and `Eis.differentiable_inner_bandL`. See round 430.)*
- by round 428's coefficient, `⟨P_m(ψ), ũ_s⟩ = (2π/Γ(s))(2π|m|/9)^{s−1}·D_m(s)·J_ψ(s) + (entire in s)` for `Re s > 2` with `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0`, where `J_ψ(s) = ∫conj ψ(v)v^{−2}K_{s−1}(4π|m|v/9) dv`. *(Round 430: landed, `Eis.inner_pmSer_uL_bessel`, with `I_m·M_ψ(2 − s) − ⟨P_m(ψ), E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)⟩` as the entire part. See round 430.)*

Then part 4: `J_ψ` entire, and the identity theorem and the limit, giving `⟨P_m(ψ), θ⟩ = ρ(m)·J_ψ(4/3)` with `ρ(m)` independent of `ψ`.

## Round 430: S5f-10f, part 3 — the pairing of `P_m(ψ)` with `ũ_s` (`src/KubotaPmPair.lean`)

**What it is.** The seventeenth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the third part of S5f-10f. Round 429's next step planned the pairing of `P_m(ψ)` with `ũ_s` for `Re s > 2`, for `ψ` bounded and vanishing outside `[α, β]`, `α > 0`. This round proves it, with `m = δ₃x`, `ν = ρ_G dμ` as in round 423, `ψ` measurable with `|ψ| ≤ M`, vanishing outside `[α, β]` with `0 < α ≤ β`, and `H = Y + β + 1/α`:

- for `0 < Y ≤ H`, `s ↦ E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)` is complex-differentiable into `L²(ν)` at every `s` (`Eis.hasDerivAt_bandL`), so its pairings with a fixed vector are entire (`Eis.differentiable_inner_bandL`);
- for `|z| ≤ 6`, `0 < α ≤ v ≤ β` and `σ > 2`, the sum of `(v/Q_w(c, d))^σ` over the bottom rows is at most a constant `hBd(σ, α, β)` (`Eis.tsum_height_rpow_le_unif`), so on `3P × [α, β]` the pseudo-Eisenstein series of a profile with `|f(v)| ≤ v^σ` is bounded by it (`Eis.norm_pseis_le_hBd`), and Fubini applies there (`Eis.integral_fundP3_conj_mul`);
- on `3P × [α, β]`, `h_s = E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)` (`Eis.eisHigh_eq_band`), and for `Re s > 2` with `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0`, `⟨P_m(ψ), ũ_s⟩ = ∫_0^∞ v^{−3}·conj ψ(v)·∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)E(z, v; s) dz dv − ⟨P_m(ψ), E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)⟩` (`Eis.inner_pmSer_uL`);
- for `x ≠ 0`, `⟨P_m(ψ), ũ_s⟩ = (2π/Γ(s))(2π|m|/9)^{s−1}·D_m(s)·J_ψ(s) + I_m·M_ψ(2 − s) − ⟨P_m(ψ), E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)⟩`, with `J_ψ(s) = ∫_0^∞ conj ψ(v)·v^{−2}·K_{s−1}(4π|m|v/9) dv`, round 428's `D_m(s)`, `I_m = ∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9) dz` and round 427's `M_ψ` (`Eis.inner_pmSer_uL_bessel`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaPmPair.lean`, 732 lines, 28 theorems and 6 definitions; each of its 28 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The band series** (`bandF`, `bandD`, `bandL` and `bandL'`, definitions; **`hasDerivAt_bandL`**, **`differentiable_bandL`** and **`differentiable_inner_bandL`**, with `measurable_bandF`, `measurable_bandD`, `bandF_eq_zero_of_lt`, `bandD_eq_zero_of_lt`, `norm_bandF_le`, `norm_bandD_le`, `bandF_taylor`, `memLp_pseis_bandF` and `memLp_pseis_bandD`).
- **Bounds on `3P × [α, β]`** (`hBd`, a definition; **`tsum_height_rpow_le_unif`** and **`norm_pseis_le_hBd`**, with `norm_le_six_of_mem_fundP3`).
- **Integrals over `3P × [α, β]`** (**`integral_fundP3_conj_mul`** and **`lintegral_rhoT3_pm_ne_top`**, with `zpow_neg_three_le`, `uhsMeasure_fundP3_Icc_lt_top_of_pos` and `integrableOn_fundP3_of_bdd`).
- **The pairing** (**`height_le_band`**, **`eisHigh_eq_band`** and **`inner_pmSer_uL`**, with `le_band` and `eisLow_eq_band`).
- **The Bessel form** (`jPsi`, a definition; **`inner_pmSer_uL_bessel`**, with `integrableOn_Ioi_conj_mul` and `continuousOn_zpow_besselK`).

**The proof.**

- **The band series.** Round 424's proof of `hasDerivAt_gL` goes through for the profile `1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s`. It vanishes below `Y`. Its Taylor remainder in `s` is bounded uniformly in `v` (round 424's `norm_cpow_taylor_le`, with `|log v| ≤ |log Y| + |log H|` on `[Y, H]`, round 424's `abs_log_le_of_mem_Icc`). Round 424's `eLpNorm_pseis_le` turns the uniform bound into a bound in `L²(ν)`. A pairing with a fixed vector is a continuous linear map composed with `s ↦ E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)`.
- **The heights.** Round 387's `height_le_lattice` bounds the height of a bottom row `(c, d)` at `(z, v)` by `9(2v² + 4|z|² + 2)/v` times `((1 + |c|)(1 + |d|))⁻¹`. For `|z| ≤ 6` and `α ≤ v ≤ β` the first factor is at most `9(2β² + 146)/α`. Every `z ∈ 3P` has `|z| ≤ 6` (round 388's `norm_le_two_of_mem_fundP`). The double series of `((1 + |c|)(1 + |d|))^{−σ}` is the square of a convergent series (round 387's `summable_O_rpow`). Round 423's `norm_psTerm_le` bounds each term of a pseudo-Eisenstein series by the corresponding height to the power `σ`.
- **Fubini.** The integrand vanishes outside `3P × [α, β]`, which has finite measure for `dz dv` and on which `v^{−3} ≤ α^{−3}`, so it is integrable for `dz dv`. Mathlib's `integral_prod_symm` then integrates over `z` first, as in round 427's `integral_conj_eisLow`. The same bounds give the finiteness that round 429's `inner_toLp_pmSer` asks for.
- **The pairing.** At a point of `3P × [α, β]` the row `(0, 1)` has height `v ≤ β`, and every other bottom row has height at most `1/v ≤ 1/α` (round 427's `height_le_inv`), so every height is at most `H`. A term of `h_s` is `v^s` at a height `v ≥ Y` and `0` below, so there `h_s` and `E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)` have the same terms. Round 424's `uL_eq_eisLow` gives `ũ_s = E_s − h_s` for `Re s > 2` with `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0`. `E_s − h_s` and `E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)` are automorphic and in `L²(ν)` (round 423's `isAut_eisLow`, `memLp_eisLow` and `isAut_pseis`), so round 429's unfolding applies to each. On `3P × [α, β]`, `E_s − h_s = E_s − E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)`. Both parts are bounded there, and Fubini integrates each over `z` first.
- **The Bessel form.** For `v > 0`, round 428's `integral_ebr_eis1_fundP3` writes the inner integral as `v^s·I_m + (2π/Γ(s))(2π|m|/9)^{s−1}·v·K_{s−1}(4π|m|v/9)·D_m(s)`. Each part is `conj ψ` times a function continuous on `(0, ∞)` (round 373's `continuousAt_besselK`), hence bounded on `[α, β]`, and `ψ` vanishes outside `[α, β]`, so each is integrable.

All landed, with one difference. The band's upper end is `H = Y + β + 1/α` in place of `H₀`, so that `Y ≤ H`, which the bound on the band profile uses; every height is at most `H₀ ≤ H`. ## Round 431: S5f-10f, part 4 — the pairing of `P_m(ψ)` with θ (`src/KubotaPmTheta.lean`)

**What it is.** The eighteenth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the fourth part of S5f-10f. Round 430's next step planned `⟨P_m(ψ), θ⟩ = ρ(m)·J_ψ(4/3)` with `ρ(m)` independent of `ψ`, for `m = δ₃x ≠ 0`. This round proves it, for `r > 0`, `Y > 0`, `a = 4π|m|/9`, and `ψ` measurable and bounded, vanishing outside `[α, β]` with `0 < α ≤ β`:

- `J_ψ` is entire (`Eis.differentiable_jPsi`);
- for two such profiles, `⟨P_m(ψ₁), θ⟩·J_{ψ₂}(4/3) = ⟨P_m(ψ₂), θ⟩·J_{ψ₁}(4/3)` (`Eis.inner_pmSer_thetaL_cross`);
- `J_{1_{[1, 2]}}(4/3) ≠ 0` (`Eis.jPsi_ind12_ne_zero`), so with `ρ(m) = ⟨P_m(1_{[1, 2]}), θ⟩/J_{1_{[1, 2]}}(4/3)`, `⟨P_m(ψ), θ⟩ = ρ(m)·J_ψ(4/3)`, where `J_ψ(4/3) = ∫_0^∞ conj ψ(v)·v^{−2}·K_{1/3}(4π|m|v/9) dv` (`Eis.inner_pmSer_thetaL`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaPmTheta.lean`, 557 lines, 21 theorems and 5 definitions; each of its 21 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **`J_ψ` is entire** (`jKer`, a definition; **`jPsi_eq_mellin`** and **`differentiable_jPsi`**, with `bkK_le_one`, `measurable_bkK`, `zpow_neg_two_le`, `bkK_isBigO_bot`, `measurable_jKer_integrand`, `norm_jKer_integrand_le`, `norm_jKer_le` and `continuousOn_jKer`).
- **Two profiles** (`besC` and `aPm`, definitions; **`aPm_eq`**, **`differentiableOn_aPm`**, **`tendsto_aPm`** and **`inner_pmSer_thetaL_cross`**).
- **`ρ(m)`** (`ind12` and `rhoM`, definitions; **`jPsi_ind12_ne_zero`** and **`inner_pmSer_thetaL`**, with `bkR_pos`, `measurable_ind12`, `norm_ind12_le`, `ind12_eq_zero` and `memLp_pmSer_ind12`).

**The proof.**

- **`J_ψ` is entire.** `K_ν(x)` is half the Mellin transform at `ν` of round 361's kernel `bkK(x, ·)`, `t ↦ e^{−x(t + 1/t)/2}`. So `J_ψ(s)` is a double integral over `v` and `t`, absolutely convergent: its integrand is at most `M·α^{−2}·1_{[α, β]}(v)` times `t^{Re s − 2}·bkK(aα, t)`, since `bkK` decreases in `x` (round 361's `bkK_anti`), and the second factor is integrable (round 361's `integrableOn_bkR`). Fubini (Mathlib's `integral_integral_swap`) gives `J_ψ(s) = ½·M[G](s − 1)` with `G(t) = ∫_0^∞ conj ψ(v)·v^{−2}·bkK(av, t) dv`. `G` is continuous on `(0, ∞)` by dominated convergence, since `bkK ≤ 1` there, and `|G(t)| ≤ C·bkK(aα, t)`. Round 361's `bkK_le_top` gives the decay `e^{−aαt/2}` at `∞`, and `bkK_isBigO_bot`, the argument of round 361's `mellinConvergent_bkK` as a lemma, gives `O(t^{−b})` at `0` for every `b`. Mathlib's `mellin_differentiableAt_of_isBigO_rpow_exp` then applies at every point, as in round 428's `differentiable_besselK`.
- **Two profiles.** `A_ψ(s) = ⟨P_m(ψ), ũ_s⟩ − I_m·M_ψ(2 − s) + ⟨P_m(ψ), E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)⟩`, with `H = Y + β + 1/α`, is `(2π/Γ(s))(2π|m|/9)^{s−1}·D_m(s)·J_ψ(s)` for `Re s > 2` with `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0` (round 430's `inner_pmSer_uL_bessel`). So `F = A_{ψ₁}J_{ψ₂} − A_{ψ₂}J_{ψ₁}` vanishes on the open set `U ∩ {Re s > 2}`, where `U = {Re s > 1, 0 < Im s < π/r}` is round 427's domain. On `U`, `Im ĥ(s) > 0` (round 418's `im_hhat_pos`), so `F` is holomorphic there (round 424's `differentiableAt_inner_uL`, round 427's `differentiable_mellinPsi`, round 430's `differentiable_inner_bandL`, and `differentiable_jPsi`). Mathlib's identity theorem gives `F = 0` on `U`, as in round 427. Along `s = 4/3 + iε`, which lies in `U` for `0 < ε < π/r`, `iε·⟨P_m(ψ), ũ_s⟩ → ⟨P_m(ψ), θ⟩` (round 425's `tendsto_uL_thetaL`). The other two terms of `iε·A_ψ(s)` tend to `0`, since they are `iε` times continuous functions of `s`. And `J_ψ(s) → J_ψ(4/3)`. So the limit of `iε·F(s) = 0` is `⟨P_m(ψ₁), θ⟩·J_{ψ₂}(4/3) − ⟨P_m(ψ₂), θ⟩·J_{ψ₁}(4/3)`.
- **`ρ(m)`.** For `x > 0`, `bkR(r, x) > 0`, since its integrand is positive on `(0, ∞)` and integrable (Mathlib's `setIntegral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg_ae`). So `K_{1/3}(x) = ½·bkR(1/3, x) > 0` (round 374's `besselK_third_ofReal`), and `J_{1_{[1, 2]}}(4/3) = ∫_1^2 v^{−2}·K_{1/3}(av) dv > 0`. The cross relation with `ψ₂ = 1_{[1, 2]}`, which is in `L²(ν)` by round 429's `memLp_pmSer_Icc`, then gives `⟨P_m(ψ), θ⟩ = ρ(m)·J_ψ(4/3)`.

**Against the plan.** Round 430's next step listed:

- "`J_ψ` entire, for `ψ` measurable, bounded and vanishing outside `[α, β]`, `α > 0`: `K_ν(x)` is half the Mellin transform at `ν` of round 361's kernel `bkK(x, ·)`, so `J_ψ(s)` is half the Mellin transform at `s − 1` of `t ↦ ∫conj ψ(v)v^{−2}·bkK(4π|m|v/9, t) dv` (Fubini), which has the decay of round 361's `mellinConvergent_bkK`; Mathlib's `mellin_differentiableAt_of_isBigO_rpow_exp` applies at every point, as in round 428's `differentiable_besselK`;"
- "the ratio of two profiles: with `A_ψ(s) = ⟨P_m(ψ), ũ_s⟩ − I_m·M_ψ(2 − s) + ⟨P_m(ψ), E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)⟩`, this round gives `A_{ψ₁}(s)·J_{ψ₂}(s) = A_{ψ₂}(s)·J_{ψ₁}(s)` for `Re s > 2` with `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0`, since both sides are `(2π/Γ(s))(2π|m|/9)^{s−1}·D_m(s)·J_{ψ₁}(s)·J_{ψ₂}(s)`; both sides are holomorphic on round 427's `U` (round 424's `differentiableAt_inner_uL`), so they agree on `U` (Mathlib's identity theorem, as in round 427), and along `s = 4/3 + iε` (round 425's `tendsto_uL_thetaL`) `⟨P_m(ψ₁), θ⟩·J_{ψ₂}(4/3) = ⟨P_m(ψ₂), θ⟩·J_{ψ₁}(4/3)`;"
- "a profile `ψ₀` with `J_{ψ₀}(4/3) ≠ 0`, such as `1_{[α, α + 1]}`, through the positivity of `K_{1/3}` on `(0, ∞)` (round 374's `besselK_third_ofReal`); then `ρ(m) = ⟨P_m(ψ₀), θ⟩/J_{ψ₀}(4/3)`."

All landed. The profile is `1_{[1, 2]}`. The positivity of `K_{1/3}` also needs that of round 361's `bkR`, which this round proves (`bkR_pos`). The decay at `0` is `bkK_isBigO_bot`, stated separately; round 361 and round 428 prove it inside their proofs. The identity theorem is applied to the difference `A_{ψ₁}J_{ψ₂} − A_{ψ₂}J_{ψ₁}` and the zero function.

**The next step.** S5f-10f, part 5: the Fourier coefficients of θ. With `θ̃` round 425's automorphic representative of θ (`thetaF`, equal to θ almost everywhere by round 425's `thetaL_ae_eq_thetaF`), the plan, for `m = δ₃x ≠ 0`:

See round 432.)*
- then `⟨P_m(ψ), θ⟩ = ∫_0^∞ v^{−3}·conj ψ(v)·∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)θ̃(z, v) dz dv` (Fubini), and this round's theorem for every profile gives `∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)θ̃(z, v) dz = ρ(m)·v·K_{1/3}(4π|m|v/9)` for almost every `v > 0`. *(Round 432: landed, `Eis.inner_pmSer_thetaL_unfold` and `Eis.coef_thetaF_ae`. See round 432.)*

Then the constant term of θ̃ in the same way (round 427's `inner_pseis_thetaL`, with round 430's band series for profiles below `max(Y, 1/Y)`), and the Fourier expansion of θ̃.

## Round 432: S5f-10f, part 5 — the Fourier coefficients of θ (`src/KubotaThetaCoef.lean`)

**What it is.** The nineteenth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the fifth part of S5f-10f. Round 431's next step planned the Fourier coefficients of θ's automorphic representative `θ̃` (round 425's `thetaF`, equal to θ almost everywhere). This round proves them, for `m = δ₃x`, `r > 0` and `Y > 0`:

- for `α > 0` the number of `γ ∈ SL_2(ℤ[ω])` with `γ·p` in the box `{|z| ≤ Z, α ≤ v ≤ β}` is bounded independently of `p` (`Eis.tsum_boxZ_le`);
- a measurable `u` with `|u|` invariant under `Γ_1(3)` and `∫|u| dν < ∞` is integrable on every such box against `dz dv/v³` (`Eis.lintegral_boxZ_lt_top`), in particular `θ̃` (`Eis.lintegral_boxZ_thetaF_lt_top`);
- for `ψ` measurable and bounded, vanishing outside `[α, β]` with `α > 0`, `⟨P_m(ψ), θ⟩ = ∫_0^∞ v^{−3}·conj ψ(v)·∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)θ̃(z, v) dz dv` (`Eis.inner_pmSer_thetaL_unfold`);
- for `x ≠ 0`, `∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)θ̃(z, v) dz = ρ(m)·v·K_{1/3}(4π|m|v/9)` for almost every `v > 0`, with round 431's `ρ(m)` (`Eis.coef_thetaF_ae`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaThetaCoef.lean`, 677 lines, 21 theorems, 5 definitions and an instance; each of its 21 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`). *(Round 434: 687 lines and 22 theorems, with 22 axiom lines of the same kind; `lintegral_boxZ_le`, the bound inside `lintegral_boxZ_lt_top`'s proof, is a theorem of its own. See round 434.)*

- **Counting** (`rowBd`, `boxT`, `cBox`, `boxZ` and `cTr`, definitions; **`tsum_boxT_le`** and **`tsum_boxZ_le`**, with `rowBd_finite`, `row_mem_rowBd`, `measurableSet_boxT`, `cBox_ne_top`, `tsum_boxT_le_of_siegel`, `measurableSet_boxZ` and `cTr_ne_top`). *(Round 516: `measurableSet_boxT`, which no proof used, is removed.)*
- **Local integrability** (the instance `isFiniteMeasure_muR_rhoG`; **`lintegral_boxZ_lt_top`** and **`lintegral_boxZ_thetaF_lt_top`**, with `measurable_thetaF`, `memLp_thetaF` and `enorm_thetaF_slAct`).
- **Unfolding** (**`inner_pmSer_thetaL_unfold`**, with `setLIntegral_volume_le` and `integral_fundP3_conj_mul_of_int`).
- **The coefficients** (**`coef_thetaF_ae`**, with `integrableOn_slice`, `integrableOn_ebr_thetaF` and `Ioi_zero_eq_iUnion_Icc`).

**The proof.**

- **Counting.** Let `s` be in round 385's Siegel set, so `|z(s)| ≤ 2` and `v(s) ≥ 1/2`. If `γ·s` has height at least `α`, then `α(|cz + d|² + |c|²v²) ≤ v` for the bottom row `(c, d)` of `γ`. This bounds `|c|² ≤ 2/α`. If `c ≠ 0`, then `|c| ≥ 1` (round 361's `one_le_norm_σO`), so `v ≤ 1/α` and `|d| ≤ 1/α + 2√(2/α)`. If `c = 0`, `d` is a unit and `|d| = 1` (round 368's `norm_σO_unit`). So the bottom rows lie in a finite set depending only on `α` (round 385's `finite_normSq_le`). Two `γ` with the same bottom row differ by a translation (round 385's `eq_slT_mul`), and a translation moves `P` off itself (round 385's `eq_zero_of_mem_fundP`). So at most one of them sends `s` into a given translate `(P + σ(t)) × [α, β]`. Every orbit meets the Siegel set (round 385's `exists_mem_siegelK`), so the bound holds at every point. The disc `|z| ≤ Z` is covered by the translates `P + σ(t)` with `|σ(t)| ≤ Z + 2` (round 385's `exists_transl_mem_fundP`).
- **Local integrability.** Round 386's `lintegral_unfold` writes `∫_{box}|u| dμ` as `∫ρ_G(p)·Σ_γ 1_{box}(γp)·|u(p)| dμ(p)`, using the invariance of `|u|`. The sum over `Γ_1(3)` is at most the sum over `SL_2(ℤ[ω])`, which counting bounds. `ν = ρ_G dμ` is finite (round 423's `lintegral_puLe_top_mul_lt_top`). So `θ̃ ∈ L²(ν)` (round 425's `thetaL_ae_eq_thetaF`) is in `L¹(ν)`. `|θ̃(γp)| = |θ̃(p)|` by round 425's `isAut_thetaF`, since `|κ(γ)| = 1`. `θ̃` is measurable, being a kernel integral of θ (Mathlib's `StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right'`).
- **Unfolding.** Round 429's `inner_toLp_pmSer` applies with `u = θ̃`, since `rhoT3·|conj(ψĕ)θ̃|` is at most `M·|θ̃|` on the box `{|z| ≤ 6, α ≤ v ≤ β}`, which contains `3P × [α, β]` (round 430's `norm_le_six_of_mem_fundP3`). Round 430's Fubini, `integral_fundP3_conj_mul`, asks for a bound on `F`. Its proof goes through for `F` integrable on `3P × [α, β]` for `dz dv`, which follows from local integrability, since `v^{−3} ≥ β^{−3}` there (`setLIntegral_volume_le`).
- **The coefficients.** Let `S` be a measurable subset of `[1/(n + 1), n + 1]` and `ψ = 1_S`. This round's unfolding and round 431's `inner_pmSer_thetaL` give `∫_S v^{−3}·a(v) dv = ρ(m)·∫_S v^{−2}K_{1/3}(4π|m|v/9) dv`, with `a(v) = ∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)θ̃(z, v) dz`. Here `a` is integrable on `[1/(n + 1), n + 1]` by Fubini's slice (Mathlib's `Integrable.integral_prod_right`), and the Bessel term is continuous there (round 430's `continuousOn_zpow_besselK`). Mathlib's `Integrable.ae_eq_zero_of_forall_setIntegral_eq_zero` gives `v^{−3}a(v) = ρ(m)·v^{−2}K_{1/3}(4π|m|v/9)` for almost every `v` in `[1/(n + 1), n + 1]`. These intervals cover `(0, ∞)`.

## Round 433: S5f-10f, part 6 — the constant term of θ (`src/KubotaThetaConst.lean`)

**What it is.** The twentieth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the sixth part of S5f-10f. Round 432's next step planned the constant term of θ's representative `θ̃` for all `v > 0`. This round proves it, for `r > 0`, `Y > 0`, and `ψ` measurable and bounded, vanishing outside `[α, β]` with `0 < α ≤ β`:

- for `Re s > 2` with `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0`, `⟨E(ψ), ũ_s⟩ = (9√3/2)·(M_ψ(2 − s) + φ(s)M_ψ(s)) − ⟨E(ψ), E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)⟩` with `H = Y + β + 1/α` (`Eis.inner_pseis_uL_band`);

- `∫_{3P} θ̃(z, v) dz = (9√3/2)·Res φ·v^{2/3}` for almost every `v > 0` (`Eis.const_thetaF_ae`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaThetaConst.lean`, 435 lines, 8 theorems; each of its 8 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The residue** (**`inner_pseis_thetaL_gen`**).
- **The constant term** (**`inner_pseis_thetaL_unfold`** and **`const_thetaF_ae`**, with `integrableOn_thetaF` and `ae_eq_of_setIntegral_Icc`).

**The proof.**

- **The pairing for `Re s > 2`.** As in round 430, with `E(ψ)` in place of `P_m(ψ)` and round 426's `inner_toLp_pseis` in place of round 429's unfolding. On `3P × [α, β]`, `E_s − h_s = E_s − E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)` (round 430's `eisLow_eq_band`), and both are bounded there (round 430's `norm_pseis_le_hBd`). Round 389's `constTerm_eis1` gives `∫_{3P} E(z, v; s) dz = (9√3/2)·(v^s + φ(s)v^{2−s})` for every `v > 0`. With `v^{−3}·v^s = v^{−1−(2−s)}` and `v^{−3}·v^{2−s} = v^{−1−s}` (round 427's `cpow_neg_one_sub`), the integral over `v` is `(9√3/2)·(M_ψ(2 − s) + φ(s)M_ψ(s))`.
- **The residue.** `F(s) = ⟨E(ψ), ũ_s⟩ + ⟨E(ψ), E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)⟩ − (9√3/2)·M_ψ(2 − s)` and `G(s) = (9√3/2)·φ(s)M_ψ(s)` agree for `Re s > 2` in round 427's `U` (round 416's `eisPhi_eq_phiC`). Both are holomorphic on `U`: round 424's `differentiableAt_inner_uL`, round 430's `differentiable_inner_bandL`, round 427's `differentiable_mellinPsi` and round 417's `differentiableAt_phiC`. So they agree on `U` (Mathlib's identity theorem). Along `s = 4/3 + iε`, `iε·F(s) → ⟨E(ψ), θ⟩` (round 425's `tendsto_uL_thetaL`, the other two terms being `iε` times continuous functions), and `iε·G(s) → (9√3/2)·Res φ·M_ψ(4/3)` (round 417's `tendsto_phiC_residue`), as in round 427.
- **The constant term.** Round 426's `inner_toLp_pseis` applies with `u = θ̃` by round 432's local integrability, and round 432's `integral_fundP3_conj_mul_of_int` integrates over `z` first. With `ψ = 1_S` for measurable `S ⊆ [1/(n + 1), n + 1]`, the two pairings give `∫_S v^{−3}·a₀(v) dv = (9√3/2)·Res φ·∫_S v^{−1−4/3} dv`, with `a₀(v) = ∫_{3P} θ̃(z, v) dz`. `ae_eq_of_setIntegral_Icc`, the argument of round 432's `coef_thetaF_ae` stated for any two functions, gives `v^{−3}·a₀(v) = (9√3/2)·Res φ·v^{−7/3}` for almost every `v > 0`.

**Against the plan.** Round 432's next step listed:

- "the identity theorem and the limit, as in round 427, giving `⟨E(ψ), θ⟩ = (9√3/2)·Res φ·M_ψ(4/3)` for every such `ψ`;"
- "unfolding `E(ψ)` against `θ̃` (round 426's `inner_toLp_pseis`, with this round's local integrability), and as in this round, `∫_{3P} θ̃(z, v) dz = (9√3/2)·Res φ·v^{2/3}` for almost every `v > 0`."

All landed, with `α ≤ β` added to the first two. The band's upper end `H = Y + β + 1/α` needs it, as in round 430.

See round 434.)*
- for `m = δ₃x ≠ 0` and `v_m = 9/(4π|m|)`, the integral of `|a_m(v)| ≤ ∫_{3P}|θ̃(z, v)| dz` over `[v_m, 2v_m]` is at most `(2v_m)³` times the integral of `|θ̃|` over the box `{|z| ≤ 6, v_m ≤ v ≤ 2v_m}` against `dz dv/v³`, which round 432's `lintegral_boxZ_lt_top` bounds by `cTr(6)·cBox(v_m)·∫|θ̃| dν`; with round 432's `coef_thetaF_ae`, the left side is `|ρ(m)|·v_m²·∫_1^2 u·K_{1/3}(u) du`, so `|ρ(m)| ≤ C(1 + |m|)^N`. *(Round 434: landed with `N = 5`, as `|ρ(m)| ≤ C·|m|⁵`, the left side bounded below through the decrease of `K_{1/3}`, and the bound inside `lintegral_boxZ_lt_top`'s proof stated as `Eis.lintegral_boxZ_le`; `Eis.norm_rhoM_le`. ## Round 434: S5f-10f, part 7 — the growth of θ's Fourier coefficients (`src/KubotaThetaGrowth.lean`)

**What it is.** The twenty-first step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the seventh part of S5f-10f. Round 433's next step planned a growth bound for the coefficients `ρ(m)` of θ (round 431's `rhoM`). This round proves it, with `m = δ₃x` and `|m| = |σ(m)|`:

- `#{x ∈ ℤ[ω] : |σ(x)|² ≤ R} ≤ (4R + 3)²` for `R ≥ 0` (`Eis.tsum_normSq_le_le`), so round 432's count `cBox(α)` of bottom rows is at most `(11/α)²(147/α²)²` for `0 < α ≤ 1` (`Eis.cBox_le`);
- for `u` measurable with `|u|` invariant under `Γ_1(3)`, `∫|u| dz dv/v³ ≤ cTr(Z)·cBox(α)·∫|u| dν` over each box `{|z| ≤ Z, α ≤ v ≤ β}` with `α > 0` (`Eis.lintegral_boxZ_le`, added to `src/KubotaThetaCoef.lean`);
- for `r > 0` and `Y > 0` there is `C` with `|ρ(m)| ≤ C·|m|⁵` for every `m = δ₃x ≠ 0` (`Eis.norm_rhoM_le`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaThetaGrowth.lean`, 278 lines, 4 theorems; each of its 4 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. `src/KubotaThetaCoef.lean` gains 1 theorem, whose axiom line is the same).

- **Counting** (**`tsum_normSq_le_le`** and **`cBox_le`**).
- **The box bound** (**`lintegral_boxZ_le`**, in `KubotaThetaCoef.lean`).
- **The growth of `ρ(m)`** (**`norm_rhoM_le`**, with `bkR_anti`).

**The proof.**

- **Counting.** Write `x = a + bω` with round 294's coordinates `crd`. Then `|σ(x)|² = a² − ab + b²` (round 361's `normSq_σO_crd`), so `|σ(x)|² ≤ R` gives `a² ≤ 2R` and `b² ≤ 2R`, hence `|a|, |b| ≤ ⌈2R⌉`, as in the proof of round 385's `finite_normSq_le`. There are `(2⌈2R⌉ + 1)² ≤ (4R + 3)²` such pairs. A row `(c, d)` of round 432's `rowBd(α)` has `|σ(c)|² ≤ 2/α` and `|σ(d)| ≤ 1 + 1/α + 2√(2/α) ≤ 6/α` for `α ≤ 1`, so `cBox(α) ≤ (8/α + 3)²(144/α² + 3)² ≤ (11/α)²(147/α²)²`.
- **The box bound.** It is the bound inside round 432's proof of `lintegral_boxZ_lt_top`, by round 386's `lintegral_unfold` and round 432's `tsum_boxZ_le`. It is now a theorem of its own, and `lintegral_boxZ_lt_top` follows from it.
- **The lower bound.** Let `A = 4π|m|/9` and `v₀ = 1/A`. Since `|m| ≥ 1` (round 361's `one_le_norm_σO`), `A ≥ 1` and `v₀ ≤ 1`. For almost every `v > 0`, `a_m(v) = ∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)θ̃(z, v) dz = ρ(m)·v·K_{1/3}(Av)` (round 432's `coef_thetaF_ae`), and `K_{1/3}(x) = bkR(1/3, x)/2` (round 374's `besselK_third_ofReal`). On `[v₀, 2v₀]`, `Av ≤ 2`, so `bkR(1/3, Av) ≥ bkR(1/3, 2) > 0` (`bkR_anti` and round 431's `bkR_pos`). So `∫_{v₀}^{2v₀}|a_m| ≥ |ρ(m)|·v₀²·bkR(1/3, 2)/2`.
- **The upper bound.** `|a_m(v)| ≤ ∫_{3P}|θ̃(z, v)| dz`, since `|ĕ| = 1`. Tonelli turns the integral over `[v₀, 2v₀]` into one over `3P × [v₀, 2v₀]`, which is at most `(2v₀)³` times the integral against `dz dv/v³` (round 432's `setLIntegral_volume_le`). `3P` lies in `{|z| ≤ 6}` (round 430's `norm_le_six_of_mem_fundP3`), and `lintegral_boxZ_le` with `cBox_le` bounds the integral over the box by `cTr(6)·(11/v₀)²(147/v₀²)²·∫|θ̃| dν`. That is finite, since `θ̃` is in `L²(ν)` and `ν` is finite (round 432's `memLp_thetaF` and `isFiniteMeasure_muR_rhoG`). So `|ρ(m)|·v₀²·bkR(1/3, 2)/2 ≤ 8·11²·147²·cTr(6)·∫|θ̃| dν·v₀^{−3}`, and `v₀^{−5} = A⁵ = (4π/9)⁵|m|⁵`.

**Against the plan.** Round 433's next step listed:

- "the counts of round 432 with explicit constants: `#{x ∈ ℤ[ω] : |σ(x)|² ≤ R}` at most polynomial in `R` (from the proof of round 385's `finite_normSq_le`), so `cBox(α)` at most polynomial in `1/α`;"
- "for `m = δ₃x ≠ 0` and `v_m = 9/(4π|m|)`, the integral of `|a_m(v)| ≤ ∫_{3P}|θ̃(z, v)| dz` over `[v_m, 2v_m]` is at most `(2v_m)³` times the integral of `|θ̃|` over the box `{|z| ≤ 6, v_m ≤ v ≤ 2v_m}` against `dz dv/v³`, which round 432's `lintegral_boxZ_lt_top` bounds by `cTr(6)·cBox(v_m)·∫|θ̃| dν`; with round 432's `coef_thetaF_ae`, the left side is `|ρ(m)|·v_m²·∫_1^2 u·K_{1/3}(u) du`, so `|ρ(m)| ≤ C(1 + |m|)^N`."

Both landed. The bound for `cBox(α)` is stated for `0 < α ≤ 1`, the range the growth bound uses. Round 432's `lintegral_boxZ_lt_top` states only that the box integral is finite; the bound inside its proof is now `lintegral_boxZ_le`. The left side is bounded below by `|ρ(m)|·v_m²·K_{1/3}(2)`, since `K_{1/3}` decreases, instead of being computed as `|ρ(m)|·v_m²·∫_1^2 u·K_{1/3}(u) du`. The exponent is `N = 5`, in the form `|ρ(m)| ≤ C·|m|⁵`. Since `|ρ(m)| ≥ 0` and `|m| > 0`, `C ≥ 0`, so this gives the planned `C(1 + |m|)⁵`.

**The next step.** S5f-10f, part 8: θ as its Fourier series. The plan, with `c₀ = Res φ`, `τ(δ₃x) = ρ(δ₃x)/(9√3/2)` for `x ≠ 0` and `τ = 0` elsewhere, and `S(z, v) = thSer c₀ τ z v` (round 361's `thSer`):

- `S` converges absolutely and locally uniformly on upper half-space, by this round's growth bound and the decay of `K_{1/3}` (round 361's `bkR_le_exp`), so `S` is continuous there;
- the characters `ĕ(mz/9)`, `m ∈ δ₃ℤ[ω]`, are orthogonal on `3P`, with `∫_{3P} ĕ(mz/9) dz = 0` for `m ≠ 0` (the integral round 428 left unevaluated), so that for every `v > 0` the coefficients `∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)S(z, v) dz` are those rounds 432 and 433 found for `θ̃` at almost every `v`; *(Round 435: the orthogonality landed, `Eis.integral_fundP3_ebr_eq_zero` and `Eis.integral_fundP3_ebr_mul`; the coefficients of `S` remain. See round 435.)*
- uniqueness: a function periodic under `3ℤ[ω]`, square-integrable on `3P`, whose coefficients all vanish, is zero almost everywhere, through the linear map `(s, t) ↦ 3(s + tω)` from `ℝ²/ℤ²` onto `ℂ/3ℤ[ω]` and Mathlib's Fourier basis `mFourierBasis` of `L²` of the unit torus. With the local square-integrability of `θ̃` (`lintegral_boxZ_le` applied to `|θ̃|²`), `θ̃ = S` almost everywhere. *(Round 435: the uniqueness landed, on `3P` without periodicity, `Eis.ae_eq_zero_of_coef`, and on `ℂ` for periodic functions, `Eis.ae_eq_zero_of_periodic`; `θ̃ = S` remains. See round 435.)*

Then `S` automorphic at every point, from the automorphy of `θ̃`, the invariance of `dz dv/v³` (round 383) and the continuity of `S`. The continuity of `θ̃` itself, which round 432's next step listed, is then not needed. After that, S5f-11 to S5f-16 of round 360's plan.
