## Round 448: S5f-12, part 9 — the traces and the cube eigenrelation (`src/KubotaCubeEigen.lean`)

**What it is.** The thirty-fifth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the ninth part of S5f-12. Round 447's next step planned the data of round 439's `translates_eq_zero` for the cube translates, the constant terms of the traces, and then `D = 0` almost everywhere and the eigenrelation at every point for θ's Fourier series `thS` (round 436). Here `p` is a primary prime, `M_q` is round 446's `cubeMat`, which acts by `(z, v) ↦ ((z + 3q)/p³, v/|p|³)`, and `D = N(p)⁻³Σ_{q mod p³} θ̃∘M_q − N(p)⁻¹θ̃` is round 446's `cubeDiff`. This round carries out all three. For `r > 0` and `Y > 0`:

- `D = 0` almost everywhere on upper half-space (`Eis.cubeDiff_ae_eq_zero`);
- `N(p)⁻³Σ_{q mod p³} thS(M_q·P) = N(p)⁻¹·thS(P)` for every `P` in upper half-space (`Eis.thS_cube_eigen`), that is, `N(p)⁻³Σ_{q mod p³} thS((z + 3q)/p³, v/|p|³) = N(p)⁻¹·thS(z, v)` for every `z ∈ ℂ` and `v > 0` (`Eis.thS_cube_eigen_coord`).

This is the cube eigenrelation of S5f-12.

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaCubeEigen.lean`, 449 lines, 18 theorems and 4 definitions; each of its 18 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **Almost every height** (`ae_Ioi_comp_mul`).
- **Slices** (`integrableOn_fundP3_of_mul`, `integrable_cubeDiff_slAct` and `integrable_cubeDiff_inv_slAct`).
- **The translates** (`cubeG`, `cubeC`, `cubeH` and `cubeE`, definitions, with `det_cubeG`, `cubeH_le`, `finite_cubeH`, `slAct_cubeE`, `kub_cubeE` and `sum_cubeC`).
- **The traces** (**`integral_trace_cube`**).
- **The eigenrelation almost everywhere** (`ae_good_heights`; **`cubeDiff_ae_eq_zero`**).
- **The eigenrelation at every point** (`continuousOn_actP`, `ae_uhs_thetaF_eq_thS` and `ae_thetaF_eq_thS_actP`; **`thS_cube_eigen`** and **`thS_cube_eigen_coord`**).

**The proof.**

- **Almost every height.** For `c > 0`, `v ↦ cv` maps Lebesgue measure to a multiple of itself (Mathlib's `Real.map_volume_mul_left`), so a property of almost every `w > 0` holds at `cv` for almost every `v > 0`.
- **Slices.** For `G ≥ 0` measurable and periodic under `3ℤ[ω]` and `μ ∈ ℤ[ω]` nonzero, `∫_{3P} G(μz) dz = ∫_{3P} G` (round 444's `lintegral_fundP3_mul`), so a measurable function periodic under `3ℤ[ω]` is integrable on `3P` when `z ↦ f(μz)` is. Along an affine image of `3P` whose multiplier is divisible by `p³`, each term of `D∘γ`, for `γ ∈ Γ_1(3)`, is `κ(γ′)·θ̃` along another affine image of `3P` (round 446's `cubeMat_slAct`). The mean of θ̃ there is its constant term at the new height (round 446's `integral_thetaF_affine`), which is not `0` (round 443's `const_theta_ne_zero`), so the term is integrable (Mathlib's `Integrable.of_integral_ne_zero`), as in the proofs of round 446's two theorems. For a multiplier divisible by `p⁶`, `M_q⁻¹γ = γ′β′` (round 446's `cubeMat_inv_slAct`) turns `D∘M_q⁻¹∘γ` into `D∘γ′` along an affine image of `3P` whose multiplier is divisible by `p³`.
- **The translates.** They are indexed by `Option (ℤ[ω]/p³)`: `I`, with coefficient `−N(p)⁻¹`, the group `Γ(3p³)` and the identity, and `M_q`, with coefficient `N(p)⁻³`, the group `Γ′(p)` and round 447's `cubeEquiv`. Round 447's `slAct_cubeEquiv` and `kub_cubeEquiv` give the intertwining and the invariance of `κ` for `M_q`; for `I` they hold since `I` acts as the identity (round 439's `actP_one`). The combination `Σ_j c_j·θ̃∘g_j` is `D` (Mathlib's `Fintype.sum_option`).
- **The traces.** Each `θ̃∘g_j` is automorphic on `Γ(3p³)` (round 439's `isAut_comp_actP`, with round 425's `isAut_thetaF`), so `D` is, and `D∘g⁻¹` is automorphic on the group of the translate `g` (round 439's `isAut_comp_actP_inv`). Its trace to `Γ_1(3)` is automorphic on `Γ_1(3)` (round 439's `isAut_trK`). The translations by `3ℤ[ω]` lie in `Γ_1(3)` and have `κ = 1` (round 387's `slT_mem_Gam3`, round 426's `kub_slT`), so the trace is periodic under `3ℤ[ω]`. At `(p⁶z, v)` the trace is a finite sum of terms `conj κ(δ)·D(g⁻¹·δ·(p⁶z, v))` with `δ ∈ Γ_1(3)`. At a height `v` where θ̃ has its constant term at `v`, at `|p|^{2k−3}v` and at `|p|^{2k−3}|p|^{2j−3}v` for `j, k ≤ 3`, each term is integrable on `3P` with mean `0`, by the slices above and round 446's `integral_cubeDiff_slAct` and `integral_cubeDiff_inv_slAct`, with `μ = p⁶` and `t = 0`. So the slice of the trace at `v` is integrable on `3P`, its mean is that of its rescaling by `p⁶` (round 444's `integral_fundP3_mul`), and this mean is `0`.
- **The eigenrelation almost everywhere.** θ̃ has its constant term at almost every height (round 433's `const_thetaF_ae`), so, by the scaling above, almost every `v > 0` is a height as in the traces (`ae_good_heights`). The traces then have constant term `0` at almost every height, and round 439's `translates_eq_zero` gives `D = 0` almost everywhere.
- **The eigenrelation at every point.** θ̃ equals `thS` almost everywhere on upper half-space (round 437's `ae_thetaF_eq_thS`), so also for `dz dv/v³` (round 383's `uhsMeasure`), which has a density with respect to Lebesgue measure there (Mathlib's `withDensity_absolutelyContinuous`). The `M_q` preserve `dz dv/v³` (round 383's `measurePreserving_actP`), so `θ̃∘M_q = thS∘M_q` almost everywhere too, and the two sides of the eigenrelation for `thS` agree almost everywhere. Both are continuous on upper half-space: `thS` is (round 436's `continuousOn_thS`), and so is the action of a matrix of determinant `1` (`continuousOn_actP`, through round 361's `uhsDen_pos`, as round 437's `continuousOn_slAct`). As in round 443, Lebesgue measure on upper half-space has the null sets of `dz dv/v³` there (round 443's `restrict_UHS_ac`), and continuous functions equal almost everywhere on an open set are equal there (Mathlib's `Measure.eqOn_open_of_ae_eq`). In coordinates this is `thS_cube_eigen_coord` (round 446's `actP_cubeMat`).

## Round 449: S5f-12, part 10 — θ's coefficients at `p³m` (`src/KubotaCubeCoef.lean`)

**What it is.** The thirty-sixth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the tenth part of S5f-12. Round 448's next step planned the cube average of a theta-type series and, from round 448's `thS_cube_eigen_coord`, the relation `τ(p³m) = |p|·τ(m)` for the coefficients `τ` of θ's Fourier series (round 436's `tauTh`, with `thS = thSer(Res φ, τ)`). This round proves them. For `r > 0`, `Y > 0` and a primary prime `p`:

- `τ(p³m) = |p|·τ(m)` for every `m ∈ ℤ[ω]` (`Eis.tauTh_cube`);
- `ρ(p³x) = |p|·ρ(x)` for every `x ≠ 0` (`Eis.rhoM_cube`), with round 431's `ρ = rhoM`, so that `ρ(x)·v·K_{1/3}(4π|δ₃x|v/9)` is the integral of `ĕ(−δ₃xz/9)·thS(z, v)` over `3P` (round 436's `integral_ebr_thS`).

With round 448's eigenrelation this completes S5f-12.

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaCubeCoef.lean`, 276 lines, 8 theorems; each of its 8 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The character sum** (`sum_ebr_quot`).
- **The cube average of a theta-type series** (`thTerm_add_div`, `thTerm_cube` and `sum_thTerm_cube`; **`cube_avg_thSer`**).
- **The coefficients** (`thSer_coef_eq`; **`tauTh_cube`** and **`rhoM_cube`**).

**The proof.**

- **The character sum.** For `c ≠ 0`, `ĕ(σ(δ₃x)·(σ(3q)/σ(c))/9) = ψ_c(−qx)` (round 363's `ebr_shift`, with `δ₃² = −3`), and `Σ_{q mod c} ψ_c(qb)` is `N(c)` when `c ∣ b` and `0` otherwise (round 363's `sum_ψc_mul`).
- **The cube average.** The phase of the term of index `m` at `(z + 3q)/p³` is its phase at `z/p³` times `ĕ(σ(m)·(σ(3q)/σ(p³))/9)`. For `m = δ₃x`, the sum of this factor over `q mod p³` is `N(p)³` when `p³ ∣ x` and `0` otherwise, by the character sum. So the sum over `q` keeps the indices `m = p³m′` with `δ₃ ∣ m′`; for `δ₃ ∤ m′`, `d(p³m′) = 0`, since `p` is prime to `δ₃` (round 362's `isCoprime_δ3`). The term of index `p³m′` at `(z/p³, v/|p|³)` is `|p|⁻³d(p³m′)` times the term of index `m′` at `(z, v)`, and the constant term `c·(v/|p|³)^{2/3}` is `N(p)⁻¹c·v^{2/3}`, since `N(p) = |p|²` (round 297's `sq_norm_σO`). The sums over `q` and `m` are interchanged by the absolute convergence of round 436's `summable_thTerm`, and `m = p³m′` is reindexed by Mathlib's `Function.Injective.tsum_eq`.
- **The coefficients.** By round 436's `integral_ebr_thSer`, the integral over `3P` of `ĕ(−σ(δ₃x)z/9)·thSer(c, d)(z, v)` is `(9√3/2)·d(δ₃x)·v·K_{1/3}(4π|δ₃x|v/9)` for `x ≠ 0`. `K_{1/3}` is positive at positive arguments (round 431's `bkR_pos`, through round 374's `besselK_third_ofReal`), so two such series equal at every `z` at one height have the same coefficients at `δ₃x`, `x ≠ 0` (`thSer_coef_eq`). At height `1`, round 448's `thS_cube_eigen_coord` and the cube average give `thSer(N(p)⁻¹Res φ, d′) = thSer(N(p)⁻¹Res φ, N(p)⁻¹τ)` (round 371's `thSer_mul_const`) with `d′(m) = |p|⁻³τ(p³m)`. So `|p|⁻³τ(p³δ₃x) = N(p)⁻¹τ(δ₃x)`, that is `τ(p³δ₃x) = |p|·τ(δ₃x)`. At the other indices both sides are `0`: `τ` vanishes off the `δ₃x` with `x ≠ 0` (round 436's `tauTh_of_not`), and `δ₃ ∣ p³m` only if `δ₃ ∣ m`. For `ρ`, `τ(δ₃x) = ρ(x)/(9√3/2)` for `x ≠ 0` (round 436's `tauTh_δ3_mul`).

**Against the plan.** Round 448's next step listed:

- "the cube average of a theta-type series (round 361's `thSer`): for `d` supported on `δ₃ℤ[ω]` with `|d(m)| ≤ C|m|⁵` and `d(0) = 0`, `N(p)⁻³Σ_{q mod p³} thSer(c, d)((z + 3q)/p³, v/|p|³) = thSer(N(p)⁻¹c, d′)(z, v)` with `d′(m) = |p|⁻³d(p³m)`. For `m ∈ δ₃ℤ[ω]`, the sum over `q mod p³` of `ĕ(3mq/(9p³))` is `N(p)³` when `p³` divides `m/δ₃` and `0` otherwise;"
- "then round 436's `integral_ebr_thSer`, applied to both sides of this round's `thS_cube_eigen_coord`, gives `τ(p³m) = |p|·τ(m)` for every `m ∈ ℤ[ω]`, for θ's coefficients `τ` (round 436's `tauTh`)."

Both landed as planned. The cube average is proved for `p` primary, not necessarily prime; `d′` is supported on `δ₃ℤ[ω]` since `p` is prime to `δ₃`. The relation is also stated for round 431's `ρ` (`rhoM_cube`).

## Round 450: S5f-13, part 1 — θ's coefficients as residues (`src/KubotaCoefResidue.lean`)

**What it is.** The thirty-seventh step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the first part of S5f-13. Round 449's next step planned `ρ(m)` as a residue of round 430's Dirichlet series `D_m(s) = Σ_c S_m(c)N(c)^{−s}`, and then the sums `S_m(c)` at the powers of a primary prime `p`. This round proves the first, in the form in which the second will use it. For `m = δ₃x` let `Λ_x(s) = (2π/Γ(s))(2π|m|/9)^{s−1}·D_m(s)`, the factor of `J_ψ(s)` in round 430's identity. For `r > 0`, `Y > 0`, finitely many `x_i ≠ 0` and entire functions `a_i`:

- if `Σ_i a_i(s)·Λ_{x_i}(s) = 0` for `Re s > 2`, then `Σ_i a_i(4/3)·ρ(x_i) = 0` (`Eis.sum_rhoM_eq_zero`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaCoefResidue.lean`, 228 lines, 7 theorems and 3 definitions; each of its 7 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The strip** (`stripR`, a definition; `isOpen_stripR`, `isPreconnected_stripR` and `im_hhat_ne_zero_of_mem`).
- **Round 430's identity along the strip** (`dirL` and `pairF`, definitions; `pairF_eq`, `differentiableOn_pairF` and **`tendsto_pairF`**).
- **Relations among the Dirichlet series** (**`sum_rhoM_eq_zero`**).

**The proof.**

- **The strip.** `1 < Re s`, `0 < Im s < π/r` is open and convex, and `Im ĥ(s) > 0` on it (round 418's `im_hhat_pos`).
- **Round 430's identity along the strip.** With `ψ = 1_{[1, 2]}` (round 431's `ind12`), round 430's `inner_pmSer_uL_bessel` gives `⟨P_m(ψ), ũ_s⟩ = Λ_x(s)·J(s) + I_m·M_ψ(2 − s) − ⟨P_m(ψ), E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ Y + 3]v^s)⟩` for `Re s > 2` and `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0`, and `I_m = ∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9) dz = 0` for `x ≠ 0` (round 435's `integral_fundP3_ebr_eq_zero`). So `F_x(s) = ⟨P_m(ψ), ũ_s⟩ + ⟨P_m(ψ), E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ Y + 3]v^s)⟩` is `Λ_x(s)·J(s)` there (`pairF_eq`). `F_x` is complex-differentiable on the strip, since `s ↦ ũ_s` is (round 424's `differentiableAt_uL`) and the second pairing is entire (round 430's `differentiable_inner_bandL`). As `ε → 0⁺`, `iε·ũ_{4/3+iε} → θ` (round 425's `tendsto_uL_thetaL`), `⟨P_m(ψ), θ⟩ = ρ(x)·J(4/3)` (round 431's `rhoM`), and `iε` times the entire pairing tends to `0`; so `iε·F_x(4/3 + iε) → ρ(x)·J(4/3)` (`tendsto_pairF`).
- **Relations among the Dirichlet series.** Let `J_i` be `J` at `m = δ₃x_i` and `G = Σ_i a_i·F_{x_i}·Π_{j ≠ i}J_j`, complex-differentiable on the strip (round 431's `differentiable_jPsi`). At the points of the strip with `Re s > 2`, `G = (Σ_i a_i·Λ_{x_i})·Π_j J_j = 0`. So `G` vanishes near a point of the strip, hence on the whole strip (Mathlib's `AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq_zero`). At `4/3 + iε`, `iε·G` tends to `(Σ_i a_i(4/3)·ρ(x_i))·Π_j J_j(4/3)`, and `J_j(4/3) ≠ 0` (round 431's `jPsi_ind12_ne_zero`).

**Against the plan.** Round 449's next step listed:

- "`ρ(m)` as a residue of round 430's Dirichlet series `D_m(s) = Σ_c S_m(c)N(c)^{−s}`. On the strip `Re s > 1`, `0 < Im s < π/r`, `Im ĥ(s) > 0` (round 418's `im_hhat_pos`), so `s ↦ ⟨P_m(ψ), ũ_s⟩` is complex-differentiable there (round 424's `differentiableAt_uL`). Round 430's identity then continues `(2π/Γ(s))(2π|m|/9)^{s−1}D_m(s)J_ψ(s)` from `Re s > 2` to the strip, and by round 425's `tendsto_uL_thetaL`, `ρ(m)·J_ψ(4/3)` is the limit of `iε` times it at `s = 4/3 + iε` as `ε → 0⁺`;"
- "the sums `S_m(c)` at the powers of `p`, their twisted multiplicativity in `c`, and the relation they give between `D_{hp⁵}` and `D_{hp²}` for `Re s > 2`; its limit at `4/3`, with this round's relation, gives `τ(hp²) = 0`."

The first landed as a statement about linear relations (`sum_rhoM_eq_zero`). The plan's continuation is `F_x`, and its limit is `tendsto_pairF`, for `ψ = 1_{[1, 2]}`. The relations pass through the products with the `J`s, with no division by `J`. The second did not land.

**The next step.** S5f-13, part 2: the relations among the `D_m` at a primary prime `p ∤ h`, for `m = δ₃hp^e`. The plan, with `c = p^k c′` and `p ∤ c′`:

Then `S_m(p^k c′) = (9/p)₃^k·conj((c′/p)₃)^k·g_k(m)·S_m(c′)`, with `g_k(m) = Σ_{f mod p^k, p ∤ f} (f/p)₃^k·ĕ(mf/p^k)`, and `S_{mp^e}(c′) = conj((c′/p)₃)^e·S_m(c′)`; *(Round 451: landed, with the local sum `G_k(m)` taking `3f` in the phase, `Eis.cuspSm_mul_pow` and `Eis.cuspSm_twist`. ## Round 451: S5f-13, part 2 — the sums `S_m(c)` at a primary prime (`src/KubotaSmFactor.lean`)

**What it is.** The thirty-eighth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the second part of S5f-13. Round 450's next step planned the relations among round 430's Dirichlet series `D_m(s) = Σ_c S_m(c)N(c)^{−s}` at a primary prime `p`, beginning with the factorization of round 428's sums `S_m(c) = Σ_{d mod 3c} (c/d)₃·ĕ((m/9)(d/c))`, over the `d` with `(c, d)` a bottom row of `Γ_1(3)`. This round proves the factorization. For `m = δ₃x`, a primary prime `p`, `k ≥ 1`, and `c′ ≠ 0` with `3 ∣ c′` and `p ∤ c′`:

- `S_m(p^k c′) = (3/p)₃^k·(c′/p)₃^{2k}·G_k(m)·S_m(c′)`, with the local sum `G_k(m) = Σ_{f mod p^k, p ∤ f} (f/p)₃^k·ĕ((m/9)·(3f/p^k))` (`Eis.cuspSm_mul_pow`);
- `S_{δ₃xp^e}(c′) = (c′/p)₃^{2e}·S_{δ₃x}(c′)` for every `e`, for `p` primary and prime to `c′` (`Eis.cuspSm_twist`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaSmFactor.lean`, 350 lines, 10 theorems and 3 definitions; each of its 10 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The summand** (`smTerm`, a definition; `cuspSm_eq`, `smTerm_add` and `tsum_quot_eq_sum`).
- **The local sum** (`locTerm` and `locG`, definitions; `locTerm_add`).
- **The factorization** (`bRow_crt`, `cub_crt` and `smTerm_crt`; **`cuspSm_mul_pow`**).
- **The twist by `p^e`** (`smTerm_twist`; **`cuspSm_twist`**).

**The proof.**

- **The summand.** The summand of `S_m(c)` at `d` is periodic modulo `3c`: the bottom rows and the symbol are (round 389's `bRow_add_iff` and `cub_add_of_bRow`), and `ĕ((m/9)·3u) = 1` for `m ∈ δ₃ℤ[ω]` (round 428's `ebr_period`). A sum over the classes modulo `N` of a function periodic modulo `N` is its sum over any complete residue system (`tsum_quot_eq_sum`, as round 295's `gaussTr_eq_sum`).
- **The factorization.** `p^k` and `3c′` are coprime, so the `3c′f₁ + p^k f₂`, with `f₁` and `f₂` running over residues modulo `p^k` and `3c′`, form a complete residue system modulo `3p^k c′` (round 295's `crt_rep_bijective`). For such `d`: `d` is primary exactly when `f₂` is, since `p^k ≡ 1 (mod 3)`; `d` is prime to `p^k` exactly when `p ∤ f₁`, since `p ∤ 3c′`; and `d` is prime to `c′` exactly when `f₂` is (`bRow_crt`). The symbol is `(p^k c′/d)₃ = (p/d)₃^k·(c′/d)₃`. By cubic reciprocity (round 290's `cub_recip`), `(p/d)₃ = (d/p)₃ = (3c′f₁/p)₃`, and by periodicity (round 382's `cub_add_three_mul`), `(c′/d)₃ = (c′/p^k f₂)₃ = (c′/p)₃^k·(c′/f₂)₃` (`cub_crt`). The phase splits as `ĕ((m/9)(3f₁/p^k))·ĕ((m/9)(f₂/c′))`, so the summand is `(3/p)₃^k·(c′/p)₃^{2k}` times the local summand at `f₁` times the summand of `S_m(c′)` at `f₂` (`smTerm_crt`), and the double sum factors.
- **The twist.** With `πp^e + 3wc′ = 1`, `π` is primary and prime to `c′`, and the `πf` run over the classes modulo `3c′` with `f`. `(c′/π)₃·(c′/p)₃^e = (c′/πp^e)₃ = 1` (round 382's `cub_add_three_mul`), so `(c′/π)₃ = (c′/p)₃^{2e}`, as `(c′/p)₃³ = 1` (round 362's `cub_pow_three`). The phase at `πf` for `mp^e` is the phase at `f` for `m` times `ĕ((m/9)·3(−wf)) = 1` (`smTerm_twist`).

**Against the plan.** Round 450's next step listed:

- "the factorization of round 428's sums. The classes mod `3c` split by the Chinese remainder theorem into classes mod `p^k` and mod `3c′`, and cubic reciprocity gives `(p/d)₃ = (d/p)₃` for primary `d`. Then `S_m(p^k c′) = (9/p)₃^k·conj((c′/p)₃)^k·g_k(m)·S_m(c′)`, with `g_k(m) = Σ_{f mod p^k, p ∤ f} (f/p)₃^k·ĕ(mf/p^k)`, and `S_{mp^e}(c′) = conj((c′/p)₃)^e·S_m(c′)`;"
- "the table of `g_k(δ₃hp^e)`: for `k ≤ e`, `φ(p^k)` when `3 ∣ k` and `0` otherwise; for `k = e + 1`, `N(p)^e` times a Gauss sum modulo `p`; and `0` for `k ≥ e + 2`;"
- "hence, for `Re s > 2`, writing `D_h` for `D_{δ₃h}`: `D_{hp³} = (1 + N(p)^{3−3s})·D_h − (9/p)₃·N(p)^{−s}·g_1(δ₃h)·D_{hp}` and `D_{hp⁵} = (1 + N(p)^{3−3s})·D_{hp²}`;"
- "then this round's theorem and round 449's `rhoM_cube` give `ρ(hp²) = 0`, and `ρ(hp)` as a Gauss sum times `ρ(h)`."

The first landed with the local sum `G_k(m) = Σ_{f mod p^k, p ∤ f} (f/p)₃^k·ĕ((m/9)·(3f/p^k))`, the planned `g_k(m)` with `3f` in the phase. The factor is the planned one: substituting `3f` for `f` gives `(3/p)₃^k·G_k = (9/p)₃^k·g_k`, and `(c′/p)₃^{2k} = conj((c′/p)₃)^k` since `(c′/p)₃` is a cube root of unity. Neither identity is stated in Lean, since the next steps use `G_k`. The twist landed for `p` primary and prime to `c′`, as `(c′/p)₃^{2e}`. The second, the third and the fourth did not land.

See round 452.)*

## Round 452: S5f-13, part 3 — the local sums `G_k(δ₃hp^e)` (`src/KubotaLocTable.lean`)

**What it is.** The thirty-ninth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the third part of S5f-13. Round 451 factored round 428's sums `S_m(p^k c′)` at a primary prime `p` through the local sum `G_k(m) = Σ_{f mod p^k, p ∤ f} (f/p)₃^k·ĕ((m/9)·(3f/p^k))`, and its next step planned the table of `G_k(δ₃hp^e)` for a primary prime `p ∤ h`. This round proves it. For `k ≥ 1`, with `N = N(p)` and the Gauss sum `γ_j(h) = Σ_{f mod p} (f/p)₃^j·ĕ((δ₃h/9)·(3f/p))`:

- for `1 ≤ k ≤ e`, `G_k(δ₃hp^e) = N^{k−1}(N − 1)` when `3 ∣ k`, and `0` otherwise (`Eis.locG_low`);
- `G_{e+1}(δ₃hp^e) = N^e·γ_{e+1}(h)` (`Eis.locG_mid`), and `γ_j(h) = −1` for `3 ∣ j`, `j ≥ 1` and `p ∤ h` (`Eis.gaussP_three`), so that `G_{e+1}(δ₃hp^e) = −N^e` when `3 ∣ e + 1` (`Eis.locG_mid_three`);
- `G_k(δ₃hp^e) = 0` for `k ≥ e + 2` and `p ∤ h` (`Eis.locG_high`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaLocTable.lean`, 332 lines, 13 theorems and 2 definitions; each of its 13 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **Sums over `ℤ[ω]/N`** (`tsum_quot_affine'`, `tsum_quot_eq_zero_of_mul`, `tsum_quot_eq_zero_of_add` and `tsum_quot_dvd_fiber`).
- **The Gauss sums modulo `p`** (`gTerm` and `gaussP`, definitions; `ebr_gTerm`, `gTerm_add` and **`gaussP_three`**).
- **The table** (`locTerm_low`, **`locG_low`**, `locTerm_mid`, **`locG_mid`**, `locG_mid_three` and **`locG_high`**).

**The proof.**

- **Sums over `ℤ[ω]/N`.** For `u` prime to `N`, `q ↦ a + uq` permutes the classes modulo `N` (`tsum_quot_affine'`, round 445's `tsum_quot_affine` for any modulus). So if a dilation by a `g` prime to `N`, or a translation, multiplies a function periodic modulo `N` by `l`, its sum over the classes is `l` times itself, and vanishes for `l ≠ 1`. For `M ∣ N`, each class modulo `M` has `N(N)/N(M)` classes modulo `N` over it (round 414's `card_fiber_mul`), so `N(M)·Σ_{q mod N} F(q) = N(N)·Σ_{q mod M} F(q)` for `F` periodic modulo `M` (`tsum_quot_dvd_fiber`).
- **The Gauss sums modulo `p`.** The phase `ĕ((δ₃h/9)·(3f/p))` is the additive character `ψ_p(−fh)` (round 363's `ebr_shift`, with `δ₃² = −3`), and the summand is periodic modulo `p`. For `3 ∣ j`, `j ≥ 1`, `(f/p)₃^j` is `1` for `p ∤ f` (round 362's `cub_pow_three`) and `0` for `p ∣ f` (round 445's `cub_span_eq_zero`). So `γ_j(h)` is the sum of `ψ_p(−fh)` over all the classes minus its term at `f = 0`, which is `0 − 1`, since `p ∤ h` (round 363's `sum_ψc_mul`).
- **`k ≤ e`.** `p^e/p^k = p^{e−k}`, so the phase is `ĕ((δ₃y/9)·3f) = 1` with `y = hp^{e−k}` (round 428's `ebr_period`), and the summand is `(f/p)₃^k`, which is `0` for `p ∣ f`. It is periodic modulo `p`, so `G_k` is `N^{k−1}` times its sum over the classes modulo `p`. That sum is `N − 1` for `3 ∣ k`. For `3 ∤ k`, a `g` prime to `p` with `(g/p)₃ ≠ 1` (round 445's `exists_cub_ne_one`) has `(g/p)₃^k ≠ 1` (round 445's `σO_pow_ne_one`), and `f ↦ gf` multiplies the sum by it, so the sum is `0`.
- **`k = e + 1`.** `p^e/p^{e+1} = 1/p`, so the local summand is the summand of `γ_{e+1}(h)`, both `0` for `p ∣ f`. It is periodic modulo `p`, so `G_{e+1}` is `N^e` times its sum over the classes modulo `p`.
- **`k ≥ e + 2`.** Translating `f` by `p^{k−e−1}t` keeps the condition `p ∤ f` and the symbol (round 362's `cub_congr`), and multiplies the phase by `ĕ((δ₃hp^e/9)·(3p^{k−e−1}t/p^k)) = ψ_p(−th)`. Since `p ∤ h`, some `t` has `ψ_p(−th) ≠ 1` (round 363's `dvd_of_ψc_mul_eq_one`), and the sum vanishes.

**Against the plan.** Round 451's next step listed:

- "for `k ≤ e`, the phase is `1` (`ĕ(δ₃y/3) = 1` for `y ∈ ℤ[ω]`, as round 428's `ebr_period`), and `G_k` is the sum of `(f/p)₃^k` over the classes `f` modulo `p^k` prime to `p`: `N(p)^{k−1}(N(p) − 1)` when `3 ∣ k` and `0` otherwise;"
- "for `k = e + 1`, `G_k = N(p)^e·Σ_{f mod p, p ∤ f} (f/p)₃^k·ĕ(δ₃hf/(3p))`: `−N(p)^e` when `3 ∣ k`, and `N(p)^e` times a cubic Gauss sum otherwise;"
- "for `k ≥ e + 2`, `G_k = 0`: over the classes `f ≡ f₀ (mod p^{k−e−1})` the symbol is constant and the phase sums to `0`, since `p ∤ h`;"
- "then the relations among the `D_m` and the consequences for `ρ` planned in round 450."

The first landed as planned, for a primary prime `p` and every `h`. The second landed with the Gauss sum `γ_{e+1}(h)` taken over all the classes modulo `p`, the class of `0` contributing `0`: `G_{e+1} = N(p)^e·γ_{e+1}(h)` for every `h`, and `γ_{e+1}(h) = −1` when `3 ∣ e + 1` and `p ∤ h`. The third landed by a single translation `f ↦ f + p^{k−e−1}t` with `ψ_p(−th) ≠ 1`, which multiplies the sum by `ψ_p(−th)`, in place of summing the phase over the classes `f ≡ f₀ (mod p^{k−e−1})`. The fourth did not land.

**The next step.** S5f-13, part 4: the relations among the `D_m` at a primary prime `p ∤ h` planned in round 450, writing `D_h` for `D_{δ₃h}` as there. The plan, with `A_a(s) = Σ_{p ∤ c′} (c′/p)₃^a·S_{δ₃h}(c′)·N(c′)^{−s}`:

- for `Re s > 2`, the sum over `c` splits by the exponent of `p` in `c = p^k c′`, `p ∤ c′`, and round 451's `cuspSm_mul_pow` and `cuspSm_twist` give `D_{hp^e}(s) = A_{2e}(s) + Σ_{k ≥ 1} (3/p)₃^k·G_k(δ₃hp^e)·N(p)^{−ks}·A_{2k+2e}(s)`. The sums converge absolutely, since `|S_m(c)| ≤ N(3c) = 9N(c)` and `Σ_c N(c)^{1−Re s}` converges for `Re s > 2`; *(Round 453: landed as planned, `Eis.dirD_split` and `Eis.dirD_split_sum`, with `Eis.summable_dirD`. See round 453.)*
- the Gauss sums: `γ_{j+3}(h) = γ_j(h)` for `j ≥ 1`, and `γ_1(h)·γ_2(h) = N(p)` for `p ∤ h`; *(Round 453: landed as planned, `Eis.gaussP_add_three` and `Eis.gaussP_one_mul_two`. See round 453.)*
- with this round's table, `D_{hp⁵} = (1 + N(p)^{3−3s})·D_{hp²}` and `D_{hp³} = (1 + N(p)^{3−3s})·D_h − (3/p)₃·N(p)^{−s}·γ_1(h)·D_{hp}`. These are round 450's relations, since `γ_1(h) = G_1(δ₃h)` and `(3/p)₃·G_1(δ₃h) = (9/p)₃·g_1(δ₃h)` (round 451's conversion); *(Round 453: landed as planned, `Eis.dirD_p5` and `Eis.dirD_p3`. See round 453.)*
- then round 450's `sum_rhoM_eq_zero` and round 449's `rhoM_cube` give `ρ(hp²) = 0`, and `ρ(hp)` as a Gauss sum times `ρ(h)`.

## Round 453: S5f-13, part 4 — the relations among the `D_m` at a primary prime (`src/KubotaDirSplit.lean`)

**What it is.** The fortieth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the fourth part of S5f-13. Round 452's next step planned the relations among round 428's Dirichlet series `D_m(s) = Σ_c S_m(c)N(c)^{−s}` at a primary prime `p ∤ h`, writing `D_h` for `D_{δ₃h}` as in round 450. This round proves them. For `Re s > 2`, with `N = N(p)`, `X = N(p)^{−s}`, `t = (3/p)₃`, round 452's Gauss sums `γ_j(h)` and `A_a(s) = Σ_{p ∤ c} (c/p)₃^a·S_{δ₃h}(c)·N(c)^{−s}`:

- `D_m(s)` converges absolutely, since `|S_m(c)| ≤ 9N(c)` (`Eis.summable_dirD`, `Eis.norm_cuspSm_le`);
- `D_{hp^e}(s) = A_{2e}(s) + Σ_{k ≥ 1} t^k·G_k(δ₃hp^e)·X^k·A_{2k+2e}(s)` for every `h` and `e` (`Eis.dirD_split`), a finite sum over `k ≤ e + 1` for `p ∤ h` (`Eis.dirD_split_sum`);
- `γ_{j+3}(h) = γ_j(h)` for `j ≥ 1` (`Eis.gaussP_add_three`), and `γ_1(h)·γ_2(h) = N` for `p ∤ h` (`Eis.gaussP_one_mul_two`);
- `D_{hp⁵} = (1 + N³X³)·D_{hp²}` and `D_{hp³} = (1 + N³X³)·D_h − t·X·γ_1(h)·D_{hp}` for `p ∤ h` (`Eis.dirD_p5`, `Eis.dirD_p3`), round 450's relations with `N(p)^{3−3s}` written `N³X³`.

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaDirSplit.lean`, 364 lines, 15 theorems and 2 definitions; each of its 15 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The series** (`dirD`, a definition; `dirL_eq`, `cuspSm_of_not_dvd`, `norm_cuspSm_le` and **`summable_dirD`**).
- **The split by the exponent of `p`** (`dirA`, a definition; `normSq_cpow_mul`, `normSq_cpow_pow`, `dirA_add_three`, `dirA_mod_three`, **`dirD_split`** and `dirD_split_sum`).
- **The Gauss sums modulo `p`** (`gaussP_add_three` and **`gaussP_one_mul_two`**).
- **The relations** (`cub_three_pow_three`, **`dirD_p5`** and **`dirD_p3`**).

**The proof.**

So `|S_m(c)|/9 ≤ N(c)`, and round 441's `summable_mul_normSq_cpow` gives absolute convergence for `Re s > 2`.

So `D_{hp^e}` is the double sum over `k` and `c′` (Mathlib's `Summable.tsum_prod'`). For `3 ∣ c′`, round 451's `cuspSm_mul_pow` and `cuspSm_twist` give `S_{δ₃hp^e}(p^k c′) = t^k·(c′/p)₃^{2k+2e}·G_k(δ₃hp^e)·S_{δ₃h}(c′)` for `k ≥ 1`, and `(c′/p)₃^{2e}·S_{δ₃h}(c′)` for `k = 0`. For `3 ∤ c′` both sides are `0`, since `3` is prime to `p` (round 370's `isCoprime_three_of_primary`). `A_a` depends only on `a` modulo `3`, since `(c′/p)₃³ = 1` (round 362's `cub_pow_three`). For `p ∤ h` the terms with `k ≥ e + 2` vanish (round 452's `locG_high`).

With `t³ = 1`, `D_{hp²} = (1 − N²X³)·A_1` and `D_{hp⁵} = (1 + N²(N − 1)X³ − N⁵X⁶)·A_1 = (1 + N³X³)(1 − N²X³)·A_1`. In `(1 + N³X³)·D_h − tXγ_1·D_{hp}` the coefficient of `A_0` is `1 + N³X³ − Nγ_1γ_2X³ = 1 + N²(N − 1)X³`, and that of `A_2` is `tN³γ_1X⁴`.

## Round 454: S5f-13, part 5 — θ's coefficients at `hp²` and `hp` (`src/KubotaCoefPrime.lean`)

**What it is.** The forty-first step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the fifth part of S5f-13. Round 453's next step planned θ's coefficients at `hp²` and `hp` for a primary prime `p ∤ h`, from round 453's relations, round 450's residue principle and round 449's cube relation. This round proves them. With `N = N(p)`, `X = N(p)^{−s}`, `t = (3/p)₃`, round 452's Gauss sums `γ_j(h)` and round 431's `ρ` (`rhoM`):

- **The coefficients at `4/3`** (`coef_four_thirds_cube` and `coef_four_thirds_sq`).

With round 453's relations, for `Re s > 2`: `Λ_{hp⁵} = (|p|³)^{s−1}(1 + N³X³)·Λ_{hp²}` (`dirL_p5`) and `Λ_{hp³} = (|p|³)^{s−1}(1 + N³X³)·Λ_h − t·γ_1(h)·X·(|p|²)^{s−1}·Λ_{hp}` (`dirL_p3`), from `(|p|⁵)^{s−1} = (|p|³)^{s−1}(|p|²)^{s−1}` and `(|p|³)^{s−1} = (|p|²)^{s−1}·|p|^{s−1}`.
- **The coefficients at `4/3`.** The coefficients are entire in `s`, since `|p| > 0` and `N > 0` (Mathlib's `Differentiable.const_cpow`). At `s = 4/3`, with `N = |p|²` (round 294's `normSq_σO`): `(|p|³)^{1/3}(1 + N³·(N^{−4/3})³) = |p|(1 + |p|⁻²) = |p| + |p|⁻¹`, and `N^{−4/3}·(|p|²)^{1/3} = |p|^{−8/3 + 2/3} = |p|⁻²`, through the real powers (Mathlib's `Complex.ofReal_cpow`).
- **θ's coefficients.** Round 450's `sum_rhoM_eq_zero` turns the relations into `ρ(hp⁵) = (|p| + |p|⁻¹)·ρ(hp²)` and `ρ(hp³) = (|p| + |p|⁻¹)·ρ(h) − t·γ_1(h)·|p|⁻²·ρ(hp)`. Round 449's `rhoM_cube` gives `ρ(hp⁵) = |p|·ρ(hp²)` and `ρ(hp³) = |p|·ρ(h)`. So `|p|⁻¹·ρ(hp²) = 0`, and `|p|⁻¹·(|p|⁻¹·t·γ_1(h)·ρ(hp) − ρ(h)) = 0`. With `t³ = 1` and round 453's `γ_1(h)·γ_2(h) = N = |p|²`, `ρ(hp) = t²·γ_2(h)·ρ(h)/|p|`.

## Round 455: S5f-13, part 6 — θ's coefficients at the squarefree-times-cube indices prime to `6` (`src/KubotaCoefSqfree.lean`)

**What it is.** The forty-second step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the sixth part of S5f-13. Round 454's next step planned θ's coefficients at the squarefree indices prime to `6`, up to `ρ(1)`, in the form of round 361's `KubotaTheta`. This round proves them, and the cube factor. For primary `n` and `b` with `(n)` squarefree and `N(nb)` prime to `6`, with round 305's normalized Gauss sum `γ₂(n)` (`gamI 2 (span {n})`) and round 281's sextic symbol:

- `ρ(n) = (δ₃/n)₆²·conj γ₂(n)·ρ(1)` (`Eis.rhoM_sqfree`), and `ρ(nb³) = |b|·ρ(n)` (`Eis.rhoM_mul_cube`);
- so `τ(δ₃nb³) = τ(δ₃)·N(b)^{1/2}·(δ₃/n)₆²·conj γ₂(n)` (`Eis.tauTh_sqfree_cube`), round 361's coefficient formula at `δ₃nb³` with `C = τ(δ₃)`.

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaCoefSqfree.lean`, 280 lines, 11 theorems; each of its 11 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The Gauss sums modulo `p` in the display's normalization** (`gaussP_twist`, `conj_σO_cub`, **`gaussP_one_two`** and `cub_three_sq_eq_sym6`).
- **θ's coefficients at squarefree indices** (**`rhoM_mul_prime_sym`**, `gamI_one`, `conj_sym6_pow_four`, `rhoM_prod_πP` and **`rhoM_sqfree`**).
- **The cube factor and the display's coefficients** (**`rhoM_mul_cube`** and **`tauTh_sqfree_cube`**).

**The proof.**

- **The twist.** For a primary prime `p ∤ h`, with `ah + bp = 1`, `f ↦ af` permutes the classes modulo `p` (round 452's `tsum_quot_affine'`). It multiplies the symbol `(f/p)₃^j` by `(a/p)₃^j`, and `(a/p)₃ = (h/p)₃²` since `(a/p)₃(h/p)₃ = (ah/p)₃ = 1`. It leaves the phase `ψ_p(−afh) = ψ_p(−f + pfb)` at `ψ_p(−f)` (round 294's `ψc_add_mul`). So `γ_j(h) = (h/p)₃^{2j}·γ_j(1)` (`gaussP_twist`).
- **The normalization.** `γ₂(𝔭) = Σ_{r mod p} (r/𝔭)₆²·ψ_p(r)/|p|`, with the primary generator `p` of `𝔭` (round 290's `pgen_eq`). Here `(r/𝔭)₆² = (r/p)₃` (round 362's `sym6_sq_eq_cub`), `conj (r/p)₃ = (r/p)₃²` since `(r/p)₃` is `0` or a cube root of unity (`conj_σO_cub`), and `conj ψ_p(r) = ψ_p(−r)` (round 371's `conj_ψc`). So `γ_2(1) = |p|·conj γ₂(𝔭)` (`gaussP_one_two`). Also `3 = −δ₃²`, so `(3/p)₃² = (δ₃/p)₃⁴ = (δ₃/p)₃ = (δ₃/p)₆²` (`cub_three_sq_eq_sym6`). With round 454's `rhoM_mul_prime_eq`, `ρ(hp) = (δ₃/p)₆²·(h/p)₆²·conj γ₂(𝔭)·ρ(h)` for `N(p)` prime to `6` (`rhoM_mul_prime_sym`).
- **The squarefree indices.** By induction on a finite set `A` of primes prime to `6` (round 305's `Pr`, round 307's `idl`): `ρ(∏_{P∈A} π_P) = (δ₃/𝔫)₆²·conj γ₂(𝔫)·ρ(1)` with `𝔫 = ∏_{P∈A} P`. For `A = ∅` both sides are `ρ(1)`, since `γ₂(𝒪) = 1` (`gamI_one`). Adding `P ∉ A`, `π_P ∤ ∏_{Q∈A} π_Q` (round 305's `isCoprime_πP`). `rhoM_mul_prime_sym` multiplies `ρ` by `(δ₃/P)₆²·(n_A/P)₆²·conj γ₂(P)`, and round 305's `gamI_two_mul`, `γ₂(𝔞𝔟) = γ₂(𝔞)·γ₂(𝔟)·(a/𝔟)₆⁴`, multiplies the right side by the same factor. Here `conj((n_A/P)₆⁴) = (n_A/P)₆²`, from `conj w = w⁵` (round 319's `chiS_conj_eq_pow_five`) and `w⁷ = w` (round 364's `sym6_pow_seven`), which is `conj_sym6_pow_four`. For primary `n` with `(n)` squarefree of norm prime to `6`, `n = ∏_{P ∈ primeSet (n)} π_P` (round 305's `pgen_eq_prod`), which gives `rhoM_sqfree`.
- **The cube factor.** By induction on `N(b)`: a primary `b` of norm `1` is `1` (round 290's `primary_unique`). Otherwise a prime factor `P` of `(b)` is prime to `6` (round 288's `six_not_mem_of_factor`), and `b = π_P·b′` with `b′` primary (round 414's `primary_mul_iff`) of smaller norm. Round 449's `rhoM_cube` gives `ρ(n·b³) = |π_P|·ρ(n·b′³)` (`rhoM_mul_cube`). Then round 436's `tauTh_δ3_mul`, `τ(δ₃x) = ρ(x)/(9√3/2)`, and `N(b)^{1/2} = |b|` (round 297's `sq_norm_σO`) give `tauTh_sqfree_cube`.

**Against the plan.** Round 454's next step listed:

- "the twist of the Gauss sum: `γ_j(h) = (h/p)₃^{2j}·γ_j(1)`, by `f ↦ fh′` with `hh′ ≡ 1 (mod p)`;"
- "the display's normalization: `γ_2(1) = |p|·conj(gamI 2 (p))`, since `(r/p)₆² = (r/p)₃` (round 292's `chi6_sq`) and `conj ψ_p(r) = ψ_p(−r)`; and `t² = (δ₃/p)₃ = (δ₃/p)₆²`, since `3 = −δ₃²`. So `ρ(hp) = (δ₃/p)₆²·(h/p)₃·conj(gamI 2 (p))·ρ(h)`;"
- "the twisted multiplicativity `conj gamI 2 (ab) = (a/b)₃·conj gamI 2 (a)·conj gamI 2 (b)` for coprime primary `a` and `b` (the Chinese remainder theorem and cubic reciprocity), and induction over the prime factors: `ρ(n) = (δ₃/n)₆²·conj(gamI 2 (n))·ρ(1)` for squarefree primary `n` prime to `6`. With round 449's `rhoM_cube`, `ρ(nb³) = |b|·ρ(n)` for primary `b` prime to `6`."

**What it is.** The forty-sixth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the fourth part of S5f-14. From `3s + ty = 1` (round 370's `isCoprime_three_of_primary`), `v = ty + 3sλ` is primary, `v ≡ λ (mod y)`, and `v` is prime to `c`. ## Round 460: S5f-15, part 1 — the translation law at the cusps `γ_±` (`src/KubotaCuspTrans.lean`)

**What it is.** The forty-seventh step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the first part of S5f-15. Round 459's next step planned θ's expansions at `γ_± = (1, 0; ω^{±1}, 1)`, starting from how θ∘γ_t transforms under the translations by `3ℤ[ω]`. This round proves that law and what it gives for the modes, for `t = ω` and `t = ω²` and θ's Fourier series `thS` (round 436):

- `θ(γ_t(w + 3x)) = χ_t(x)·θ(γ_t w)` for every `x ∈ ℤ[ω]`, with `χ_t(x) = (t/(1 − 3tx))₃` (`Eis.kub_cuspPar`, `Eis.thS_lowT_add`);
- `χ_t` is a character, trivial on `λℤ[ω]`, with `χ_t(1) = σ(t)` (`Eis.chiT_add`, `Eis.chiT_lam_mul`, `Eis.chiT_one`);
- there is `m₀ = ±1` with `ĕ(m₀·3x/9) = χ_t(x)` for every `x`, so `θ(γ_t(z, v))·ĕ(−m₀z/9)` is periodic under `3ℤ[ω]` (`Eis.exists_cuspClass`, `Eis.thS_lowT_twist_add`);
- `u∘γ_t` is automorphic with the conjugated character `κ_t(γ) = κ(γ_t·γ·γ_t⁻¹)` when `u` is automorphic with Kubota's character (`Eis.isAut_comp_lowT`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaCuspTrans.lean`, 474 lines, 38 theorems and 4 definitions; each of its 38 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The conjugated translations** (`lowT` and `cuspPar`, definitions; `lowT_coe`, `lowT_ω`, `lowT_ω_sq`, `cuspPar_coe`, `cuspPar_mem`, `lowT_mul_slT`, `primary_one_sub` and **`kub_cuspPar`**). *(Round 516: `lowT_ω` and `lowT_ω_sq`, which no proof used, are removed. `lowT`'s docstring records that `γ_ω` and `γ_{ω²}` are `gamPlus` and `gamMinus` by definition.)*
- **The character** (`chiT`, a definition; `chiT_eq_kub`, `cuspPar_add`, **`chiT_add`**, `chiT_zero`, `norm_chiT`, `chiT_mul_conj`, `chiT_neg`, `chiT_nsmul` and `chiT_zsmul_eq_one`).
- **The translation law** (**`thS_lowT_add`**).
- **The character on `λℤ[ω]` and at `1`** (`cub_omega_of_norm`, `absNorm_crd_eq`, `crd_eq`, `cub_omega_sq`, `chiT_lam`, **`chiT_lam_mul`** and **`chiT_one`**).
- **The class of the modes** (`ebr_third`, `ebr_neg_third`, `varpi_eq_ebr`, `ebr_one_eq_one`, `ebr_lam_mul`, `ebr_add_period`, `ebr_nsmul`, **`exists_cuspClass`** and **`thS_lowT_twist_add`**).
- **The conjugated character** (`kubT`, a definition; `lowT_conj_mem`, `isUChar_kubT`, `kubT_slT` and **`isAut_comp_lowT`**).

**The proof.**

- **Kubota's character at `γ_t·T_{3x}·γ_t⁻¹`.** The product is `(1 − 3tx, 3x; −3t²x, 1 + 3tx)`, congruent to the identity modulo `3` (round 382's `mem_Gam3`). Its lower left entry is `t·(a − 1)` with `a = 1 − 3tx` primary, so by round 361's `kub` and round 369's `kub_of_ne` its value is `(t(a − 1)/a)₃ = (t/a)₃·(−1/a)₃ = (t/a)₃` (round 362's `cub_mul_left`, `cub_congr`, `cub_neg` and `cub_one`). For `tx = 0` both sides are `1` (round 362's `cub_one_right`).
- **The character.** `x ↦ γ_t·T_{3x}·γ_t⁻¹` is a homomorphism, so `χ_t` is a character with values on the unit circle (round 382's `kub_mul_Gam3`, round 387's `norm_kub`).
- **The translation law.** `γ_t·T_{3x} = (γ_t·T_{3x}·γ_t⁻¹)·γ_t`, and round 437's `isAut_thS` gives the factor `χ_t(x)`.
- **The character on `λℤ[ω]` and at `1`.** Round 362's `cub_omega`, `(ω/b)₃ = ω^{(N(b)−1)/3}` for primary `b`, with `(ω²/b)₃ = (ω/b)₃²`, applies at `1 − 3ωλ = 4 + 6ω`, `1 − 3ω²λ = −5 − 3ω` and `1 − 3λ = 4 − 3ω`, of norms `28`, `19` and `37` (round 308's `absNorm_crd`). It gives `χ_t(λ) = χ_t(ωλ) = 1` for `t = ω` and `t = ω²`. Every `y ∈ ℤ[ω]` is `a + bω`, so `λy = aλ + b·ωλ` and `χ_t(λy) = 1`. At `1 − 3ω` and `1 − 3ω²`, both of norm `13`, it gives `χ_t(1) = σ(t)`.
- **The class of the modes.** `ĕ(1/3) = −1/2 − (√3/2)i` and `ĕ(−1/3) = −1/2 + (√3/2)i` (Mathlib's `Real.cos_pi_div_three` and `Real.sin_pi_div_three`). `σ(ω)` has real part `−1/2` and imaginary part of square `3/4` (round 294's `varpi_re_im`), so it is one of the two. Both `x ↦ ĕ(m₀·3x/9)` and `χ_t` are characters trivial on `λℤ[ω]` (round 428's `ebr_period`), and every `x = a + bω` is `(a + b) + λb`, so the two agree once they agree at `1`. There the phases are `ĕ(±1/3)`, with `ĕ(1/3)² = ĕ(−1/3)` and `ĕ(−1/3)² = ĕ(1/3)`, so `m₀ = 1` or `m₀ = −1` matches `χ_t(1) = σ(t)`, according to which of the two `σ(ω)` is. The twisted function `θ(γ_t(z, v))·ĕ(−m₀z/9)` then takes the factor `χ_t(x)·conj χ_t(x) = 1` under `z ↦ z + 3x` (round 363's `ebr_add` and `conj_ebr`).
- **The conjugated character.** `Γ_1(3)` is normal (round 382's `gam3_normal`), so `γ_t·γ·γ_t⁻¹ ∈ Γ_1(3)` for `γ ∈ Γ_1(3)`, and `κ_t` is a unitary character (round 421's `IsUChar`). Then `u(γ_t·γw) = u((γ_tγγ_t⁻¹)·γ_tw) = κ_t(γ)·u(γ_tw)`.

**Against the plan.** Round 459's next step listed:

- "the translation law: for `t = ω^{±1}` and `x ∈ ℤ[ω]`, `γ_t·(1, 3x; 0, 1)·γ_t⁻¹ = (1 − 3tx, 3x; −3t²x, 1 + 3tx)` lies in `Γ_1(3)`, so round 437's `atG_thS` gives, for `x ≠ 0`, `θ(γ_t(w + 3x)) = (−3t²x/(1 − 3tx))₃·θ(γ_t w)`, a character of `x` (the release's `ramifiedSourceFunction_omega_translate` gives `ω^{A+B}` at `x = A + Bω` for `t = ω`, read for the route and not used);"
- "the modes: a mode `ĕ(mz/9)` of `θ∘γ_t` transforms by `ĕ(mx/3)`, which depends only on `m` modulo `λ`, so the modes lie in one class modulo `λ`, a nonzero class when the character is not trivial; then `λ ∤ m` and the constant term is `0`. The profiles would be `v·K_{1/3}(4π|m|v/9)`, as at `∞` (rounds 431–437);"
- "the coefficients: `θ∘γ_t` is a residue of `E_s∘γ_t`, whose bottom rows `(c, d)·γ_t = (c + dt, d)` have moduli prime to `λ`, so its Fourier coefficients would be Dirichlet series of Gauss sums with moduli prime to `3`. So would those of `E_s∘S` at the cusp `0` (round 440 computed its constant term, a Dirichlet series over primary moduli), where `θ∘S = θ` (round 443). The release writes its series at `γ_t` as six such series (its `ramifiedCuspGaussSeries_eq_six`, read for the route and not used). With round 450's residue principle at both cusps, the coefficients at `γ_t` would be finite combinations of `τ`, and their support and size condition would follow from this round's `thetaSupp_tauTh` where the six indices keep the form `uλ^k·n·b³`;"
- "then `KubotaTheta` (S5f-16), with the constant `K` the largest of the three."

**The proof.**

- **The series with the character `κ_t`.** For `g ∈ Γ_1(3)`, `γ_{(c, d)}·g = T_{3x}·γ_{(c, d)g}` (round 429's `gamRow_mul_eq`), so `κ_t(γ_{(c, d)}) = χ_t(x)·κ_t(γ_{(c, d)g})·conj κ_t(g)` (round 460's `isUChar_kubT` and `kubT_slT`, round 421's `IsUChar.map_inv`). The translation by `3x` multiplies `ĕ(m·z/9)` by `ĕ(m·3x/9) = χ_t(x)`, which cancels `conj χ_t(x)`. So the term of `(c, d)` at `g·w` is `κ_t(g)` times the term of `(c, d)g` at `w`, and `(c, d) ↦ (c, d)g` permutes the bottom rows (round 429's `rowGEquiv`).
- **The series at the cusp.** `κ_t(γ_t⁻¹·g·γ_t) = κ(g)`, and `γ_t⁻¹·g·γ_t ∈ Γ_1(3)` (round 382's `conj_mem_Gam3`), so `Q_t` is automorphic with Kubota's character. `|κ_t| = 1`, so the terms of `P^{(t)}_m(ψ)` have the absolute values of the terms of round 429's `P_m(ψ)`, those of `E(ψ)` (round 429's `tsum_enorm_pmTerm_eq`). At the cusp `g·∞` the terms of `Q_t` are those of `E(|ψ|)` at the cusp `γ_t⁻¹g·∞`, bounded by round 429's `tsum_enorm_psTerm_slAct_le`, and round 423's `lintegral_puLe_top_mul_lt_top` gives `Q_t ∈ L²(ν)`.
- **The change of variables by `γ_t`.** As round 442's `integral_conj_sS_inv_mul` for `S`: for `u` automorphic with `κ_t` and `w` automorphic with Kubota's character, `conj u(p)·w(γ_t p)` is invariant under `Γ_1(3)`, and the partition of unity moved by `γ_t` gives the same integral (round 439's `integral_muR_slAct` and `integral_isPU_eq`, round 442's `isPU_rhoG_comp`). So `∫conj u(γ_t⁻¹p)·w(p) dν = ∫conj u(p)·w(γ_t p) dν`, with integrability from `L²(ν)` (Mathlib's `MemLp.integrable_mul`).
- **Unfolding.** `w∘γ_t` is automorphic with `κ_t` (round 460's `isAut_comp_lowT`), so `conj(term of P^{(t)}_m(ψ))·w(γ_t p)` is `conj(ψ(v(γp))·ĕ(m·z(γp)/9))·w(γ_tγp)` at `γ = γ_{(c, d)}`, and the integrand `conj(ψ(v)·ĕ(mz/9))·w(γ_t(z, v))` is periodic under `3ℤ[ω]` for `m` in the class. Round 426's `integral_unfold_family`, `integral_rhoH_eq` and `muR_rhoT3` unfold it to `3P × (0, ∞)`, as in round 429's `integral_conj_pmSer_mul`.
- **The pairing with θ.** θ in `L²(ν)` is the class of θ's Fourier series, extended by `0` off upper half-space (round 425's `thetaL_ae_eq_thetaF`, round 448's `ae_uhs_thetaF_eq_thS`), which is automorphic (round 437's `isAut_thS`). On `3P × [α, β]` the function `(z, v) ↦ θ(γ_t(z, v))` is bounded: the set lies in the compact `{|z| ≤ 6} × [α, β]` (round 430's `norm_le_six_of_mem_fundP3`), where it is continuous (round 436's `continuousOn_thS`, round 437's `continuousOn_slAct`). Round 430's `lintegral_rhoT3_pm_ne_top` then gives the integrability that the unfolding uses.

It is square-integrable as round 429's `P_m(ψ)` is, since `|κ_t| = 1`;"

## Round 462: S5f-15, part 3 — the Fourier coefficients of the Eisenstein series at the cusps `γ_t` and `0` (`src/KubotaCuspCoef.lean`)

**What it is.** The forty-ninth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the third part of S5f-15. Round 461's next step planned the Fourier coefficients of `E_s∘γ_t` and the pairing of round 461's `Q_t` with `ũ_s`. This round proves both, and the same at the cusp `0`, for `t` a unit and `m ≠ 0` with `ĕ(m·3x/9) = χ_t(x)` for every `x` (round 461's `Eis.CuspClass`):

- `E(γ_t·p, s) = Σ_{(c, d)} cuspF(c − dt, d)·(v/Q_p(c, d))^s`, and the weight is periodic in `d` modulo `3c` up to `ĕ(−(m/9)·3u)` (`Eis.eis1_slAct_lowT`, `Eis.wtCuspT_add`);
- for `Re s > 2` and `v > 0`, `∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)E(γ_t·(z, v), s) dz = (2π/Γ(s))(2π|m|/9)^{s−1}·v·K_{s−1}(4π|m|v/9)·Σ_c S^t_m(c)N(c)^{−s}` with `S^t_m(c) = Σ_{d mod 3c} cuspF(c − dt, d)·ĕ((m/9)(d/c))`, and there is no term `v^s` (`Eis.integral_ebr_eis1_lowT`);
- at the cusp `0`, for `m = δ₃x ≠ 0`, the same with `S⁰_m(c) = Σ_{d mod 3c} cuspF(−d, c)·ĕ((m/9)(d/c))` (`Eis.integral_ebr_eis1_sS`);
- for `ψ` bounded and vanishing outside `[α, β]` with `0 < α ≤ β`, `Re s > 2` and `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0`, `⟨Q_t(ψ), ũ_s⟩ = (2π/Γ(s))(2π|m|/9)^{s−1}·(Σ_c S^t_m(c)N(c)^{−s})·J_ψ(s) − ⟨Q_t(ψ), E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)⟩` with `H = Y + β + 1/α` (`Eis.inner_pmSerC_uL`), and the same at the cusp `0` for `P_m(ψ)∘S⁻¹` (`Eis.inner_pmSerS_uL`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaCuspCoef.lean`, 764 lines, 31 theorems and 8 definitions; each of its 31 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **Twisted tiling** (`wtSum`, a definition; `hasSum_integral_ebr_wt`, `tsum_lintegral_wt_ne_top` and **`integral_ebr_wtSeries`**).
- **The cusp `γ_t`** (`wtCuspT`, `rowTEquiv` and `cuspSmT`, definitions; `rowMul_lowT`, `cuspF_rowMul`, `eisTerm_slAct_lowT`, **`eis1_slAct_lowT`**, **`wtCuspT_add`**, `norm_cuspF_le`, `not_bRow_lowT`, `wtCuspT_zero_fst`, `lowT_row_ne_zero`, `conj_chiT_of_class` and **`integral_ebr_eis1_lowT`**).
- **The cusp `0`** (`wtCusp0`, `rowSEquiv` and `cuspSm0`, definitions; `eis1_slAct_sS'`, `cuspF_add_fst`, `wtCusp0_add`, `wtCusp0_zero_fst` and **`integral_ebr_eis1_sS`**).
- **The band at `g·p`** (`height_slAct_le`, **`eisHigh_slAct_eq_band`** and **`eisLow_slAct_eq_band`**).
- **The pairings** (`pmSerS`, a definition; `enorm_comp_lowT`, `setLIntegral_lowT_lt_top`, `lintegral_rhoT3_pmC_ne_top`, `setLIntegral_conj_ebr_mul`, **`inner_pmSerC_uL`**, `isAut_pmSerS`, `memLp_pmSerS`, `inner_toLp_pmSerS` and **`inner_pmSerS_uL`**). *(Round 516: `isAut_pmSerS`, which no proof used, is removed.)*

**The proof.**

- **Twisted tiling.** For `c ≠ 0` and a weight `F` with `|F| ≤ 1` and `F(d + 3cu) = F(d)·ĕ(−ξ·3u)`, the term of `d + 3cu` integrated over `3P` is the term of `d` integrated over `3P` moved by `3u` (round 389's `uhsDen_res`), so the sum over `d` in a class modulo `3c` is one integral over `ℂ` (round 389's `integral_tile3`), computed by round 428's `integral_ebr_height_cpow`. The sum over the classes gives `W(c)·|c|^{−2s}·(2π/Γ(s))(2π|ξ|)^{s−1}·v·K_{s−1}(4π|ξ|v)`, as in round 428's `hasSum_integral_ebr_eisTerm_c`. For `|w| ≤ 1`, `w(0, d) = 0` and `Re s > 2` the double series of the integrals of the absolute values converges (round 389's `tsum_lintegral_height_c`, round 388's `tsum_norm_σO_rpow_le`), so the integral and the sum may be exchanged.
- **The cusp `γ_t`.** `(c, d)·γ_t = (c + dt, d)`, so the term of `(c, d)` at `γ_t·p` is `cuspF(c, d)` times the height of the row `(c + dt, d)` at `p` (round 387's `height_rowMul`), and `(c, d) ↦ (c + dt, d)` is a bijection. With round 460's `cuspPar`, `(c − dt, d)·γ_tT_{3u}γ_t⁻¹ = (c − (d + 3cu)t, d + 3cu)`; that matrix lies in `Γ_1(3)` and its `κ` is `χ_t(u)` (round 460's `chiT_eq_kub`), so round 387's `cub_rowMul` gives `w_t(c, d + 3cu) = w_t(c, d)·conj χ_t(u)`, and `conj χ_t(u) = ĕ(−(m/9)·3u)` for `m` in the class (round 363's `conj_ebr`). A row `(−dt, d)` is not a bottom row for `t` a unit: `3 ∣ dt` would give `3 ∣ d`, against `d ≡ 1 (mod 3)` (round 290's `not_three_dvd_one`).
- **The cusp `0`.** Round 440's `eis1_slAct_sS` gives the terms at `S·p` on the rows `(d, −c)`. With `(c, d) ↦ (−d, c)` the weight of the row `(c, d)` is `cuspF(−d, c)`, periodic in `d` modulo `3c` (round 440's `bRow_add_fst_iff`, round 362's `cub_congr`), and for `m = δ₃x` the twist `ĕ(−(m/9)·3u)` is `1` (round 428's `ebr_period`). No bottom row has `d = 0`.
- **The band.** For `g` sending no bottom row to `(0, *)`, every height at `g·p` is at most `1/v` (round 387's `height_rowMul`, round 427's `height_le_inv`), so the terms of `h_s` at `g·p` with `v ≥ α` have heights at most `Y + β + 1/α` once they reach `Y`, as in round 442's `eisHigh_sS_eq_band`. For `γ_t`, `c + dt ≠ 0` on the bottom rows.
- **The pairings.** For `u` automorphic and in `L²(ν)`, `|u∘γ_t|` is invariant under `Γ_1(3)` (round 460's `lowT_conj_mem`, round 442's `slAct_conj`), so `u∘γ_t` is integrable on `3P × [α, β]` (round 432's `lintegral_boxZ_lt_top`, round 442's `lintegral_enorm_comp_lt_top`). Round 461's `inner_toLp_pmSerC`, with `ũ_s = E_s − h_s` for `Re s > 2` and `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0` (round 424's `uL_eq_eisLow`), the band, round 432's Fubini step `integral_fundP3_conj_mul_of_int` and the coefficient give the Bessel form with round 430's `J_ψ`. At the cusp `0`, `⟨P_m(ψ)∘S⁻¹, w⟩ = ⟨P_m(ψ), w∘S⟩` (round 442's `integral_conj_sS_inv_mul`) unfolds by round 429's `integral_conj_pmSer_mul`, and round 442's `eisLow_sS_eq_band` and `setLIntegral_sS_lt_top` do the rest.

- "the coefficient of `ĕ(mz/9)` at height `v`, for `m` in the class: `∫_{3P} E_s(γ_t(z, v))·ĕ(−mz/9) dz = Σ_{c′} S^{(t)}_m(c′)·N(c′)^{−s}·(planar transform)`, with `S^{(t)}_m(c′) = Σ_{d mod 3c′} (c′/d)₃·ĕ(m·d/(9c′))` over the `d` with `(c′ − dt, d)` a bottom row, through round 428's `integral_ebr_height_cpow` and the sum over `d` in its classes modulo `3c′`, as round 428's `hasSum_integral_ebr_eisTerm_c` at `∞` and round 440's at the cusp `0`. ## Round 463: S5f-15, part 4 — the Kubota sums at the cusps `γ_t` and `0` (`src/KubotaCuspIdent.lean`)

**What it is.** The fiftieth step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the fourth part of S5f-15. Round 462's next step planned the relation between round 462's Kubota sums at the cusps `γ_t` and `0`, and θ's coefficients at `γ_t`. This round proves the relation, and the relation between the two pairings with `ũ_s` that it gives, for `tt′ = 1`, `m` in the class of the cusp `γ_t` (round 461's `Eis.CuspClass`), `λ = ω − 1` and `m′ = δ₃ω²tλ²m = −tλ³m`:

- `S^t_m(c) = 0` unless `c ≡ t (mod 3)` (`Eis.cuspSmT_eq_zero`);
- `S^t_m(ta) = ĕ(mt′/9)·S⁰_{m′}(a)` for every `a` (`Eis.cuspSmT_mul`), so `Σ_c S^t_m(c)N(c)^{−s} = ĕ(mt′/9)·Σ_a S⁰_{m′}(a)N(a)^{−s}` for every `s` (`Eis.tsum_cuspSmT_eq`);
- for `ψ` measurable and bounded, vanishing outside `[α, β]` with `0 < α ≤ β`, `ψ̃(v) = ψ(3√3·v)`, `Re s > 2` and `Im ĥ(s) ≠ 0`, the pairing of `Q_t(ψ)` with `ũ_s` plus its band term is `ĕ(mt′/9)·(3√3)^{−s}` times the same for `P_{m′}(ψ̃)∘S⁻¹` (`Eis.inner_pmSerC_uL_eq`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaCuspIdent.lean`, 493 lines, 22 theorems and 4 definitions; each of its 22 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **Sums of a periodic function over the classes** (`eq_of_mk_eq_of_periodic`, **`tsum_repQ_eq_of_span`** and **`tsum_repQ_affine`**).
- **The summands** (`kubTermT` and `kubTerm0`, definitions; `cuspSmT_eq`, `cuspSm0_eq`, **`kubTermT_periodic`**, **`kubTerm0_periodic`**, **`cuspSmT_eq_zero`** and **`cuspSm0_eq_zero`**).
- **The termwise identity** (`kubPoly`, a definition; `δ3_eq_lam_neg`, `kubota_sum_poly` and **`kubTermT_affine`**).
- **The sums and the Dirichlet series** (**`cuspSmT_mul_primary`**, **`cuspSmT_mul`** and **`tsum_cuspSmT_eq`**).
- **The pairings** (`sclPsi`, a definition; **`norm_σO_cuspIdx`**, **`jPsi_comp_mul`**, `sqrt27_pos`, `measurable_sclPsi`, `norm_sclPsi_le`, `sclPsi_eq_zero` and **`inner_pmSerC_uL_eq`**).

**The proof.**

- **Sums over the classes.** A function periodic modulo `c` takes one value on a class, so its sum over the classes does not depend on the representatives. For `(c) = (c′)` Mathlib's `Ideal.quotEquivOfEq` identifies the two quotients. For `α` prime to `c`, `r ↦ αr + β` is a bijection of the classes: the class of `α` is a unit, and multiplication by a unit followed by a translation is a permutation of the quotient ring.
- **The summands.** The summand of `S^t_m(c)` at `d` is `cuspF(c − dt, d)·ĕ((m/9)(d/c))`. Moving `d` by `3cy` multiplies the weight by `conj χ_t(y)` (round 462's `wtCuspT_add`), which is `ĕ(−(m/9)·3y)` for `m` in the class (round 462's `conj_chiT_of_class`), and the exponential by `ĕ((m/9)·3y)`. At the cusp `0`, `ĕ(m·3y/9) = 1` for `m = δ₃x` (round 428's `ebr_period`). A nonzero summand of `S^t_m(c)` needs `3 ∣ c − dt` and `d ≡ 1 (mod 3)`, so `3 ∣ c − t`; one of `S⁰_m(c)` needs `c` primary.
- **The termwise identity.** For `a` primary, round 370's `isCoprime_three_of_primary` gives `3u + va = 1`. Put `d = (va − 3uλ³t²)b + va`. Then `d − 1 = b − 3(u + ub + uλ³t²b)` and `d + λ³t²b = a·v(b + 1 + λ³t²b)`, so `d` is primary exactly when `3 ∣ b`, and `d` is prime to `a` exactly when `b` is (round 459's `isCoprime_lam_of_primary`); the two summands vanish together. Where they do not, `((ta − dt)/d)₃ = (t/d)₃(a/d)₃ = (t/d)₃(d/a)₃` (round 362's `cub_congr` and `cub_mul_left`, round 290's `cub_recip`) and `(d/a)₃ = (−λ³t²b/a)₃ = (t/a)₃²(b/a)₃` (round 362's `cub_neg` and `cub_pow_three`, round 369's `cub_pow_left`). The class gives `(t/d)₃ = χ_t(−t′d₁)` with `d = 1 + 3d₁` and `(t/a)₃ = χ_t(−t′a₁)` with `a = 1 + 3a₁` as values of `ĕ` (round 460's `chiT`). The exponents then agree up to `m·3λy/9` with `y = −ω·w` for an explicit `w`, by a polynomial identity in `𝒪` modulo `3u + va = 1`, `tt′ = 1` and `ω² + ω + 1 = 0` (`kubota_sum_poly`, its coefficients found by a Gröbner reduction in sympy and checked by Lean's `linear_combination`), and `ĕ(m·3λy/9) = 1` (round 460's `ebr_lam_mul`).
- **The sums.** `(3ta) = (3a)` since `t` is a unit, and `va − 3uλ³t²` is prime to `3a`: to `3` since it is `va ≡ 1`, and to `a` since it is `−λ³t² + a·v(1 + λ³t²)`. So the sum over the classes modulo `3ta` is the sum over the classes modulo `3a`, then the sum at `(va − 3uλ³t²)b + va`, and the termwise identity gives `ĕ(mt′/9)·S⁰_{m′}(a)`. For `a` not primary both sides vanish. The Dirichlet series follow by `a ↦ ta`, with `N(ta) = N(a)` (round 361's `normSq_σO_unit`).
- **The pairings.** `N(δ₃) = 3`, `N(λ) = 3` and `N(ω) = N(t) = 1` (round 361's `normSq_σO_lam` and `normSq_σO_unit`), so `|m′| = 3√3·|m|`. Mathlib's `integral_comp_mul_left_Ioi` rescales round 430's `J_ψ`. With round 462's `inner_pmSerC_uL` and `inner_pmSerS_uL` and the identity of the Dirichlet series, `(2π|m′|/9)^{s−1} = (3√3)^{s−1}(2π|m|/9)^{s−1}` (Mathlib's `Complex.mul_cpow_ofReal_nonneg`) and `(3√3)^{−s}(3√3)^{s−1}·3√3 = 1` give the relation.

**Against the plan.** Round 462's next step listed:

- "`S^t_m(c) = 0` unless `c ≡ t (mod 3)`: a nonzero term needs `(c − dt, d)` to be a bottom row, so `3 ∣ c − dt` and `d ≡ 1 (mod 3)`;"
- "for `a` primary and `m` in the class, `S^t_m(ta) = ĕ(m/(9t))·S⁰_{m′}(a)` with `m′ = −tλ³m`. The classes `d ≡ 1 (mod 3)` modulo `3ta` and `b ≡ 0 (mod 3)` modulo `3a` correspond through `λ³t²b ≡ −d (mod a)`; then `(ta/d)₃ = (t/d)₃(d/a)₃` (round 290's `cub_recip`), `(−b/a)₃ = (t/a)₃(d/a)₃`, and the class gives `(t/d)₃·ĕ(m(d − 1)/(9t)) = 1` for `d ≡ 1 (mod 3)`. A numerical check of the identity in this session (moduli of norm at most 49, both cusps, both embeddings, 146 nonzero cases) found no exception; it is a check, not a proof;"
- "then `Σ_c S^t_m(c)N(c)^{−s} = ĕ(m/(9t))·Σ_a S⁰_{m′}(a)N(a)^{−s}`, and with `|m′| = 3^{3/2}|m|` and `ψ̃(v) = ψ(3^{3/2}v)`, the pairing of `Q_t(ψ)` with `ũ_s` plus its band term is `ĕ(m/(9t))·3^{−3s/2}` times the same for `P_{m′}(ψ̃)∘S⁻¹`, for `Re s > 2`;"
- "the identity theorem and the limit as in round 431, with `⟨P_{m′}(ψ̃)∘S⁻¹, θ⟩ = ⟨P_{m′}(ψ̃), θ⟩` (round 443's `thetaF_sS_ae`), give `⟨Q_t(ψ), θ⟩ = ĕ(m/(9t))·3^{−1/2}·ρ(m′)·J_ψ(4/3)` with round 431's `ρ`; then θ∘γ_t's Fourier series and the support and size condition for its coefficients (S5f-15), and `KubotaTheta` (S5f-16)."

The first landed (`Eis.cuspSmT_eq_zero`). The second landed (`Eis.cuspSmT_mul_primary` and `Eis.cuspSmT_mul`), with `m′` written `δ₃ω²tλ²m` and `ĕ(m/(9t))` written `ĕ(mt′/9)`, through an affine change of class `b ↦ (va − 3uλ³t²)b + va` modulo `3a` in place of the correspondence of the classes through `λ³t²b ≡ −d (mod a)`. The third landed (`Eis.tsum_cuspSmT_eq` and `Eis.inner_pmSerC_uL_eq`), with `3^{3/2}` written `3√3`. The fourth did not land.

**The next step.** S5f-15, part 5: θ's coefficients at `γ_t`. The plan:

## Round 464: S5f-15, part 5 — θ's coefficients at the cusps `γ_t` (`src/KubotaCuspTheta.lean`)

**What it is.** The fifty-first step toward the owner's "Finalise the theta derivation", and the fifth part of S5f-15. Round 463's next step planned θ's Fourier coefficients at the cusp `γ_t` from round 463's relation between the pairings of `Q_t(ψ)` and `P_{m′}(ψ̃)∘S⁻¹` with `ũ_s`. This round proves them, for `tt′ = 1`, `m ≠ 0` in the class of the cusp `γ_t` (round 461's `Eis.CuspClass`), `λ = ω − 1`, `m′ = δ₃ω²tλ²m`, `ψ̃(v) = ψ(3√3·v)` and `ρ` round 431's `Eis.rhoM`. In the pointwise formulas `θ` is round 436's Fourier series `Eis.thS`, which round 437 showed equal to θ almost everywhere:

- for `ψ` measurable and bounded, vanishing outside `[α, β]` with `0 < α ≤ β`, `⟨Q_t(ψ), θ⟩ = ĕ(mt′/9)·(3√3)^{−4/3}·⟨P_{m′}(ψ̃)∘S⁻¹, θ⟩` (`Eis.inner_pmSerC_thetaL_eq`), and `⟨Q_t(ψ), θ⟩ = ρ_t(m)·J_ψ(4/3)` with `ρ_t(m) = ĕ(mt′/9)·3^{−1/2}·ρ(m′)` (`Eis.inner_pmSerC_thetaL_rho`);
- `∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)·θ(γ_t(z, v)) dz = ρ_t(m)·v·K_{1/3}(4π|m|v/9)` for every `v > 0` (`Eis.coef_lowT`).

**What is proved** (`src/KubotaCuspTheta.lean`, 550 lines, 15 theorems and 2 definitions; each of its 15 axiom lines is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **The function `A_y`** (`aBand`, a definition; **`differentiableOn_aBand`** and **`tendsto_aBand`**).
- **θ at the cusp `0` in `L²(ν)`** (**`inner_comp_sS_inv_thetaL`**).
- **The residue relation** (**`residue_eq_of_eq_cpow`**).
- **θ's pairing at `γ_t`** (`rhoCusp`, a definition; **`aBand_pmSerC_eq`**, **`inner_pmSerC_thetaL_eq`**, **`inner_pmSerS_thetaL`**, `cuspIdx_ne_zero`, `sqrt27_cpow` and **`inner_pmSerC_thetaL_rho`**).
- **The coefficients** (**`inner_pmSerC_thetaL_unfold`**, `integrableOn_ebr_thSU_lowT`, **`coef_lowT_ae`**, **`continuousOn_coef_lowT`** and **`coef_lowT`**).

**The proof.**

- **The function `A_y`.** For `y ∈ L²(ν)`, `A_y(s) = ⟨y, ũ_s⟩ + ⟨y, E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)⟩` with `R = 2cosh r − 2`. It is holomorphic on round 427's `U`, where `Im ĥ(s) > 0` (round 418's `im_hhat_pos`), by round 424's `differentiableAt_inner_uL` and round 430's `differentiable_inner_bandL`. As `ε → 0⁺`, `iε·⟨y, ũ_{4/3+iε}⟩ → ⟨y, θ⟩` (round 425's `tendsto_uL_thetaL`) and `iε·⟨y, E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^{4/3+iε})⟩ → 0`, the band term being entire in `s`.
- **θ at the cusp `0`.** For `u` measurable and automorphic with Kubota's character, with `u` and `u∘S⁻¹` in `L²(ν)`, round 442's `integral_conj_sS_inv_mul` moves `S⁻¹` from `u` to θ's representative `θ̃`, and round 443's `thetaF_sS_ae` removes it: `θ̃∘S = θ̃` almost everywhere for `ν` (Mathlib's `withDensity_absolutelyContinuous`).
- **The residue relation.** `F(s) = A₁(s) − ζ·c^{−s}·A₂(s)` is holomorphic on `U` and vanishes on the open set `U ∩ {Re s > 2}`, so it vanishes on `U`, which is convex (round 427's `convex_domU`), by Mathlib's `AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq`. The curve `4/3 + iε` lies in `U` for `0 < ε < π/r`, so there `iε·A₁ = ζ·c^{−s}·iε·A₂`, and the uniqueness of limits gives `a₁ = ζ·c^{−4/3}·a₂`, as in round 431's `inner_pmSer_thetaL_cross`.
- **θ's pairing at `γ_t`.** Round 463's `inner_pmSerC_uL_eq` is the hypothesis of the residue relation for `y = Q_t(ψ)` and `y = P_{m′}(ψ̃)∘S⁻¹`, with `ζ = ĕ(mt′/9)` and `c = 3√3`. The cusp-`0` step and round 431's `inner_pmSer_thetaL` give `⟨P_{m′}(ψ̃)∘S⁻¹, θ⟩ = ρ(m′)·J_{ψ̃}(4/3)` with `J_{ψ̃}` taken at `4π|m′|/9 = 3√3·4π|m|/9` (round 463's `norm_σO_cuspIdx`), which is `3√3·J_ψ(4/3)` (round 463's `jPsi_comp_mul`). Finally `(3√3)^{−4/3}·3√3 = 3^{−1/2}`, since `3√3 = √3³` (Mathlib's `Complex.ofReal_cpow`, `Real.rpow_add_one` and `Real.rpow_natCast_mul`).
- **The coefficients.** Round 461's `inner_pmSerC_thetaL` writes `⟨Q_t(ψ), θ⟩` as an integral over `3P × (0, ∞)` against `dz dv/v³`, and round 430's `integral_fundP3_conj_mul`, with the bound of round 461's `exists_bound_thS_lowT`, splits it as `∫_0^∞ v^{−3}·conj ψ(v)·a(v) dv` with `a(v) = ∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)·θ(γ_t(z, v)) dz`. For each `n`, on `[1/(n + 1), n + 1]`, the profiles `ψ = 1_S` turn `⟨Q_t(ψ), θ⟩ = ρ_t(m)·J_ψ(4/3)` into `∫_S (v^{−3}a(v) − ρ_t(m)v^{−2}K_{1/3}(4π|m|v/9)) dv = 0` for every measurable `S` in the interval, so the integrand vanishes almost everywhere there (Mathlib's `Integrable.ae_eq_zero_of_forall_setIntegral_eq_zero`), and so on `(0, ∞)` (round 432's `Ioi_zero_eq_iUnion_Icc`), as in round 432's `coef_thetaF_ae`. `a` is continuous on `(0, ∞)` by dominated convergence (Mathlib's `continuousOn_of_dominated`, with round 461's bound and round 436's `continuousOn_thS` composed with round 437's `continuousOn_slAct`), and so is the right side (round 373's `continuousAt_besselK`), so the two agree at every `v > 0` (Mathlib's `Measure.eqOn_open_of_ae_eq`).

**Against the plan.** Round 463's next step listed:

- "the identity theorem on round 427's `domU` and the limit `iε·A(4/3 + iε)` as in round 431, for `A(s) = ⟨y, ũ_s⟩ + ⟨y, E(1[Y ≤ v ≤ H]v^s)⟩` at `y = Q_t(ψ)` and at `y = P_{m′}(ψ̃)∘S⁻¹`, with this round's relation: `⟨Q_t(ψ), θ⟩ = ĕ(mt′/9)·(3√3)^{−4/3}·⟨P_{m′}(ψ̃)∘S⁻¹, θ⟩`;"
- "`⟨P_{m′}(ψ̃)∘S⁻¹, θ⟩ = ⟨P_{m′}(ψ̃), θ⟩` (round 442's `integral_conj_sS_inv_mul`, round 443's `thetaF_sS_ae`) `= ρ(m′)·J_{ψ̃}(4/3)` (round 431's `inner_pmSer_thetaL`), and `J_{ψ̃}(4/3) = 3√3·J_ψ(4/3)` (this round's `jPsi_comp_mul`), so `⟨Q_t(ψ), θ⟩ = ĕ(mt′/9)·3^{−1/2}·ρ(m′)·J_ψ(4/3)`;"
- "round 461's `inner_pmSerC_thetaL` and round 432's Fubini step give `∫_{3P} ĕ(−mz/9)θ(γ_t(z, v)) dz = ĕ(mt′/9)·3^{−1/2}·ρ(m′)·v·K_{1/3}(4π|m|v/9)` for almost every `v > 0`, as round 432's `coef_thetaF_ae`, and for every `v > 0` by continuity (round 436's `continuousOn_thS`);"
- "then θ∘γ_t's Fourier series, whose coefficients off the class vanish by round 460's translation law, the support and size condition for its coefficients from round 459's `thetaSupp_tauTh` (S5f-15), and `KubotaTheta` (S5f-16)."

The first landed (`Eis.residue_eq_of_eq_cpow` and `Eis.inner_pmSerC_thetaL_eq`), with the identity theorem and the limit in a lemma of their own. The second landed (`Eis.inner_comp_sS_inv_thetaL`, `Eis.inner_pmSerS_thetaL` and `Eis.inner_pmSerC_thetaL_rho`). Round 361's `atG` at `gamPlus.map σO` and `gamMinus.map σO` is θ at `γ_ω` and `γ_{ω²}` by definition. The two constants are replaced by their maximum (`ThetaSupp.mono`).

## Round 469: the exponent of the error in the prime number theorem, `limsup log|ψ(x) − x| / log x = Θ` with `½ ≤ Θ ≤ 11/12` (`external/pnt/PsiExponent.lean`)

**What it is.** The owner asked, after round 468, to follow the doors listed then ("Follow as suggested"): the exact exponent of the error in the prime number theorem, then a Lindelöf bound on `Re s > 11/12`, and register entries for three research directions. This round is the first. Round 338 recorded that for `Θ = sup Re ρ < 1` both halves of 1as(viii)'s statement are in the stack, and that "They are not joined as one theorem." Round 466 gives `Θ ≤ 11/12`. This round joins them:

- `PsiExponent.Theta`, the supremum of the real parts of the nontrivial zeros of `ζ`, with `½ ≤ Θ ≤ 11/12`;
- `ψ(x) − x = O(x^{Θ+ε})` and `ψ(x) − x = Ω±(x^{Θ−ε})`;
- `limsup_{x→∞} log|ψ(x) − x| / log x = Θ`.

**What is proved** (`external/pnt/PsiExponent.lean`, 162 lines, 15 theorems and 3 definitions; each of its 6 axiom lines in `build.sh`'s final check is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **`Theta`** (a definition): `sSup {σ | ∃ ρ, IsNontrivialZero ρ ∧ ρ.re = σ}`, with `Pilot1bt.IsNontrivialZero ρ` the predicate `riemannZeta ρ = 0 ∧ ¬∃ n : ℕ, ρ = −2(n + 1)` of `src/T1bt.lean`.
- **`Theta_le`** (`Θ ≤ 11/12`), **`half_le_Theta`** (`½ ≤ Θ`) and **`zeta_ne_zero_of_Theta_lt`** (`Θ < Re s → ζ(s) ≠ 0`).
- **`psi_isBigO_Theta`**: `(ψ - id) =O[atTop] fun x ↦ x ^ (Θ + ε)` for every `ε > 0`.
- **`psi_omega_Theta`**: for `0 < ε < Θ` and all `c` and `X`, some `x > X` has `c·x^{Θ−ε} < ψ(x) − x` and some `x > X` has `ψ(x) − x < −c·x^{Θ−ε}`.
- **`limsup_expo`**: `limsup expo atTop = Θ`, where `expo x = log|ψ(x) − x| / log x` with Mathlib's `Real.log` (so `expo x = 0` where `ψ(x) = x`).

**The proof.**

- **The range.** Every nontrivial zero has `Re ρ ≤ 11/12` by round 466's `Eis.ne_zero_of_re_gt_eleven_twelfths`, so `Θ ≤ 11/12`. Round 220's `PsiOmega.exists_zero_re_ge_half` gives a zero with `Re ρ ≥ ½`; it is nontrivial because the trivial zeros have negative real part (`re_trivial_neg`), so `½ ≤ Θ`.
- **The half-plane at `Θ`.** A zero with `Re s > Θ` would be trivial, with `Re s < 0 < Θ`, or nontrivial, with `Re s ≤ Θ`.
- **The two halves.** `psi_isBigO_of_zeroFree` (round 337, with the exponent `θ + ε` since round 338) at `Θ < 1`; round 220's `PsiOmega.psi_omega` at a nontrivial zero with `Re ρ > Θ − ε`, which the supremum supplies (`exists_zero_re_gt`).
- **The limit superior.** The upper half gives `expo x ≤ Θ + 2ε` eventually (`eventually_expo_le`), and the lower half with `c = 1` gives `Θ − ε ≤ expo x` frequently (`frequently_le_expo`). Mathlib's `limsup_le_of_le` and `le_limsup_of_frequently_le` close it, with the boundedness conditions from the same two facts.

**The paper.** 1as(viii) states: "limsup of ln|ψ(x)−x|/ln x is the abscissa Θ = sup Re ρ ∈ [½, 1], and Θ = ½ ⟺ RH (equivalently Σ μ(n)n^(−s) has abscissa Θ)." The first clause is now a theorem of the stack, with the range `[½, 11/12]` inside the paper's `[½, 1]`. The equivalent form for `Σ μ(n)n^{−s}` is not proved here. The route planned for it uses bounds on `1/ζ` to the right of `Re s = Θ`, round 470's target. The paper is not edited; a change to it needs CLAUDE.md's hostile review. *(Round 470: the bounds on `1/ζ` are proved, `HalfPlaneLindelof.zeta_bound_Theta`; the form for `Σ μ(n)n^{−s}` is not. See round 470.)* *(Round 472: the form for `Σ μ(n)n^{−s}` is proved: its abscissa of convergence is `Θ` (`MertensExponent.moebiusAbscissa_eq_Theta`), and `RH ⟺ Θ = ½` (`rh_iff_Theta_eq_half`). See round 472.)*

**Register entries** (STRUCTURAL-REVIEW §6, "Doors after the half-plane"), as CLAUDE.md's Check 9(b) asks for new targets: half-planes for Dirichlet L-functions by twisting the family; mean values of cubic Gauss sums from the pole at `s = 4/3`; a certified zero of `dh` with `Re s > 11/12`. ## Round 470: a Lindelöf bound in a zero-free half-plane, `ζ(s)^{±1} = O(|t|^ε)` on `Re s ≥ σ₀ > 11/12` (`external/pnt/HalfPlaneLindelof.lean`)

**What it is.** The second of the doors the owner asked for after round 468 ("Follow as suggested"), which round 469's next step planned. STRUCTURAL-REVIEW §6 records for Lindelöf: "Nothing: no subconvexity bound of any strength is in the three layers". *(Round 517: `ZetaCritBound (5/24 + ε)` and `ConvexityBound` are proved, `external/pnt/Subconvexity.lean`.)* This round proves:

- from a zero-free half-plane `Re s > θ` with `0 ≤ θ < 1`: for every `σ₀ > θ` and every `ε > 0` there are `T` and `C` with `|ζ(σ + it)| ≤ C|t|^ε` and `1/|ζ(σ + it)| ≤ C|t|^ε` whenever `σ ≥ σ₀` and `|t| ≥ T` (`HalfPlaneLindelof.zeta_bound_of_zeroFree`);
- the same with no hypothesis for every `σ₀ > 11/12` (`zeta_bound_eleven_twelfths`), and for every `σ₀ > Θ`, round 469's supremum of the real parts of the zeros (`zeta_bound_Theta`).

**What is proved** (`external/pnt/HalfPlaneLindelof.lean`, 484 lines, 10 theorems; each of its 6 axiom lines in `build.sh`'s final check is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

- **`norm_le_interp`**, with `norm_exp_weight`: let `F` be complex-differentiable on the closed rectangle `[a, b] × [t₀ − W, t₀ + W]`, with `0 ≤ a < b`, `W > 0`, `|F| ≤ A` on the rectangle, `|F| ≤ B` on its right edge, `0 < B ≤ A` and `log(A/B) ≤ W²`. Then `|F(σ + it₀)| ≤ e^{b² − σ²}A^{(b−σ)/(b−a)}B^{(σ−a)/(b−a)}` for `σ ∈ [a, b]`.
- **`hasDerivAt_log_norm`**: for `f : ℝ → ℂ` with `f(u) ≠ 0`, `u ↦ log|f(u)|` has derivative `Re(f′(u)/f(u))` at `u`.
- **`norm_zeta_le_three_halves`** and **`inv_norm_zeta_le_three_halves`**: `|ζ(s)| ≤ ζ(3/2)` and `1/|ζ(s)| ≤ ζ(3/2)` on `Re s ≥ 3/2`.
- **`rpow_le_mul_self`**: for `κ < 1` and `δ > 0`, `y^κ ≤ δy` for all large `y`.
- **`logDeriv_le_interp`**: suppose `ζ ≠ 0` on `Re s > θ`, `θ < a`, `0 ≤ a < 3/2`, `C₁ > 0`, `|ζ′/ζ(σ + it)| ≤ C₁ log|t|` for `|t| > 3` and `σ ≥ a`, and `|ζ′/ζ| ≤ B` on `Re s ≥ 3/2` with `B ≥ 1`. For `|t| > 6` with `B + (3/2)C₁|t| ≤ (|t|/2)²` and `u ∈ [a, 3/2]`: `|ζ′/ζ(u + it)| ≤ e^{9/4 − u²}A^{(3/2−u)/(3/2−a)}B^{(u−a)/(3/2−a)}`, `A = max(B, C₁ log(3|t|/2))`.
- **`zeta_bound_of_zeroFree`**, **`zeta_bound_eleven_twelfths`** and **`zeta_bound_Theta`**: as above.

**The proof.**

- **The interpolation.** Let `H(z) = F(z)·exp((z − it₀)² − (b − z)c₁ − (z − a)c₂)`, `c₁ = log A/(b − a)` and `c₂ = log B/(b − a)`. On the top and bottom edges `|H| ≤ e^{b²}`, since `(Im z − t₀)² = W² ≥ log(A/B)`; on the left edge `|H| ≤ A·e^{a² − log A} ≤ e^{b²}`; on the right edge `|H| ≤ B·e^{b² − log B} = e^{b²}`. Mathlib's maximum modulus principle on the bounded rectangle (`Complex.norm_le_of_forall_mem_frontier_norm_le`) gives `|H(σ + it₀)| ≤ e^{b²}`, which is the bound.
- **`ζ′/ζ`.** Take `b = 3/2`, `t₀ = t` and `W = |t|/2`. On the rectangle `|t|/2 ≤ |Im z| ≤ 3|t|/2`, so it does not contain `1`, `ζ ≠ 0` there (`Re z ≥ a > θ`), `ζ′/ζ` is complex-differentiable there (PNT+'s `LogDerivZetaHoloOn`) and at most `C₁ log(3|t|/2) ≤ A`; on the right edge it is at most `B`. Finally `log(A/B) ≤ A ≤ B + (3/2)C₁|t| ≤ (|t|/2)²`.
- **`ζ`.** Let `σ₁ = min(σ₀, 5/4)` and `a = (θ + σ₁)/2`. Round 337's `HalfPlanePNT.logDeriv_le_of_zeroFree` at `θ < a < 3/2` gives `C₁`, and PNT+'s `LogDerivZetaBdd_of_Re_ge_three_halves` gives `B`. For `σ ≥ 3/2` both bounds are `ζ(3/2)`. For `σ₀ ≤ σ < 3/2` and `u ∈ [σ, 3/2]`, the exponent `(3/2 − u)/(3/2 − a)` is at most `κ = (3/2 − σ₁)/(3/2 − a) < 1`, so `|ζ′/ζ(u + it)| ≤ e^{9/4}A^κB`. The derivative of `u ↦ log|ζ(u + it)|` is `Re ζ′/ζ(u + it)` (`hasDerivAt_log_norm`), and Mathlib's mean value inequality (`Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasDerivWithin_le`) gives `|log|ζ(σ + it)|| ≤ log ζ(3/2) + (3/2)e^{9/4}B·A^κ`. Since `A ≤ B + C₁ log(3|t|/2)` and `y^κ ≤ δy` for large `y` (`rpow_le_mul_self`, from Mathlib's `tendsto_rpow_neg_atTop`), this is at most `M + ε log|t|` for `|t| ≥ T`. Exponentiating gives both bounds.
- **The instances.** `θ = 11/12` from round 466's `Eis.ne_zero_of_re_gt_eleven_twelfths`; `θ = Θ` from round 469's `PsiExponent.zeta_ne_zero_of_Theta_lt`, `half_le_Theta` and `Theta_le`.

**Against the plan.** Round 469's next step listed:

- "interpolate round 337's `HalfPlanePNT.logDeriv_le_of_zeroFree`, `|ζ′/ζ(σ + it)| ≤ C log|t|` on `σ ≥ θ′`, against PNT+'s bound on `ζ′/ζ` on `Re s ≥ 3/2` (`LogDerivZetaBdd_of_Re_ge_three_halves`), by the maximum modulus principle on rectangles `[θ′, 3/2] × [t − W, t + W]` with a Gaussian factor, away from `s = 1`: `|ζ′/ζ(σ + it)| ≤ C(log|t|)^{1−λ(σ)}` with `λ(σ) > 0`;"
- "bound `log|ζ(σ + it)| − log|ζ(3/2 + it)|` by the mean value inequality, the derivative of `u ↦ log|ζ(u + it)|` being `Re ζ′/ζ(u + it)`: `log|ζ(s)| = O((log|t|)^{1−λ})`, so `ζ(s)^{±1} = O(|t|^ε)`."

Both landed by the route listed, with `θ′ = a = (θ + min(σ₀, 5/4))/2` and `W = |t|/2`. The weight is the Gaussian factor times `exp(−(3/2 − z)c₁ − (z − a)c₂)`, and `1 − λ(σ)` is `(3/2 − σ)/(3/2 − a)`.

**The paper.** 1as(viii) states: "Θ = ½ ⟺ RH (equivalently Σ μ(n)n^(−s) has abscissa Θ)." The bounds on `1/ζ` to the right of `Re s = Θ` that round 469 named for the parenthetical are now in the stack (`zeta_bound_Theta`). The step from them to the parenthetical, through `M(x) = Σ_{n≤x} μ(n) = O(x^{Θ+ε})`, is not: the stack's theorems on `M(x)` are round 221's `zeta_ne_zero_of_mertens`, which runs from a bound on `M(x)` to a zero-free half-plane, and `mertens_omega`. The paper is not edited. *(Round 472: the step is proved, `MertensExponent.mertens_isBigO_Theta` and `moebiusAbscissa_eq_Theta`. See round 472.)*

## Round 471: horizon scan of 2026-10-14, and an audit of the character in the half-plane chain (no new Lean)

**What it is.** After round 470 the owner asked to "Proceed with all 4" of the steps proposed then:

1. a horizon scan and an audit of where the chain fixes the trivial character (this round);
2. the two near doors of rounds 469–470;
3. the half-plane for every Dirichlet character, by twisting;
4. the downstream consequences: the prime number theorem in progressions, and the class-number deduction. *(Rounds 478–480: the prime number theorem in progressions modulo the `q` whose characters are all real, and Littlewood's bounds for `L(1, χ)` at the real characters; the class-number deduction is not done. See round 480.)*

**The horizon scan.** CLAUDE.md's "Looking in the right places" asks for this scan at the start of each RH-strand round series: `github.com/openai/math`, arXiv math.NT and the Lean community, "for results that fill a socket on the open-targets register or contradict a barrier claim". Each item below was read at its source, a page or file fetched here. None of the mathematics was checked here.

- **The release.** Since `fd4aeeb` (round 286) there are two commits, both of 12 October: `2710f99`, "Lock pull request conversations when opened", and its merge `1581d4c`. The only file changed is `.github/workflows/lock-prs.yml` (20 lines added). `history.md` has one dated section, "October 7, 2026", as in round 286. Family 003 is unchanged.
- **arXiv:2610.12234**, Baiying Liu: v1 of 8 October, "Slightly improved zero-free half-planes for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis", and v2 of 12 October, "Improved zero-free half-planes for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis". It moves the release's `7/8` to about `0.874957` "via varying $b$, $\ell$, and $\kappa$", and states: "We also prove its optimality within the explicitly specified exponent comparison system." Its abstract says the result is formalized in Lean.
- **S. Kintali, "A Short Proof of the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis"**, a PDF dated 7 October 2026 on the author's homepage, not on arXiv. Its abstract, with spacing and ligatures normalized from the PDF's text layer: "We prove that the Riemann zeta function, all Dirichlet L-functions, and all finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3) are zero-free in Re s > 47/48." It adapts the release's `7/8` framework, and works with one zero supremum over all primitive finite-order Hecke characters of `ℚ(√−3)`: "Poisson summation introduces finite-order twists over F, so we work with one zero supremum for this family." The inputs it names are the companion's cubic theta formulas, a quadratic Hecke large sieve and a Hecke zero-density estimate.
- **D. Cureton and J. Thorner, "A quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions"** (hexagonmath.org 2610.00200; v1 12 October, v2 14 October). For every number field `K`, `ζ_K(s)` has no zero in `Re s > 31/32`. The same holds for every finite-order Hecke L-function over `K`, "wherever it is holomorphic". "These results were proved and formalized in Lean using AxiomProver." It names as the hardest part "the formalization of the work of Kazhdan and Patterson on metaplectic forms in order to accommodate all number fields." The page read gives no link to the formalization.
- **arXiv:2610.18491**, C. Frei, E. Sofos and M. Widmer, "Some applications of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis to class groups and small generators of number fields" (13 October). It proves an effective Chebotarev theorem conditional on the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions, and: "Drawing on recent breakthroughs of OpenAI and Cureton--Thorner, we make unconditional the Ellenberg--Venkatesh bounds on $\ell$-torsion in class groups of number fields". This bears on step 4.
- **The Lean community.** Nothing found. The search found no Zulip thread, and round 286 records that the Zulip archive needs a login.

**Outcome of the scan.** Kintali (`47/48`) and Cureton–Thorner (`31/32`) claim, for every Dirichlet L-function, the register's target "Half-planes for Dirichlet L-functions by twisting the family", as the release does at `7/8` (round 277). None of them is derived here. Markers are on that register entry. Liu's optimality statement is that paper's claim, scoped to its own "exponent comparison system". It is not adopted here as a barrier.

**The audit.**

- **The companion handles a general character.** Its proof is written for a fixed finite-order Hecke character `ν` (paper2.tex, lines 665–667): "Fix a finite-order Hecke character $\nu$ of $K$ and a finite set $S$ of prime ideals that contains all prime ideals above $2$ or $3$, as well as all prime ideals dividing the conductor of $\nu$." Its family is `A_u(D) = Σ_{(n,S)=1} μ(n)ν(n)χ_n(u)W(N(n)/D)`.
- **How `ν` is absorbed.** Under Poisson summation, `ν` is absorbed into ray class characters `ξ` of a fixed modulus. At lines 810–811: "The character $\xi$ accounts for the original twist $\nu$ and for the residue-class factors in the identities below." At lines 815–817: "Choose a fixed modulus, supported on $S$, divisible by the conductor of $\nu$ and sufficiently large that all reciprocity factors below depend only on the corresponding ray classes." The 43 lines of `paper2.tex` that contain `\nu` all lie in lines 195–1599. The proof of the completed mean square begins at line 1632, and the arithmetic and theta appendix at line 2687.
- **Where the pilot fixes `ν = 1`.** In three places:

  - `S` is the set of primes above 2 and 3, as in the family's weight, nonzero only for `(absNorm I).Coprime 6` (`Eis.wsym`);
  - the fixed ray class group is `(𝒪/4)^×`, as in `ξ : MulChar (𝓞 K ⧸ span {(4 : 𝓞 K)}) ℂ` in `Eis.CompletedMeanSquare` and `Eis.ThetaRows`;
  - the reduction S0 (round 278's `HalfPlaneS0.ne_zero_of_smoothBound`) is for `r = 1 ⋆ χ₋₃`.

  For a general `ν`, the companion's route enlarges `S` and the fixed modulus by the conductor of `ν`. On this stack the chain's displays would then be restated for a general modulus, the theta step included.
- **A shorter route for the real characters.**

  - The family's twists are among its own members. Round 288's `Eis.MeanSquare σ`, proved for every `σ > 0` in round 466 (`Eis.meanSquare`), bounds the sum over every finite set of nonzero `z ∈ 𝒪_K`. Its docstring: "For every weight `W` and `ε > 0`, the sum of `|A_Z(z)|²` over any finite set of nonzero `z` with `N(z) ≤ Z^{1+σ}` is `O(Z^{2+σ+ε})`."
  - Round 281's `chi6` is defined by "`χ_P(x) = σ(u)`, where `u` is the unit of `ℤ[ω]` with `u ≡ x^{(N(P)−1)/6} (mod P)`". At `x = d³`, for `d ∈ ℤ` prime to `P`, the unit is `±1 ≡ d^{(N(P)−1)/2}`, the quadratic character of `d` in `𝒪/P`. At a prime `P` over a split `p` this is the Legendre symbol `(d/p)`. At an inert `p` it is `1`, since `d` lies in the prime field `𝔽_p` and every element of `𝔽_p` is a square in `𝔽_{p²}`. So `(d³/𝔞)₆` should be the Jacobi symbol `(d/N𝔞)` for every `𝔞` of norm prime to `6`.
  - Then `A_{d³b⁶}` is the family's member twisted by `χ_d∘N`. Round 288's averaging over `b`, with `u₀ = d³` in front, should bound `Σ μ(𝔞)(d/N𝔞)W(N𝔞/D)` by `D^{11/12+ε}`, with no change to the theta chain. With S0 for the coefficients `(d/n)·r(n)`, this gives `L(s, χ)L(s, χχ₋₃) ≠ 0` on `Re s > 11/12` for `χ = (d/·)`.
  - Every real primitive Dirichlet character is of that form [recalled: the real primitive characters are the Kronecker symbols of the fundamental discriminants; to be proved here]. *(round 477: the classification is not proved here; what the route needs, `χ(n) = J(χ(−1)q | n)` for every `n` prime to `2q`, is `Eis.RealChar.apply_eq_jacobiSym`)*
  - The route is planned for the real characters only. The family's twists have order dividing `6`, and the other characters are not examined here. The symbol identity, the twisted S0, the twisted extraction and the classification are the next steps; none is proved in this round.

**The plan**, in the order the owner approved.
