## Round 571: the diagonal in `ψ`, and the literature on cores 2 and 3 (`frontier/linnik/SEVEN-THIRDS.md` §39; `IDEAS.md` B32 marker and G14; `idea_register.py` check (R36))

**What it is.** Working toward the owner's goal "keep pushing until exponent is below 7/3". Round 570 left core 1's Farey part open from height `q^{1/6}` to `2M`, and its points of large height open throughout. This round splits round 535's coherence `θ′` by the characters `ψ` of B33's expansion, at every height at once, and scans the literature on the mean-square forms of cores 2 and 3. No exponent below `7/3` follows. No Lean changed, no probe is new, and no paper surface is edited.

- **The diagonal in `ψ` is small at every height.** In `X′(x) + e(x) = Σ_{ψ≠1}c_x(ψ)T_ψ(x)` (B33), `T_ψ(x) = F̄(ψ)U_ψ(x)` at every `x`, with `F(ψ) = Σ_{m₂≤M}ψ(m₂)` and `U_ψ(x) = Σ_{|a|,|b|≤M}ψ(ax + b)`.
  - Summed over every `x`, a proportional pair of points of the box gives `ψ̄(λ)` times `q − 1` or `q`, and a pair that is not proportional gives `−ψ(a/a′)` or `0`, by the Möbius substitution `y = (ax + b)/(a′x + b′)`. With at most `16M²(1 + log M)` proportional pairs, `Σ_x|U_ψ(x)|² ≤ 17qM²(1 + log M)`.
  - With B32's `|c_x(ψ)| ≤ r(ψ) + 3|W|²/L`, `|F(ψ)| ≤ M` and `E(W) = κ|W|⁴/L`, the terms `ψ = ψ′` of `‖X′ + e‖²` carry at most `(17/8)(κ + 9)(1 + log M)q^{−1/9}(1 + o(1))` of `θ′`, for every `W`. That is the value of B32's heuristic, `q^{−1/9}`, now a bound for these terms. The term `e(x)` carries at most `q^{−4/3+o(1)}` and `q^{−13/9+o(1)}`.
- **So core 1 is the off-diagonal.** When `κ ≤ q^{o(1)}` and `2δ < 1/9`, round 535's form of core 1 holds, up to constant factors, exactly when the terms `ψ ≠ ψ′` total at most `q^{−2δ}|box|²q|W|²`.
- **Why that resists.** Summing over `x` first leaves `K = Σ_x λ(x)U_ψ(x)Ū_{ψ′}(x)` for each choice of characters. Square-root cancellation in every `K`, with the characters bounded in absolute value, still leaves `(κ + 9)q^{1/6+o(1)}/8` of `θ′`. Cauchy–Schwarz over `ψ` leaves `q^{1/3}` (B32). The cancellation has to come from the characters themselves.
- **The literature on cores 2 and 3.** Core 2's mean-square form is the variance of the balanced `τ₃` in the residue classes mod `q` at length `q^{7/6}`, so `c = 7/6` and `k = 3` in `X = q^c`.
  - Nguyen (arXiv:2205.02354) proves the variance asymptotic for `τ_k` to composite moduli for `c ∈ (k − 1, k)`, and describes Kowalski and Ricotta's prime-modulus result as holding for `c ∈ (k − 1/2, k)`. At `k = 3` these are `(2, 3)` and `(5/2, 3)`.
  - Chandee, Li, Matomäki and Radziwiłł (arXiv:2409.01457) average the sixth moment over all moduli up to `Q`.
  - Neither reaches one prime modulus at `c = 7/6`, and Petrow–Young's Weyl bound reaches `c > 4/3` (B29).

**Sources.** Five web searches: the sixth moment of short character sums at a prime modulus; the variance of `d₃` to one prime modulus; large values of short character sums beyond the fourth moment; the exact title of Nguyen's paper; and zero density for Dirichlet `L`-functions in the `q`-aspect. ## Round 573: where the coherence sits against round 570's range (`frontier/linnik/SEVEN-THIRDS.md` §41; `IDEAS.md` B32 marker, C15, F6 and G15; `frontier/linnik/coherence_bands_probe.py`)

**What it is.** Working toward the owner's goal "keep pushing until exponent is below 7/3". Round 570 proved core 1's incoherence on the Farey points below height `q^{1/6}`, and round 571 put what is owed in the off-diagonal of B33's expansion in `ψ`. This round measures where the adversarial sets' coherence sits against both, writes the off-diagonal as an excess over multiplicative shifts, closes one route and reduces another, and scans the literature. No exponent below `7/3` follows. No Lean changed, no paper surface is edited, and one probe is new.

- **The off-diagonal as an excess over shifts.** With `Ỹ_u(x) = Σ_m R₀(uB_m(x)/x)R̄₀(uB_m(x)) − c_x(1)(|box| − Z(x))` for `u ∈ F_q^*`, `Ỹ_1(x) = X′(x) + e(x)`, and by Parseval over `ψ` the terms `ψ = ψ′` sum to the mean of `|Ỹ_u(x)|²` over `u`. So the off-diagonal at `x` is the excess of the unit shift over its multiplicative translates.
- **Measured** at `q = 10007` and `20011`, for the sets of `energy_frontier.py` with `κ ≤ 1.25`:
  - the off-diagonal carries `92%` and `84%` of `‖X′ + e‖²`;
  - the points of height at most `q^{1/6}`, round 570's proven range, carry `28%` and `15%`, and those above `q^{1/6}` and at most `4M` carry `63%` and `67%`;
  - for random sets the off-diagonal is `0.9%` and `−2.4%` of the total.

  So the adversarial sets found so far put their coherence off the diagonal and above round 570's range. These are measurements of the sets one search finds, and they bound nothing over all sets.
- **F6, closed.** The stack's half-plane proof gains because its target recurs in its family (the sixth-power members). Copies of a character such as `χ·χ₀^{(p)}` have Gram entries of about `L(1 − 1/p)(1 − 1/p′)` with one another, so `k` copies add about `kL` to every large sieve's norm. Twists by primitive cubic characters are orthogonal at length `L` when `qC² < L^{1−ε}`, but a large value at `χ` does not recur among them. For the critical cube the family's mean square over `χ mod q` is the sixth moment, core 2.
- **C15, reduced to core 4.** Young's fourth moment at prime moduli (arXiv:math/0610335) has a power-saving error. If the characters with `|L(½, χ)| ≤ q^ε` carried its main term up to `O(q^{1−δ})`, the large values at `q^{1/12}` would number at most `q^{2/3−δ′}`. That premise is a tail bound containing core 4.

**Sources.** Four web searches: large-value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials with characters to a prime modulus after Guth–Maynard; improvements to Linnik's constant for prime moduli; asymptotics for `x₁x₂x₃ ≡ y₁y₂y₃ (mod p)` in short intervals; and zero density for one prime modulus at bounded height below `7/3`. Six arXiv API queries sorted by submission date: "zero density" with Dirichlet; "large values" with characters; "character sums" with "short intervals" in math.NT; "multiplicative energy" with interval; "least prime" with progression; and "sixth moment" with Dirichlet. Seven abstracts not on file were read through the arXiv API: arXiv:2608.31060, 2505.19654, 2507.15334, 2508.14888, 0710.5176, 2505.23573 and 2606.09818 (IDEAS.md G15). The other hits were on file (among them arXiv:2507.08296, 2610.18923, 2608.16034, 2609.17875, 2608.15458) or, by title, off this goal. ## Round 574: how far the coherence exceeds the diagonal, and the authors' view of the obstruction (`frontier/linnik/SEVEN-THIRDS.md` §42; `IDEAS.md` B32 marker and G16; `frontier/linnik/cs_loss_probe.py`)

**What it is.** Working toward the owner's goal "keep pushing until exponent is below 7/3". Round 573 located the adversarial sets' coherence off the diagonal in `ψ` and above round 570's range. This round measures how far that coherence exceeds round 571's diagonal, states the resulting sufficient condition for core 1, measures how much B33's Cauchy–Schwarz gives away, and reads the method's own author on the obstruction. No exponent below `7/3` follows. No Lean changed, no paper surface is edited, and one measurement script is new.

- **A sufficient condition.** Round 571's diagonal carries at most `(17/8)(κ + 9)(1 + log M)q^{−1/9}(1 + o(1))` of `θ′`'s normalisation. So core 1 follows whenever `‖X′ + e‖²` exceeds the diagonal by a factor at most `q^{1/9−2δ}` divided by that constant.

## Round 575: a barrier for arguments built from polynomials shorter than `q` (`frontier/linnik/SEVEN-THIRDS.md` §43; `IDEAS.md` B34 and G17; `frontier/linnik/design_barrier_probe.py`)

**What it is.** Working toward the owner's goal "keep pushing until exponent is below 7/3". Rounds 573 and 574 located and measured core 1's coherence. This round asks which arguments could beat the critical count at all, and proves that one broad class cannot. The class bounds the count by the character sum of a sum of squares of Dirichlet polynomials shorter than `q`, with the needed inequality proved at every completely multiplicative function of modulus one. No exponent below `7/3` follows. No Lean changed, no paper surface is edited, and one script is new.

- **The class.** For `P = Σ_j |G_j|²` with each `G_j` of length below `q`, `Σ_χ P(χ) = (q − 1)Σ_j ‖g_j‖²` exactly, since distinct integers below `q` are distinct mod `q`. The fourth moment, the `2k`-th moments with `N^k < q`, twisted moments whose amplifiers are proved large at every such function, and finite sums of these are in the class.
- **The barrier.** Let `L` be the primes in `[N, 2N]`. Under a law `Ω` on such functions, `f(p) = 1` with probability `ρ = 2V/Σ_{p∈L} w(p/N)` for `p ∈ L`, and `f(p)` is uniform otherwise.
  - The block is then at least `V` with probability at least `1 − (N + 1)/V²`.
  - When `q ≤ N³`, the Gram matrix of `Ω` on the polynomials of length below `q` has top eigenvalue at most `λ = x²/2 + O(x)`, with `x = ρ²|L|`.
  - So every bound in the class is at least `(q − 1)(1 − (N + 1)/V²)/λ`. At the critical block that is about `q^{2/3}/(8 log² N)`, against the fourth moment's `q^{2/3}` times a constant times `log N`.
- **What it says.** A route to H\* must use something outside the class. That is a majorant that is not a sum of squares of polynomials shorter than `q`, the periodicity of the characters (Poisson summation, Gauss and Jacobi sums, Burgess's shifts), the functional equation, or congruences of height at least `q`. Cores 1–4 are stated in the last three of these terms.
- **Scan (G17).** Six web searches and seven abstracts found nothing bearing on cores 1–4.

**Sources.** Six web searches:

- "arXiv 2026 zero density estimate Dirichlet L-functions prime modulus large values Dirichlet polynomials characters";
- "multiplicative energy of intervals modulo prime x1x2x3 = y1y2y3 asymptotic sixth moment short character sums";
- "large values of short character sums count of characters |sum chi(n)| large power saving fourth moment improvement";
- a search for Chen–Gupta–Li's title with "improvement prime moduli 7/3 Linnik constant 2026";
- "sixth moment Dirichlet L-functions single prime modulus new bound 2026 arXiv";
- "ternary divisor function d_3 arithmetic progressions prime modulus variance mean square beyond 2/3 2026".

Seven abstracts were read through the arXiv API: 2509.09771, 2607.01184, 2405.20552, 1909.09497, 2608.05961, 2508.13301 and 2609.27808.

  - At `N = 10⁶`, each of 40 draws from `Ω` has its block at least `N^{5/7}`.
  - The Gram formula is within `0.0022` of Monte Carlo, and the premise holds at `q = 211` to `2.2·10⁻¹⁶`.
  - At `N = 2000` the floor lies below the fourth moment's exact count, as weak duality requires.
  - At `N = 10⁶` the floor is `0.767` times `q^{2/3}/(8 log² N)`.

## Round 576: a sieve route to Linnik's exponent below `7/3` (`frontier/linnik/SEVEN-THIRDS.md` §44; `IDEAS.md` D5 and G18; `frontier/linnik/sieve_route_probe.py`)

**What it is.** Working toward the owner's goal "keep pushing until exponent is below 7/3". Round 575's brainstorm subagent proposed Harman's sieve with the density bounds feeding its Type II sums. This round re-derived the argument and computed the sieve's losses.

The result is at paper level and unrefereed. Assume the stack's half-plane (H1) and the classical density bounds (1.4)–(1.5) as Chen–Gupta–Li state them. Then every large prime `q` and every `a` prime to `q` have a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` in `[x, 2x]` at `x = q^{2.29}`. With their `7/3` as well, `x = q^{2.27}` suffices.

That is a Linnik exponent below `7/3`. The density exponent is not lowered. No Lean changed, no paper surface is edited, and one script is new.

- **The Type II lemma.** Take the characters whose zeros near the relevant height have real part about `β`; (H2) bounds their number by `q^{A(β)(1−β)}`.
  - On them, a product of smooth prime sums of length `X` is at most `X^{β+ε}`, by the zero-free region and Mellin inversion.
  - A polynomial `W` of length `P` with arbitrary coefficients has `Σ_χ |W|² ≤ (q + P)‖w‖²`.
  - Cauchy–Schwarz over those characters gives a window `(u₁, u₂)`: for lengths `x^u` inside it, the Type II sum is `o(x)` at every `β ∈ [1/2, 11/12]`.
- **Separating the variables.** Perron's formula at height `x²` removes the sharp conditions ~~with no truncation error~~ *(Round 577: retracted, false when written. The truncation error is negligible, not absent; review F1)*. The heights it introduces cost nothing, because `A(β)(1 − β) < 1`. But they use (H2) for every `T` and (H1) at every height, and both are stated that way.
- **The sieve.** Type I information holds up to `x^{1−1/L}`. ~~Harman's fundamental theorem then evaluates `S(A_r, x^v)` for `r ≤ x^{1−u₂}`.~~ *(Round 581: retracted, false when written. It evaluates the sum over `r` with the decomposition's coefficients, not each `r` alone; SEVEN-THIRDS §44, SIEVE-ROUTE.md Proposition 6. Review F3.)* A depth-4 Buchstab decomposition does the rest, and its dropped terms are the loss.
- **Numbers.** The windows are `(0.398877, 0.475983)` at `L = 2.29` with the classical bounds and `(0.404154, 0.486050)` at `L = 2.27` with the `7/3`. The upper bounds on the loss are `0.9722` and `0.9193` *(round 585: rounded to nearest; as bounds `0.9723` and `0.9193`, not certified; review F3)*, and the midpoint estimates `0.7435` and `0.5783`. Midpoint thresholds are near `2.28` and `2.245`.
- **Strikes.** SEVEN-THIRDS §1's "Going below `7/3` needs a density exponent …" and round 528's "Going below `7/3` needs the open step of SEVEN-THIRDS.md §6" quantified over every proof (Check 9(a)), and both are struck at source.
- **Scan (G18).** Two arXiv API searches and six queries on arXiv's search page returned entries, and four abstracts were read. None of the sieve proofs of Linnik's theorem among them uses a zero-free half-plane with density bounds as Type II information. The nearest relative is Heath-Brown and Iwaniec's short-interval method for `ζ`, which uses weighted zero-density estimates for a lower bound on primes.

**Sources.**

## Round 578: a certificate for the sieve's loss, and the exponents `2.28` and `2.25` (`frontier/linnik/sieve_route_certificate.py`; `frontier/linnik/SEVEN-THIRDS.md` §§44–45)

**What it is.** After round 577 the lead proposed hardening the sieve route before building on it, starting with its numerics, and the owner replied "Start as suggested". `sieve_route_certificate.py` is new. It proves upper bounds for the loss of SEVEN-THIRDS §44's decomposition: ~~every decision in a bound is exact,~~ *(Round 579: retracted, false when written. Every test of the region, of evaluability and of decomposition is exact. The comparisons in floating point that feed a bound, `ω`'s zero tests, its table indices and the choice between two bounds, each err on the safe side. Review F2.)* every floating-point operation on a bound is rounded outward, Buchstab's `ω` is enclosed and the Type II windows are proved. On the way it found that round 576's rule for decomposition is not sharp. With the sharp rule the loss is certified below `1` at `L = 2.28` from the stack's half-plane and the classical density bounds, and at `L = 2.25` with Chen–Gupta–Li's `7/3`. The analysis of §44 is unchanged, at paper level and unrefereed. No Lean changed, and no paper surface is edited.

**What is certified** (`sieve_route_certificate.py`, gate C5): a number below `1` that is at least the loss of §44's decomposition run with a window proved to lie inside the Type II window.

| curve | `L` | cells a side | certified bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| hux | 2.28 | 600 | ~~0.9520~~ 0.9521 |
| cons | 2.25 | 600 | 0.9117 |
| hux | 2.29 | 600 | ~~0.7821~~ 0.7822 |
| cons | 2.27 | 600 | ~~0.6230~~ 0.6231 |
| hux | 2.32 | 50 | ~~0.8292~~ 0.8293 |

*(Round 584: four certified bounds were the printed values rounded down to four places, and are struck and rounded up. The printed values are `0.9520185…`, `0.9116855…`, `0.7821377…`, `0.6230258…` and `0.8292216…`; SEVEN-THIRDS §45; review F1.)*

"hux" is the curve of Chen–Gupta–Li's (1.4) and (1.5); "cons" adds their `7/3`.

**How.**

- Every coordinate is an integer multiple of `2^{−40}`, so every test of the region, of evaluability and of the conditions for decomposition compares integers.
- Each floating-point operation on a bound is followed by one step of `nextafter` outward, and each sum of `n` nonnegative terms is multiplied by `1 + 4n·2^{−53}`.
- `ω` is enclosed on intervals of length `2^{−16}` up to `16`, from `ω(t) = 1/t` on `[1, 2)` and `(tω(t))′ = ω(t − 1)`. The enclosure's width is at most `1.53·10⁻⁵`.
- The windows are proved by branch and bound in exact rational arithmetic, using that `A(β)(1 − β)` decreases on each piece of a curve.

**The sharp rule.** A non-evaluable term of depth 2 can be decomposed when `α₁ + α₂ ≤ R`, and its non-evaluable terms of depth 3 then need `α₁ + α₂ + α₃ ≤ R`, where `R = 1 − u₂`. The complement window is `(R, 1 − u₁)`, so a sum in it makes the term evaluable. So a cell whose sums stay below `1 − u₁` can be decomposed: every non-evaluable point in it meets the condition.

- Round 576's rule asks for the sums to be at most `R` on the whole cell. For `(α₁, α₂)` in a region of positive area the non-evaluable `α₃` reach `R − α₁ − α₂`, so that rule refuses the `α₃` cell across that value at every grid size.
- For hux at `2.29` the certificate prints `1.1223`, `1.0198` and `0.9705` under round 576's rule at `n = 150`, `300` and `600`, and `0.8964`, `0.8191` and `0.7821` under the sharp rule, against the midpoint estimate `0.7435`. Both sequences halve their steps as `n` doubles; extrapolated that way, the first tends to about `0.921` and the second to about `0.745`.
- The certificate also prints the cells that the sharp rule may decompose and round 576's rule refuses: `289`, `1045` and `3960` cells, of area `0.00230`, `0.00208` and `0.00197`. The area stays near `0.002`, where a boundary layer's would halve with each doubling.
- So SEVEN-THIRDS §44's "The bound converges slowly from above" was false when written. It is struck at source.
- This resolves round 577's next step: its reviewer's variant m6 (the rule tested at the lower corner) gave `0.7838`, and its decisions held at every point tested.

**The thresholds.** ~~The certificate prints the probe's midpoint estimates near the thresholds: hux at `2.275` is `1.0279` and at `2.28` is `0.9007`; cons at `2.24` is `1.1692` and at `2.245` is `0.9851`.~~ *(Round 579: retracted, false when written. The certificate prints the probe's midpoint estimates for hux at `2.275` (`1.0279`) and cons at `2.245` (`0.9851`). Those for hux at `2.28` (`0.9007`) and cons at `2.24` (`1.1692`) are printed by `sieve_route_probe.py`. Review F1.)* At `n = 600` the certificate prints hux at `2.27` (`1.2845`) and cons at `2.24` (`1.2545`), both above `1`.

**A correction.** SEVEN-THIRDS §44's Scope said that the stack's `CharDensity` statements "are for heights `O(log q)`". `Linnik.CharDensity A B C` (`external/pnt/LinnikDeduction.lean`) holds for every `T ≥ 2`, so the sentence was false when written; it is struck at source. ## Round 580: the sieve route written out, and a literature check (`frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md`; `frontier/linnik/SEVEN-THIRDS.md` §§44 and 46; `frontier/linnik/IDEAS.md` D5 and G19)

**What it is.** The next two steps of the hardening that the owner asked for after round 577 ("Start as suggested"). `SIEVE-ROUTE.md` is new. It writes out SEVEN-THIRDS §44's argument, with §45's rule for decomposition, lemma by lemma, for a referee and as a blueprint for Lean. G19 records a literature check. Writing the argument out corrected two points of §44; neither moves a number. Nothing new is certified, no Lean changed, and no paper surface is edited.

**The write-up** (`SIEVE-ROUTE.md`).

- §0 states the theorem. Assume the stack's half-plane (H1) and the density bounds (H2). Then for every large `q` and every `a` prime to `q` there is a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` in `[x, 2x]`, with `x = q^{2.28}` on the curve hux and `x = q^{2.25}` on the curve cons. No step uses that `q` is prime.
- §1 fixes the notation. §2 lists the inputs:
  - (H1) and (H2);
  - orthogonality over the characters (T1);
  - the zeros and `L′/L` (T2);
  - the fundamental lemma (T3);
  - the rough numbers (T4).

  The standard results are marked as such, and their sources were not re-read.
- §3 gives the Type II estimate:
  - Lemma 1 bounds smooth prime sums at heights up to `2x³` through the zeros within `x^ε` of the height;
  - Lemma 2 bounds the number of characters with a zero near a height, integrated over the heights;
  - the window `(u₁, u₂)` is defined;
  - Proposition 3 is the Type II bound, with the characters binned by the real parts of their zeros.

## Round 582: a uniform exponent `12/5` suffices for an exponent below `7/3`, and the Lean route planned (`frontier/linnik/sieve_route_certificate.py`; `frontier/linnik/SEVEN-THIRDS.md` §47; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §9)

**What it is.** The first step toward the goal the lead proposed after round 577, which the owner took up with "Start as suggested": a kernel-checked exponent below `7/3`. Planning it raised a question: does the sieve need density curves that depend on `σ`?

It does not, for an exponent below `7/3`. Take the uniform curve "unif", `A(σ) = min(12/5 + 1/2000, 1/(1 − σ))`: Huxley's uniform exponent with a slack of `1/2000`, capped by the trivial count. With it the certificate bounds the loss at `L = 2.333` by ~~`0.9756`~~ `0.9757` at `n = 600` *(round 584: rounded up from the printed `0.9756129805606728`; review F1)*. SIEVE-ROUTE.md §9 then plans the Lean route in eight milestones. No Lean changed, and no paper surface is edited.

**The uniform curve** (SEVEN-THIRDS §47).

- At `L = 2.333` the window ~~is `(0.417252, 0.485534)`,~~ *(round 584: the struck values are the proved window rounded outward; rounded inward it is `(0.417253, 0.485533)`; review F1. Reworded in round 585, review F7.)* is proved by branch and bound in 730 boxes.
- The certified bound is `0.9756129805606728` at `n = 600`.
- So under (H1) and `Σ_{χ mod q} N(σ, T, χ) ≤ (qT)^{(12/5 + 1/2000)(1 − σ) + o(1)}` for every `σ` and `T ≥ 2`, §44's decomposition gives `x = q^{2.333}`, below `q^{7/3}`.
- The uniform bound is implied by (1.4) and (1.5), whose largest exponent is `12/5`, so it is a weaker hypothesis.
- Scratch runs show the margin:
  - at `L = 2.333` the bound is `1.0367` at `n = 300` and `0.9510` at `n = 900` *(round 585: rounded to nearest; as bounds `1.0368` and `0.9511`; review F3)*;
  - with `A = 12/5` exactly it is `0.9637` at `n = 600` *(round 585: as a bound `0.9638`; review F3)*;
  - at `L = 2.33` with `A = 12/5` it is `1.0285` at `n = 600` *(round 585: as a bound `1.0286`, from `1.02852061…`; review F3)*;
  - at `L = 2.33` the probe's midpoint estimate is `0.9652` with `A = 12/5`, and `1.8399` with `A = 12/5 + 0.054`.
- For Lean, the stack's `LinnikTwelve.charDensity_twelve_fifths` has the exponent `12/5 + 54ε` for every `ε ≤ 1/200`. That reaches the slack `1/2000`, but it counts characters, and Lemma 2 counts zeros.

**The certificate.** `sieve_route_certificate.py` gains the curve unif and the case `(unif, 2.333, 600)`.

## Round 583: the first Lean step of milestone M1, large values at several points per character, and a survey of M1 (`external/pnt/LinnikPoints.lean`)

**What it is.** The first Lean step on SIEVE-ROUTE.md §9's route. A count of zeros (milestone M1) detects several zeros of one character, at ordinates at least `1` apart, but the stack's estimates for large values take one point per character. ~~`LinnikPoints.large_values_points` lifts that restriction for the large sieve.~~ *(Round 585: retracted, false when written. It extends `large_values_chars` only; the counting lemmas use the off-line form `large_values_chars_off` (`LinnikHybrid.lean:460`; it read `:479`, the line of its call to `large_values_chars`, corrected in round 587, review F6), which is not yet extended; review F6.)* `LinnikPoints.large_values_points` lifts that restriction for round 521's `large_values_chars`. A survey of rounds 524–527 places the rest of M1. It was made for this round by a subagent, and its main claims were spot-checked by the lead.

**The theorem.** `LinnikPoints.large_values_points`:

- Take `S ⊆ (P, 2P]`, `c_j ∈ ℂ` and `q ≥ 1`.
- Take points `(χ_i, x_i)`, `i ∈ Rs`, with `x_i ∈ [lo + ½, hi − ½]`, any two points of one character being at distance at least `1`.
- Then `Σ_i |Σ_{j∈S} c_jχ_i(j)j^{−ix_i}|² ≤ (q(hi − lo) + 8P(1 + log P))(2 + log²(2P))Σ|c_j|²`.

This is the bound of round 521's `large_values_chars`, and that theorem is the case of one point per character (`large_values_chars_of_points`). The proof groups the points by character. For each group, `DirMean.gallagher`, which is Gallagher's lemma for a `1`-separated set, bounds the group by the integral over `[lo, hi]`. Then `mean_value_chars` finishes, as in round 521.

**The survey of M1.** One point per character enters the proofs of the uniform `12/5` in five ways:

- (i) the Gallagher step of `large_values_chars` (`LinnikHybrid.lean` lines 403–409, checked), which this round generalizes;
- (ii) the count `|R| ≤ q` (`card_chars_le`), used as a count of points;
- (iii) `choose!`, which picks one zero per character in the counting lemmas (~~`LinnikDensity.lean:560` and `LinnikTwelve.lean:416` checked; the survey also names `LinnikIngham.lean:339` and `LinnikHuxley.lean:843`~~ *(round 585: retracted, false when written: two of the four sites are outside the proof of the `12/5`; review F1)* `LinnikTwelve.lean:416`, in `count_twelve_at`, and `LinnikIngham.lean:339`, in `count_nontrivial_ingham`, both in the dependency closure of `charDensity_twelve_fifths` (checked in round 585). `LinnikDensity.lean:560` and `LinnikHuxley.lean:843` are outside it);
- (iv) the Halász–Montgomery kernel. Its off-diagonal pairs have `χ ≠ χ′` (~~`LinnikLargeValues.pair_reflect`~~ `LinnikReflect.pair_reflect`, in `LinnikLargeValues.lean`, takes `hne : χ ≠ χ'`, checked) *(round 584: the theorem's namespace is `LinnikReflect`, not the file's name)*. Pairs of points of one character would bring in the principal character, with the pole of `ζ`;
- (v) the trivial character, which is counted as `+1`.

The survey's estimates, which are estimates and not checked:

- The range `σ ≤ 3/4` needs re-indexing over points only, about one round.
- The Huxley range `3/4 ≤ σ ≤ 11/12` needs the principal character's kernel, with its residue and `ζ`'s functional equation in the stack's form. That is the main risk, roughly 500 to 1000 lines.
- The stack has no local count of the zeros of `L(s, χ)`. Jensen's formula, with the stack's bounds for `L(s, χ)`, would give one in roughly 150 to 300 lines.
- The trivial character can be left out, since SIEVE-ROUTE.md §3 uses only `χ ≠ χ₀`.
- The survey also notes a way through with no new estimate. Multiplying the stack's count of characters by `2T + 1` bounds the number of points. That is not enough here: Lemma 2 sums over heights up to `x³`, and the factor `T` cancels its weight `1/(1 + |γ|)`.

## Round 586: smoothing in place of Perron at height `x²`, so that the sieve route needs counts of characters only (`frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §10)

**What it is.** SIEVE-ROUTE.md §8 named a way around Lemma 2's counts of zeros: "a smoothing that keeps the heights below `x^ε`, where a count of characters suffices; that smoothing is not worked out here". The new §10 works it out, at paper level and unrefereed.

If it holds, the density input of the sieve route at `x = q^{2.333}` is a theorem of the stack, `LinnikTwelve.charDensity_twelve_fifths`, which counts characters. Milestone M1 of the Lean plan (counts of zeros over points `(χ, t)`, which round 583's survey put at roughly 500 to 1000 lines in the Huxley range) is then not needed.

No Lean changed, no number changed, and no paper surface is edited.

**The argument.**

- **Lemma 4′.** Each sharp comparison of Lemma 4 is replaced by `G(log Z − log Y)`, where `G(u) = g(u/θ)c(u/Λ)` and `θ = x^{−ε₂}`.
  - Fourier inversion separates the variables. `Ĝ` decays like `θ^{1−K}|τ|^{−K}`, so the heights can be cut at `T₀ = x^{2ε₂}` at a cost of `O(1/x)`.
  - Each comparison then errs only on the event `Y ≤ Z < e^θY`.
- **Lemma 4″.** Those events are bounded by smooth majorants that keep the term's variables.
  - Their count over the model is `≪ x^{1−ε₂/2}`: two primes within `3θp` of each other, or a product within `3θz` of a threshold.
  - Their count over `A` differs from the model by the Type II estimate itself.
- **Proposition 3′.** With every height below `x^ε`, each character is binned once, by `b(χ)`, the largest real part of its zeros up to height `2x^ε`. The bins are then counted by (H2′), a count of characters, and Lemma 2 is not used.
- **(H2′).** (H2) implies it. With unif it follows from `charDensity_twelve_fifths` with `ε = 1/108000`, and from the trivial count `φ(q) ≤ qT` where `A(σ)(1 − σ) = 1`.
- **The rest.** Proposition 6, §6 and Proposition 7 use Lemma 4 and Proposition 3 only through the bound `x^{1−δ}/φ(q)` for each difference, so they are unchanged.

**The Lean plan, revised** (§10's "For Lean").

- M1 is not needed.
- M2 is Lemma 1 at heights up to `2x^ε`. The bound for `L′/L` can come from `Linnik.logDeriv_LFunction_le` in zero-free discs, in place of (T2).
- M3 is Proposition 3′.
- M4 is Lemmas 4′ and 4″.
- M5–M8 are unchanged.
- For hux, M1 becomes hux's curves in `σ` as counts of characters. The choice between unif and hux now turns on M7 against those curves.

**Markers** (net-state, since the earlier statements were true of Lemma 4's sharp cut-offs):

- SIEVE-ROUTE.md §8: the items for Lemma 2 and Lemma 4.
- SIEVE-ROUTE.md §9: M1, "Why counts of zeros", M2, M3, M4, M7 and "Order".
- SEVEN-THIRDS §47: the two statements about counts of zeros.
- IDEAS.md D5.

**What is checked.**

- Each Lean name cited was read in its file:
  - `Linnik.logDeriv_LFunction_le` (`LinnikChar.lean:147`, statement and docstring);
  - `LinnikTwelve.charDensity_twelve_fifths` (statement: `∃ C, 0 ≤ C ∧ CharDensity (12/5 + 54ε) 10 C` for `0 < ε ≤ 1/200`);
  - `Linnik.CharDensity` (`LinnikDeduction.lean`), which counts all characters mod `q` with a zero in `Re s ≥ σ`, `|Im s| ≤ T`.
- In Mathlib at the pinned commit, `Real.fourier_iteratedDeriv`, `Continuous.fourierInv_fourier_eq` and `Real.smoothTransition` exist (`grep`). They are the analytic pieces M4 would use.
- §§5–7 were read where they use Lemma 4 and Proposition 3: SIEVE-ROUTE.md lines 131, 145 and 155.
- The lead's self-review of the draft scoped two sentences that said the theorem rests on the stack's inputs alone. The standard inputs (T1)–(T4) of §2 remain at paper level.
- `tools/research/render_lint.py`'s `lint` was run on the changed markdown files and compared with HEAD by defect class: SIEVE-ROUTE.md goes from 9 to 12 reports, three new ones of class L10 (a nested list directly after its item's text), all in §10; the sweep adds none to SEVEN-THIRDS.md (63), IDEAS.md (51), STRUCTURAL-REVIEW.md (100) or README.md's earlier rounds. This entry takes README.md from 1839 to 1842 reports, three new ones of class L10, the style of the entries around them. None of these files is a paper surface.

**Check 4.** Novel. §8 named the smoothing and said it was not worked out. §9's "Why counts of zeros" concerned the large sieve with Lemma 4's sharp cut-offs.

**Check 9.** (a) "M1 is not needed" and "counts of characters suffice" are scoped to this route with §10, at paper level. (b) No change to the register's targets. (c) No criterion is fed a signal.

## Round 588: the owner's goals, and the smooth cut-off of Lemma 4′ in Lean (`external/pnt/SieveSmooth.lean`; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §11)

**The owner's decision.** "Keep on the lean work but note this as a follow on goal. My immediate goal is to formalise 2.333 then to push on using the 7/3 result then to abstract all that is relevant to a clean gh repo & publish". SIEVE-ROUTE.md §11 records it:

1. a Lean formalization of `x = q^{2.333}` by §10's route with the curve unif;
2. then the `7/3` result, with the curve cons;
3. then a clean repository on GitHub, published.

Lower exponents are a follow-on goal. §11 records the floor of this framework, `L > 1 + A_max/2` for a nonempty Type II window, and the two routes on record. It also records the main risk of the first goal, the size of M7's certificate, with a candidate remedy.

**The Lean file.** `external/pnt/SieveSmooth.lean` is the first step of M4: the analytic part of Lemma 4′. It imports only Mathlib. With `g = Real.smoothTransition`, `θ > 0`, `Λ ≥ 0` and `G(u) = g(u/θ) − g((u − 2Λ)/θ)`:

- `G` is smooth, vanishes outside `[0, 2Λ + θ]`, and takes values in `[0, 1]` when `θ ≤ 2Λ`.
- For `u ≤ Λ`, `1[u > 0] − G(u)` and `1[u ≥ 0] − G(u)` lie in `[0, 1]` and vanish unless `0 ≤ u < θ` (`indicator_sub_G`).
- `‖G^{(K)}‖₁ ≤ 2θ^{1−K}‖g^{(K)}‖₁` for `K ≥ 1` (`integral_norm_iteratedDeriv_GC_le`), from `G^{(K)}(u) = θ^{−K}(g^{(K)}(u/θ) − g^{(K)}((u − 2Λ)/θ))` and the vanishing of `g^{(K)}` outside `[0, 1]`.
- `(2π|ξ|)^K‖𝓕G(ξ)‖ ≤ 2θ^{1−K}‖g^{(K)}‖₁` (`pow_mul_norm_fourier_GC_le`), by Mathlib's `Real.fourier_iteratedDeriv`.
- `𝓕G` is integrable (`integrable_fourier_GC`).
- **Separation:** `G(a − b) = ∫ e^{2πiξa}e^{−2πiξb}𝓕G(ξ) dξ` for real `a` and `b` (`GC_sub_eq_integral`), by Mathlib's `Continuous.fourierInv_fourier_eq`.

§10 writes the cut-off as `g(u/θ)c(u/Λ)`. The two forms agree on `u ≤ Λ`, and every property §10 uses holds for this one, with support `[0, 2Λ + θ]` in place of `[0, 2Λ]`. The file was prototyped in scratch during the review of round 586.

**What is checked.**

- `lean` was run on `SieveSmooth.lean` alone, with the build's `LEAN_PATH` (Mathlib at `MATHLIB_REV`): no errors and no warnings.
- `#print axioms` gives `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` for `indicator_sub_G`, `pow_mul_norm_fourier_GC_le`, `integrable_fourier_GC` and `GC_sub_eq_integral`.
- `external/pnt/build.sh` now lists the file, imports it in the final check and prints those four axioms; `bash -n` passes. The rest of the layer was not rebuilt, since none of its sources changed.
- `tools/research/render_lint.py`'s `lint` was run on the changed markdown files and compared with HEAD by defect class: SIEVE-ROUTE.md goes from 12 to 15 reports, three new ones of class L10 (a nested list directly after its item's text), all in §11; README.md (1842), IDEAS.md (51), SEVEN-THIRDS.md (63), STRUCTURAL-REVIEW.md (100) and `external/pnt/README.md` (10) gain none. ## Round 589: the step curve for `x = q^{2.333}`, and its density in Lean (`external/pnt/LinnikStep.lean`; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §12)

**The problem.** Round 588 named the main risk of the first goal (SIEVE-ROUTE.md §11). ~~With the curve unif at `L = 2.333` the loss certificate needs about `9.0` million cells of depth 4, too many to replay in Lean.~~ *(Round 590: retracted, false when written: `n = 410` certifies with about `2.1` million; review F3.)* With the curve unif at `L = 2.333` the committed loss certificate uses about `9.0` million cells of depth 4, and the coarsest grid tried that certifies, `n = 410`, about `2.1` million (SIEVE-ROUTE.md §9). Either is too many to replay in Lean.

**The curve step.** It is unif below `σ = 5/6` and `101/50` from `5/6` on.

- The certificate's bound depends on the curve only through the window of SIEVE-ROUTE.md §3. Its left end `u₁` is set at `β = 11/12`, where step's `101/50` replaces unif's `12/5 + 1/2000`. At `L = 2.333` the proved window is `(0.400943, 0.485533)`, against unif's `(0.417253, 0.485533)` (rounded inward).
- The certificate then bounds the loss by `0.8579` at `n = 70` (rounded up from the printed `0.857896…`), with 916 cells of depth 2 and 1568 of depth 4. The decomposition runs on the printed window, `(0.4009429927873498, 0.4855336467326197)` *(round 590: this sentence added; review F5)*.
- With a crude upper bound for `ω`, `0` below `1`, `1/t` on `[1, 2)` and `0.5672` on `[2, 16)`, the bound at `n = 70` is `0.8660` (rounded up from `0.865918…`).

**The Lean file.** `external/pnt/LinnikStep.lean` proves step's density on `[5/6, 1]`. `LinnikStep.charDensity_step` gives `C ≥ 0` such that for every `q ≥ 1`, `5/6 ≤ σ ≤ 1` and `T ≥ 2`, at most `C(qT)^{(101/50)(1−σ)}(log qT)^{10}` characters mod `q` have a zero of `L(s, χ)` with `Re s ≥ σ` and `|Im s| ≤ T`.

- The proof is round 527's on `[3/4, 11/12]`, with three parameters changed: `X = ⌊Q^{1/2000}⌋`, `Y = Q^{201/400}` and the power trick's target `Q^{2/3+ε}`, in place of `⌊Q^{1/25}⌋`, `Q^{3/5}` and `Q^{4/5+ε}`. The power is then at most `1334` in place of `22`.
- Up to powers of `Q^ε`, the first term of Huxley's estimate carries `Q^{(201/100)(1−σ)}`. The second carries `Q^{(2/3)(4−6σ)+1}`, below `Q^{(101/50)(1−σ)}` by at least `Q^{1/300}`. The integral class carries `Q^{(201/100)(1/2−σ)+1/500+1}`, below it by `Q^{13/1000−σ/100}`.
- With the fourth moment as its input for the integral class, this argument gives a constant `A` on `[σ₁, 11/12]` when `A > 3/(3σ₁ − 1)` and `A > 2 + 8x`, `X = Q^x`, and no constant at or below `2` (SIEVE-ROUTE.md §12). Huxley's curve `3/(3σ − 1)` is `2` at `5/6`.

So with step, at paper level, the density input (H2′) of SIEVE-ROUTE.md §10 follows from `LinnikTwelve.charDensity_twelve_fifths`, `LinnikStep.charDensity_step` and the trivial count. M7 becomes a certificate of 2484 cells at `n = 70`. Of `ω` it needs only facts that follow from its delay equation (SIEVE-ROUTE.md §12).

## Round 591: Lemma 1 of the sieve route in Lean, at a height `y` (`external/pnt/SieveLemma1.lean`, `external/pnt/SieveWeight.lean`; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §§9 and 10, M2)

**What it is.** Milestone M2 of the first goal (SIEVE-ROUTE.md §§9–11). It is Lemma 1 of §3, the bound for a smooth prime sum at a height `y` through a zero-free rectangle about `y`, at the heights §10 needs.

**The theorem.** `SieveWeight.norm_Sp_le`: let `f0` be smooth and real with support in `[1/2, 2]`, and `K ≥ 0` an integer. There are `B, C ≥ 0` such that for every `q ≥ 1`, `χ ≠ 1` mod `q`, `½ ≤ θ ≤ 11/12`, `0 < δ ≤ 1/24`, `H ≥ 0`, `P ≥ 4` and real `y`: if `L(·, χ)` has no zero in `Re s > θ`, `|Im s − y| < H + 1`, then

`|Σ_{p ≤ 2P} χ(p)(p/P)^{−iy}f0(p/P)| ≤ M A B(P^{θ+δ} + P^{11/12+δ}(1 + H)^{−K})/log P + C(⌊√N⌋ + 1)(⌊log₂ N⌋ + 1)`,

with `N = ⌊2P⌋`, `M = KL(θ, θ + δ) + KL(11/12, 11/12 + δ)` and `A = log(q + 2) + log(|y| + 4) + 1`.

- `B` and `C` depend only on `f0` and `K`. The bound is therefore uniform in the scale `P`, the modulus and the height.
- §3's Lemma 1 at heights `|y| ≤ 2x^ε` follows on paper. Take `θ = β(χ, y)`, which is at least `1/2` by its definition and at most `11/12` by the stack's zero-free half-plane. Take `H = x^ε − 1`, `δ = ε` and `K ≥ 2/ε`.
  - For fixed `δ`, `KL(θ, θ + δ)` is a continuous function of `θ` on `[1/2, 11/12]` (`LogDerivDisc.Kld`), so it is bounded there.
  - Then `|Σ_p φ(p/Q)χ(p)p^{−iy}| ≪_ε Q^{β(χ,y)+ε} log x`, against §3's `log² x`.
  - That deduction belongs to M3, which uses it.

**The proof.**

- `SieveLemma1.lean` proves the bound for `Σ_n χ(n)Λ(n)w(n/X)` with a general weight `w` (`norm_Sw_le`). Its hypotheses are that `w` is continuous on `(0, ∞)`, that `𝓜w` converges at `2` and is differentiable on `Re s ≥ θ + δ`, and that `(1 + |t − y|)^{K+3}|𝓜w(σ + it)| ≤ B` for `θ + δ ≤ σ ≤ 2`. The proof has four steps.
  - Perron's formula with the weight (`perron_weight`, from Mathlib's `mellinInv_mellin_eq`) writes the sum as an integral on `Re s = 2`.
  - The whole line moves to `Re s = 11/12 + δ` (`integral_pw_shift`, by `SmoothPerron.verticalIntegral_shift`), through the stack's zero-free half-plane `Re s > 11/12`.
  - For `|t − y| ≤ H` it then moves across the rectangle `[θ + δ, 11/12 + δ] × [y − H, y + H]` to `θ + δ`, inside the zero-free rectangle of the hypothesis.
  - There `Linnik.logDeriv_LFunction_le` bounds `L′/L` (`norm_pw_le`). Beyond height `H`, the decay of `𝓜w` gives the factor `(1 + H)^{−K}`.

  This is round 520's `Linnik.norm_Sx_le` with the weight `w` in place of `e^{−u}`, and with the rectangle centred at height `y`.
- `SieveWeight.lean` applies it to primes, with §3's weight. Put `ψ_P(u) = f0(u)(1 + log u/log P)⁻¹`. Then `f0(n/P)/log n = ψ_P(n/P)/log P`. This is §3's `ψ = φ/log(Qu)` times `log P`.
  - In the variable `v = −log u`, `𝓜ψ_P(σ + it)` is the Fourier transform of `e^{−σv}f0(e^{−v})(1 − av)⁻¹`, with `a = 1/log P` (Mathlib's `mellin_eq_fourier`).
  - Leibniz's rule bounds that function's derivatives uniformly in `0 ≤ σ ≤ 2` and `P ≥ 4` (`exists_bound_iteratedDeriv_gw`), with Mathlib's `iter_deriv_inv_linear` for `(1 − av)⁻¹`.
  - So round 588's `SieveSmooth.pow_mul_norm_fourier_le` gives `(1 + |t|)^{K+3}|𝓜ψ_P(σ + it)| ≤ B` (`exists_mellin_bound`).
  - `norm_Sw_le` with `w(u) = u^{−iy}ψ_P(u)`, whose Mellin transform is `𝓜ψ_P(s − iy)` (Mathlib's `mellin_cpow_smul`), bounds the sum over `Λ` (`norm_Sw_wy_le`).
  - The sum over `Λ` is `log P` times the prime sum plus the proper prime powers' share (`Sw_wy_eq`). There are at most `(⌊√N⌋ + 1)(⌊log₂ N⌋ + 1)` proper prime powers up to `N` (`card_properPrimePow_le`), and each contributes at most `max |f0|`.

**Against the plan.** SIEVE-ROUTE.md §10's plan for M2 moved only the segment `|Im s − y| ≤ x^ε` and bounded the tails on `Re s = 2` by `ChiUniform.logDeriv_LFunction_right`. The proof here moves the whole line to `11/12 + δ` first, since the stack has no zero in `Re s > 11/12`. So its tails lie on `Re s = 11/12 + δ`, where the decay of `𝓜w` controls them. §3's choice of `Y` to avoid ordinates, and (T2), are not used.

**What is checked.**

SIEVE-ROUTE.md (18) and `external/pnt/README.md` (10) gain no reports, and README.md (1850) gains only five reports of class L10 (a nested list directly after its item's text), all in this entry. None of these files is a paper surface.

## Round 593: Proposition 3′ for the curve step in Lean, pointwise in the heights (`external/pnt/SieveTypeII.lean`; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §§8–10, M3)

**What it is.** Milestone M3 of the first goal (SIEVE-ROUTE.md §§9–11): Proposition 3′ of §10, the Type II estimate at small heights, for the curve step of §12 at `L = 2333/1000`, pointwise in the heights.

**The theorem.** `SieveTypeII.typeII_step`: let `L = 2333/1000`, let `f0` be smooth and real with support in `[1/2, 2]`, and take `K₀ ≥ 0`, `e₁ > 0` and `0 < η ≤ 10⁻⁵`. For every large `q`, every `P` with `q^{(401/1000)L} ≤ P ≤ q^{(485/1000)L}`, every `S ⊆ (P, 2P]`, `a_m` and `h₀`, every `K ≤ K₀`, and every `Q_j ≥ q^{e₁}` and `|h_j| ≤ q^η` (`j < K`) with `∏_j Q_j ≤ 2^{K₀}q^L/P`:

`Σ_{χ≠1} |Σ_{m∈S} a_mχ(m)m^{−ih₀}| · |∏_{j<K} Σ_{p≤2Q_j} χ(p)(p/Q_j)^{−ih_j}f0(p/Q_j)| ≤ q^{L−1/50000}(Σ_m |a_m|²/P)^{1/2}`.

- With `|a_m| ≤ 1` the right side is at most `x^{1−1/(50000L)}`, `x = q^L`: a power saving.
- The window `[401/1000, 485/1000]` is rational. It lies inside step's proved window `(0.400943, 0.485533)` (rounded inward; §12), so the margins are fixed numbers.
  - The least margin, `5.5·10⁻⁵` in the exponent of `q`, is at `β = 11/12` and the left end of the window.
  - A scratch run of the certificate on this window bounds the loss by `0.871` at `n = 70`, and by `0.8791` with the crude bound for `ω` (both rounded up). The committed certificate does not run this window yet; that is M7's.
- ~~What remains of Proposition 3′ is the integral over the heights against `∏ k′(τ_i)`.~~ *(Round 594: retracted, false when written: more remains. Proposition 3′ as stated takes coefficients bounded by `τ(m)^C`, which needs a divisor-moment bound for `Σ_m |a_m|²/P`, and heights up to `JT₀`, which needs `JT₀ ≤ q^η`, that is `ε₂ < η/(2L)` in §10's parameters. One weight `f0` for all the prime sums suffices for §10's use; review F-1.)* What remains of Proposition 3′ includes the integral over the heights against `∏ k′(τ_i)`. A bound that holds at every point of the support needs only the measure's total mass, `≪ (log x)^J`.

**The proof.** It follows §10.

- **(T1).** `Σ_χ |Σ_{j∈S} c_jχ(j)j^{−it}|² ≤ (P + q)Σ_{j∈S} |c_j|²` for `S ⊆ (P, 2P]` (`sum_chars_dp_sq_le`). The sum over `χ` is at most `φ(q)Σ_a |D_a|²` over the classes mod `q` (`LinnikHybrid.sum_chars_norm_sq_le` with `dp_twist_eq`). Each class meets `(P, 2P]` in at most `P/q + 1` integers (`card_class_le`), and Cauchy–Schwarz in each class finishes.
- **The bins.** The bin of `χ` is the largest `i < N` such that `L(·, χ)` has a zero with `Re s > β_i` and `|Im s| ≤ T`, or `0` (`bin`). The grid is `β_i = 1/2 + (5/12)(i/500000)`, of width `1/1200000`, and `T = 2q^η + 1`.
  - The bins do not depend on the heights.
  - Above its bin a character has no zero with `Re s > β_{i+1}` and `|Im s − h_j| < q^η + 1`. In the last bin the stack's half-plane `Re s > 11/12` takes the place of the bin (`bin_rect`). This is Lemma 1's rectangle.
  - In a bin `i > 0` a character has a zero with `Re s ≥ β_i` and `|Im s| ≤ T` (`card_bin_le`).
- **In each bin.**
  - Lemma 1 (`SieveWeight.norm_Sp_le`) at `θ = β_{i+1}`, `δ = 10⁻⁶` and `H = q^η` bounds each prime sum by `2Q_j^{θ+2δ}` for large `q` (`MB_le`).
    - The decay is chosen with `η·K ≥ (5/12)(L + 1)`. *(Round 594: here `K` is Lemma 1's decay, `Kd` in the file, not the number of prime sums; review F-4.)*
    - The logarithms are absorbed by `Q_j^δ ≥ q^{e₁δ}`.
    - `KL(θ, θ + δ)` is bounded by its sum over the grid.
  - The counts are those of step (`card_zero_step`): `LinnikTwelve.charDensity_twelve_fifths` at `ε = 1/108000` on `[2801/4801, 5/6)`, `LinnikStep.charDensity_step` from `5/6` on, and at most `q` characters below `2801/4801`.
  - Cauchy–Schwarz over the bin with (T1) (`sum_bins_le`, `typeII_pointwise`) then gives a constant times `q^{E + η/2}`, times powers of `log q` and `(Σ|a_m|²/P)^{1/2}` (`bin_bound`).
- **The exponents.** With `P = q^m`, `E = (L − m)(β_i + w) + A(β_i)(1 − β_i)/2 + t`, where `t = (1 + m)/2` when `P ≤ q` and `t = m` when `P ≥ q`.
  - On the window, `E ≤ L − 1/25000` for every bin width `w ≤ 4·10⁻⁶` (`exponent_le`). *(Round 594: `w` is the bin width plus `2δ`, `17/6000000` in use; review F-4.)*
  - On each piece of step `E` is linear in `β` (`nlinarith` with the products of the bounds).
- **The sum.** Over the 500000 bins the constants and the logarithms are absorbed by `q^{3/200000}`, which leaves `q^{L−1/50000}` (`typeII_step`).

**What is checked.**

- `external/pnt/build.sh` lists the file after `SieveWeight`, imports it in the final check and prints the axioms of four of its theorems; `bash -n` passes. The final check, run alone against `build/`, prints 321 axiom lines, all inside the three (12 s). The rest of the layer was not rebuilt.

SIEVE-ROUTE.md (18) and `external/pnt/README.md` (10) gain no reports, and README.md (1860) gains only five reports of class L10 (a nested list directly after its item's text), all in this entry. The float certificate on this window gives `0.8790613232425407` (rounds 593 and 594).

**What the tests say about points.** M8 will need these, so the file proves them for points of the exponent space:

- if a box passes `surelyEval`, every point of it is evaluable, that is, has a sub-sum of its exponents in `U` (`eval_of_surelyEval`);
- a non-evaluable point of the region of depth 2 lies in a candidate cell (`cover2`);
- ~~on a cell that may be decomposed, `α₁ + α₂` and `α₁ + α₂ + α₃` stay at most `1 − u₂` at non-evaluable points, and each non-evaluable `α₃` lies in a counted row~~ *(Round 597: retracted, false when written: `cover3` takes `α₃` in the region of depth 3, and outside it both conclusions fail; review of round 596, finding 1.)* on a cell that may be decomposed, `α₁ + α₂` stays at most `1 − u₂` at non-evaluable points, and each non-evaluable `α₃` of the region of depth 3 keeps `α₁ + α₂ + α₃ ≤ 1 − u₂` and lies in a counted row (`sum_le_of_allowed`, `cover3`);
- a non-evaluable point of depth 4 lies in a counted cell (`cover4`);
- the crude `ω` (`omegaC`), on a cell's arguments widened by `τ < 1/DEN`, is at most the cell's value `omK/2^{60}` (`omegaC_le`). The widening covers the shift `log 2/log x` of M6's argument `log 2y/log z` for large `x`;
- each bound is at least its real counterpart, `h²` (or `h⁴`) times the cell's value of `ω` times `1/(ab²)` (or `1/(abcd²)`) (`bound2_ge`, `bound4_ge`);
- the total is the double sum of the cells' costs (`total_eq`), and a decomposed cell's cost is the sum over its counted cells of depth 4 (`refcost_eq`).

The region's conditions enter as hypotheses in units of `1/DEN`. For example, `cover2` takes `α₁ + 2α₂ < 1 + 1/DEN` and `α₁ < (V + nH)/DEN = 1/2 + 14/DEN`, which the primes' exponents meet for large `x`.

**Findings and dispositions.**

- **F1** (minor). §13's plan for the fundamental lemma combined the upper and lower sieves by `∏_j ρ_j ≥ ∏_j λ_j^+ − Σ_j (λ_j^+ − λ_j^−)∏_{i≠j} λ_i^+` under `λ_j^− ≤ ρ_j ≤ λ_j^+` and `λ_j^+ ≥ 0`. For three or more factors that is false without `ρ_j ≥ 0`: `ρ = (−10, −10, −1)`, `λ^− = ρ`, `λ^+ = 0` gives `−100 ≥ 0`. The telescoping proof needs `∏_{i<j} ρ_i ≤ ∏_{i<j} λ_i^+`. The sieve's `ρ_j` are indicators, so the route is unaffected. The hypothesis was false when written; it is struck and `ρ_j ≥ 0` added. Two siblings in the same bullet are marked:
  - a truncation at `k + 2j` gives one parity in every range, so the upper and lower sieves take `k + 2j` and `k + 2j + 1` (`k` even);
  - the level `w^{2k+4}` is the upper sieve's, and the lower sieve's terms reach `w^{2k+5}`.
- **F2** (minor). §13's M5 read "each term classified by its cell as evaluable, decomposed or dropped (M7)". Evaluability belongs to the point. Over a decomposed cell, a term of depth 3 whose sum lies in `(R, 1 − u₁)` is evaluable, and Proposition 6 cannot decompose it, so it must be evaluated. M7's lemmas are pointwise: a term is evaluable by its point, and otherwise decomposed or dropped by its cell. The clause was false when written; it is struck and annotated.

Struck at both sites.

Each bound is rounded up twice, once for `ω` and once at the end. And `sum_le_of_allowed` needs the point itself to be non-evaluable. ## Round 597: rough numbers from above and the shares of the certificate's cells (`external/pnt/SieveRough.lean`; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §13, M6), and the convergence review of round 596

**What it is.** Two parts.

- Milestone M6 of the first goal (SIEVE-ROUTE.md §13) is proved: rough numbers from above with the crude `ω*`, and the shares of the loss certificate's cells.
- A fresh-context reviewer, the repository's `hostile-reviewer` agent, ran the convergence review of round 596's sweep at 02859af. It found no MAJOR and no minor finding, so that sweep is converged. Its eight cosmetic findings and one observation are swept here.

**The theorems.**

- `SieveRough.psi_le`: for every `U` and `ε > 0` there is `z₀` such that `Ψ(y, z) ≤ (ω*(u) + ε)y/log z` for all `z ≥ z₀`, `y ≥ 1` and `u = log 2y/log z ≤ U`. Here `Ψ(y, z) = #{m ∈ (y, 2y] : p | m ⇒ p ≥ z}`, and `ω*` is `SieveCert.omegaC`: `0` below `1`, `1/u` on `[1, 2)` and `0.5672` from `2` on.
- `SieveRough.share2`: let `cellP x k` be the primes `p` whose exponent `log p/log x` lies in the cell `k` of the certificate's grid (`mem_cellP`, in the terms of `SieveCert.InCell`). For a cell `(i, j)` with `e_i + 2e_j ≤ DEN` and every `δ > 0`, eventually in `x`, `Σ_{p₁ ∈ cellP x i} Σ_{p₂ ∈ cellP x j} Ψ(x/(p₁p₂), p₂) ≤ (bound2(e_i, e_j)/K + δ)x/log x`.
- `SieveRough.share4`: the same at depth 4 with `bound4`, for `e_i + e_j + e_k + 2e_l ≤ DEN`.
- `share2_of_cand` and `share4_of_counted4`: the two on the cells that pass `cand` and `counted4`, whose tests include those inequalities.

`Ψ(x/d, p)` counts the `m` with `dm ∈ (x, 2x]` and no prime factor below `p`. ~~Summed over a cell's primes it is the model's count of the cell's terms, which M8 will drop, and the shares bound it by the certificate's own bounds.~~ *(Round 598: retracted, false when written: the model is `B/φ(q)`, with `B` the `n` prime to `q`, and the sum counts every `n` once for each of its forms `p₁p₂m`; review of round 597, finding 1.)* Summed over all pairs of primes of a cell (at depth 4, all quadruples), it is at least `φ(q)` times the model's count of the cell's terms, by a paper-level step that M8 is to state (SIEVE-ROUTE.md §13, M8). So for a cell whose terms M8 drops, the shares bound the model's count by the certificate's own bounds, divided by `φ(q)`.

**The proof.**

- `theta_near`: `|θ(t) − t| ≤ εt/log t` for all large `t`, from the stack's `ψ(t) − t = O(t^{23/24})` (`HalfPlanePNT.psi_isBigO_eleven_twelfths` at `ε = 1/24`) and Mathlib's `ψ − θ ≤ 2√t log t`.
- Abel summation against `θ`, from above (`abel_le`, on Mathlib's `sum_mul_eq_sub_sub_integral_mul`), gives three prime sums over `(a, b]` (`sum_inv_mul_log_le`, `sum_inv_le`, `sum_inv_mul_sub_log_le`). `card_primes_dyadic` gives `π(2y) − π(y) ≤ (1 + ε)y/log 2y` for large `y`.
- Buchstab's inequality by the least prime factor (`Psi_le_buchstab`): `Ψ(y, z) ≤ #{p : y < p ≤ 2y} + Σ_{z ≤ p ≤ √(2y)} Ψ(y/p, p)` for `y ≥ 2`.
- The induction is on an integer bound `K ≥ u` (`Claim`, `claim_step`, `claim_nat`). Below `u = 1` nothing is counted, and below `u = 2` only primes. Above, the step bounds each `Ψ(y/p, p)` by the hypothesis and sums `ω*((L − log p)/log p)/(p log p)`, `L = log 2y`, over two ranges (`rangeA_le`, `rangeB_le`). On `log p ≤ L/3` it has `ω* = 0.5672`, and on `L/3 < log p ≤ L/2` it has `ω* = log p/(L − log p)`. The sum is `M(u)/L` up to `O(ε)`, with `M(u) = ∫_1^{u−1} ω*`, and `ω*` is a supersolution of the delay equation: `1 + M(u) ≤ 0.5672u` for `u ≥ 2` (`super_M`, from `1 + log(u − 1) ≤ 0.5672u` and `1 + log 2 ≤ 3·0.5672`).
- The shares. At a point of a cell, `psi_le` and `SieveCert.omegaC_le` give `Ψ(x/(dp), p) ≤ (omK/K + ε)x/(dp log p)` (`psi_point`). The widening `log 2/log x` of `omegaC_le` is below `1/DEN` for large `x`. The cells lie below `α₁ + α₂ = 1` and `α₁ + ⋯ + α₄ = 1`, since `e_j ≥ V ≥ 4H` (`four_H_le_V`, by `decide`). Summed over a cell, the bound is a product of the cells' prime sums. For large `x` these are at most `h/a + δ` for `Σ 1/p` and `h/a² + δ` for `log x · Σ 1/(p log p)`, with `h` the side and `a` the lower corner (`evLe_cell_inv`, `evLe_cell_inv_log`). `SieveCert.bound2_ge` and `bound4_ge` then close the bound (`evLe_finish`).

## Round 600: Type II families in Lean (`external/pnt/SieveSep.lean`, `SieveFamily.lean`; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §13, M4), and the convergence review of round 599

**What it is.** Two parts.

- Milestone M4 of the first goal (SIEVE-ROUTE.md §13) is proved: the Type II families of §10's Lemmas 4′ and 4″.
- A fresh-context reviewer, the repository's `hostile-reviewer` agent, ran the convergence review of round 599's sweep at d9c06ab. It found no MAJOR and no minor finding, so round 599's sweep is converged. Its four cosmetic findings are swept here.

**The theorems.**

- `SieveSep.sum_sep`: for continuous integrable `g_j` with integrable `𝓕g_j`, a finite sum `Σ_i w_i ∏_j g_j(ℓ_j(i))` is the integral over `ℝ^J` of `∏_j 𝓕g_j(ξ_j)` times `Σ_i w_i e^{2πiΣ_j ξ_jℓ_j(i)}`. `SieveSep.sep_bound` bounds such integrals, for integrable `h_j` (here the `𝓕g_j`) and integrands `F_x(ξ)` continuous in `ξ`, with `Σ_x |F_x| ≤ B₁` on the box `|ξ_j| ≤ T₀` and `≤ B₂` everywhere, `B₁, B₂ ≥ 0`: by `B₁∏_j ‖h_j‖₁`, plus `B₂` times the tails `Σ_j (∫_{|t|>T₀} |h_j|) ∏_{i≠j} ‖h_i‖₁`.
- `SieveFamily.family_bound` (Lemma 4′ with Proposition 3′). Let `f0` be smooth with support in `[1/2, 2]`, `e₁ > 0` and `0 < η ≤ 10⁻⁵`. A family has `m` over `S ⊆ (P, 2P]` with coefficients `a_m`, where `q^{0.401L} ≤ P ≤ q^{0.485L}`, the window of `SieveTypeII.typeII_step`; `K ≤ K₀` primes `x_i ≤ 2Q_i` with the weights `f0(x_i/Q_i)`, `Q_i ≥ q^{e₁}` and `∏_i Q_i ≤ 2^{K₀}q^L/P`; and `J` continuous integrable `g_j` with integrable `𝓕g_j`, applied to the forms `ℓ_j = φ_j(m) + Σ_i e_{ji} log x_i`. There is `q₀` such that for `q ≥ q₀`, if `2π(Σ_j |e_{ji}|)T₀ ≤ q^η` for each `i`, the sum over `χ ≠ 1` of the family's twisted sums is at most `q^{L−1/50000}(Σ|a_m|²/P)^{1/2} ∏_j ‖𝓕g_j‖₁`, plus the number of characters `χ ≠ 1` times `Σ_m |a_m| ∏_i Σ_p |f0(p/Q_i)|` times `Σ_j (∫_{|t|>T₀} |𝓕g_j|) ∏_{i≠j} ‖𝓕g_i‖₁`.
- `SieveFamily.typeII_sharp_explicit` (Lemma 4″). Let also `0 ≤ f0 ≤ F₀`. Cut a family with `n + 1 ≤ K₀` primes by `J` sharp comparisons `P_j` in place of the `g_j`, where `P_j` holds when `ℓ_j > 0` and implies `ℓ_j ≥ 0`, each with a pivot prime of coefficient `±1`. There is `q₀` such that for `q ≥ q₀`, a unit `a` mod `q`, `0 < θ ≤ 1 ≤ Λ` with `ℓ_j ≤ Λ` on the family, `T₀ ≥ 1`, `k ≥ 2` and `2π(Σ_j |e_{ji}|)T₀ ≤ q^{1/100000}` for each `i`, `|A − B/φ(q)|` is at most an explicit bound in the cut-off's masses and tail (`massB`, `tailB`) and the pivots' counts.
- `SieveFamily.typeII_sharp`. Fix `f0` as above, `K₀`, `J₀`, `e₁ > 0`, `E₀ ≥ 0`, `Λ₀ ≥ 0` and `A₀ ≥ 0`. There are `δ > 0` and `q₀` such that, for `q ≥ q₀` and a unit `a` mod `q`, every sharp family with `|a_m| ≤ A₀` for every `m`, `J ≤ J₀`, `|e_{ji}| ≤ E₀` and `ℓ_j ≤ Λ₀ log q` on the family has `|A − B/φ(q)| ≤ A₀q^{L−δ}/φ(q)`.

The coefficients are bounded by a constant fixed before `q₀`, in place of §13's `τ(m)^C`. M5's families are to have `|a_m| ≤ 1`: in Buchstab's tree the primes of a term are distinct and decreasing, so `m` determines its tuple. §13's marker of this round says so.

**The proof.**

- *Separation* (`SieveSep`). Fourier inversion at a point (Mathlib's `Continuous.fourierInv_fourier_eq`) and over `ℝ^J` (Mathlib's `integral_fintype_prod_volume_eq_prod`). `sep_bound` integrates the pointwise bound `H(ξ)Σ_x |F_x(ξ)| ≤ B₁H(ξ) + B₂Σ_j E_j(ξ)`. Here `H = ∏_j |h_j(ξ_j)|`, and `E_j` is `H` with its `j`-th factor cut to `|ξ_j| > T₀`.
- *`family_bound`.* The separated sum factors into the twisted `m`-sum and the twisted prime sums, which are `SieveWeight.Sp` at the heights `−2πΣ_j ξ_je_{ji}` (`sum_twist_eq`, `inner_factor`). On the box the heights are at most `q^η`, and `typeII_step` bounds the sum over `χ ≠ 1`.
- *The cut-off's mass and tails.* For `SieveSmooth`'s cut-off `G` with `0 < θ ≤ 2Λ`, `‖𝓕G‖₁ ≤ π(2Λ + θ) + c₂/(2πθ)`; for `θ > 0`, `Λ ≥ 0`, `k ≥ 2` and `T₀ ≥ 1`, `∫_{|ξ|>T₀} |𝓕G| ≤ 2π·2θ^{1−k}c_k(2π)^{−k}T₀^{2−k}`. Here `c_k = ‖g^{(k)}‖₁` for Mathlib's `Real.smoothTransition` `g` (`mass_GC_le`, `tail_GC_le`), from `SieveSmooth`'s decay bounds.
- *Orthogonality.* `1[n ≡ a] − 1[(n, q) = 1]/φ(q) = φ(q)⁻¹Σ_{χ≠1} χ(a⁻¹)χ(n)` for a unit `a` (`dw_eq`).
- *Sharp against smooth.* `|∏_j I_j − ∏_j G_j| ≤ Σ_j |I_j − G_j|` for values in `[0, 1]`, and `|1[P_j] − G(ℓ_j)| ≤ G̃(ℓ_j)` with the narrow cut-off `G̃(u) = G_{θ,θ}(u + θ)` (`norm_Dsum_sharp_le`, `abs_ind_sub_G_le`). The near-boundary families are families again. Their sizes are bounded through the pivot: `G̃` confines the pivot prime to a short interval `[Y, e^{3θ}Y]`, which holds at most `(e^{3θ} − 1)R + 1` integers up to `R` (`card_short_le`, `pivot_term_le`, `pivot_sum_le`).
- *`typeII_sharp`.* Take `θ = q^{−ε₂}` with `ε₂ = 1/(400000(J₀ + 1))`, `Λ = Λ₀ log q + 1`, `T₀ = q^{1/200000}` and `k = 1200003`. The masses are at most `Cq^{ε₂}`, the tails at most `c′q^{−3}`, and the box and the pivots' counts at most constants times `A₀q^L`. So the three terms are at most `A₀q^L/φ(q)` times `a₁q^{−7/400000} + a₂q^{−1} + a₃(12q^{−ε₂} + q^{−e₁})`. That is at most `q^{−δ}` with `δ = min(ε₂, e₁)/2` once `q^δ ≥ a₁ + a₂ + 13a₃` (`bracket_le`).

## Round 604: Linnik's theorem with exponent `2333/1000` in Lean (`external/pnt/SieveBrun.lean` … `SieveMain.lean`, 21 files; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §13, M5 and M8)

**What it is.** Milestones M5 (the sieve) and M8 (the assembly) of the first goal (SIEVE-ROUTE.md §13) are proved, in 21 new files of `external/pnt`. With the milestones that rounds 588–600 landed (§13's Done: M1s, M2, M3, M4, M6, M7 and the cut-off of Lemma 4′) ~~they prove the theorem of SIEVE-ROUTE.md §0 at `x = q^{2.333}`~~ *(Round 605: retracted, false when written: `SieveMain.linnik_large` stated `p ≤ 2x` only, without the lower end of §0's theorem; round 605 states `x < p ≤ 2x`, so they now prove the theorem of §0 at `x = q^{2.333}`; review of round 604, finding 1.)* they prove Linnik's theorem with exponent `2333/1000`. That completes the first goal of SIEVE-ROUTE.md §11, the owner's "formalise 2.333". Round 603's cosmetic sweep rides with this round's review.

**The theorem.** `SieveMain.linnik_2333`: there is `K` such that for every `q ≥ 1` and every `a` prime to `q` there is a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` with `p ≤ K·q^{2333/1000}`. `#print axioms` gives `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. ~~For `q ≥ q₀` the prime lies in `(⌊q^L⌋, ⌊2q^L⌋]`, `L = 2333/1000` (`SieveMain.linnik_large`).~~ *(Round 605: retracted, false when written: `linnik_large` stated `p ≤ 2q^L` only; its proof had the lower end and dropped it. Round 605 states it, so `linnik_large` now gives, for `q ≥ q₀`, a prime in `(q^L, 2q^L]`; review of round 604, finding 1.)*

It rests on the stack's own inputs, which earlier rounds proved: the zero-free half-plane `Re s > 11/12` for Dirichlet `L`-functions (`Eis.LFunction_ne_zero_of_re_gt`, `src/DirichletCharHalfPlane.lean`) and the density estimates `LinnikTwelve.charDensity_twelve_fifths` and `LinnikStep.charDensity_step`, through `SieveTypeII.typeII_step` (round 593); the prime number theorem with error `O(x^{11/12+ε})` (`HalfPlaneFinal`), through `SieveRough`; and the certificate `SieveCert.total_le` (round 595). For the finitely many `q` below `q₀` it also uses Mathlib's Dirichlet theorem, `Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_modEq`.

**The proof.** Each file's header states its main theorems, and most headers give the steps of their proofs; `external/pnt/README.md` has a row for each file and two sections.

- *The sieve (M5).* Brun's sieve in product form (`SieveBrun.fundamental`) at the ranges `[w^{2^{−j−1}}, w^{2^{−j}})` (`SieveRanges`), with Type I's counts (`SieveCount`), gives each leaf of Buchstab's tree (`SieveLeaf.leaf_A` and `leaf_B`, in `SieveProp6.leaf_bound`). Type II with sharp prime ranges removes `SieveFamily.typeII_sharp`'s dyadic weights (`SieveTypeIIU`, `SieveTypeIIR`). Buchstab's tree over finite sets (`SieveTree`) gives Proposition 6 (`SieveProp6.prop6`): one tree at the threshold `X' = ⌊q^{b₀}⌋` for every `r ≤ X'`, whose stops have their cofactors in the lower window (`SieveStops2.stops2_bound`) and whose leaves take the fundamental lemma.
- *The assembly (M8).* Type II for a chain of primes and the rough rest of `n`, in either window (`SieveChain`). Families of prime tuples cut out by atoms, with Buchstab's identity, cells, splits and vanishing (`SieveDecomp`). §6's decomposition to depth 4 as exact identities, each family classified by its cells as `SieveCert` classifies them, gives `S(A, z_top) ≥ S(B, z_top) − (dropped) − C·Err` (`SieveBuch.Par.decomp`). At `x = q^L`, for `η > 0` there are `δ > 0` and `q₀` such that every leaf is within `ηq^L/(φ(q) log q) + q^{L−δ}/φ(q)` for `q ≥ q₀` and `a` a unit mod `q` (`SieveLeaves`, `SieveQ.leaves_ev`). For `ε > 0` and large `q` the dropped terms' `B`-count is at most `φ(q)⁻¹(0.88 + ε)x/log x`, by M6's shares and M7's total, with the corner `o(x/log x)` (`SieveDrop.drop_ev`), and `S(B, z_top) ≥ φ(q)⁻¹((1 − ε)x/log x − q)` (`SieveMain.TB_ev`). So `S(A, z_top) ≥ 0.07x/(φ(q) log x) > 0` for large `q`, and a `z_top`-rough `n ∈ (N₁, N₂]`, `z_top = ⌊√N₂⌋ + 1`, is prime. The smaller `q` take a prime from Mathlib's `Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_modEq`.

**As built, against the plan** (SIEVE-ROUTE.md §13's markers of this round).

- Proposition 6 runs one tree at `X'` in place of §5's two cases. §5's first case is proved (`SieveStops1.stops1_bound`, `window_bound`) and not used.
- Lemma 5 is not stated on its own: Type I enters through the leaves' counts.
- Each term is classified by its cell, not by its point: evaluated when its cell is inside the window (depth 1), surely evaluable, or split at `X'` with the term above it; otherwise decomposed, dropped or zero by its cell. The evaluable points of a dropped cell are dropped with it, as the certificate's costs count them.
- The corner: the cells that are neither candidates nor surely evaluable, below a cell of `p₁` outside the window, count only `n = p₁p₂` with both primes in `(z_top/4, z_top]`.
- The small `q` take a prime from Mathlib's Dirichlet theorem, not as `linnik_of_charDensity` handles them.

**What is checked.**

The files have 9718 lines. No file reported an error or a warning; `SieveMain.lean` prints its own `#print axioms` line, `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. No file has a `sorry`, `native_decide` or `axiom`. Two declarations carry `set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in`: `SieveProp6.prop6` and `SieveChain.chainTL_bound`.

## Round 607: the second goal's phase 1 in Lean, Linnik's exponent `229/100` with Chen–Gupta–Li's estimate as a hypothesis (`external/pnt`, eight new files and fifteen changed; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §14)

**What it is.** The second goal of SIEVE-ROUTE.md §11, the owner's "push on using the 7/3 result", has its phase 1 in Lean.

- `Linnik229.linnik_229` gives Linnik's theorem with exponent `229/100`. Its one hypothesis is Chen–Gupta–Li's zero-density estimate on `[5/7, 16/21]`, stated as `LinnikCGL.CGLDensity`.
- For it the sieve route of round 604 takes its numbers as parameters, and `SieveMain.linnik_2333` is re-derived as an instance.
- Phase 2 is to prove `CGLDensity`.

**The theorem.** `Linnik229.linnik_229`: if `CGLDensity` holds, there is `K` such that for every `q ≥ 1` and every `a` prime to `q` there is a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` with `p ≤ K·q^{229/100}`. `#print axioms` gives `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

- `CGLDensity` says: for every `ε > 0` there is `C` such that for every `q ≥ 1`, `5/7 ≤ σ ≤ 16/21` and `T ≥ 2`, at most `C(qT)^{(7/3)(1−σ)+ε}` characters mod `q` have a zero of `L(·, χ)` in `Re s ≥ σ`, `|Im s| ≤ T`.
- It is a definition, and the theorems that use it take it as an argument; it is not an axiom.
- `LinnikCGL.lean`'s header quotes the first sentence of Chen, Gupta and Li's abstract (arXiv:2507.08296v2) and says how their bound gives `CGLDensity`. The quotation was checked against the abstract returned by arXiv's API for 2507.08296v2, in its LaTeX source.

**The proof.** SIEVE-ROUTE.md §14 gives it in full; each file's header states its main theorems.

- *The route with parameters.* M4–M8 take a route (`SieveRoute.Route`: `L`, `w₁`, `w₂`, with `RouteOK`), its Type II estimate (`SieveRoute.TypeIIAt`), a grid of the certificate (`SieveCert.Grid`, with `GridOK`) and the fit between them (`SieveQ.Fits`). `SieveMain.linnik_route` gives Linnik's theorem with exponent `L` from these and a certificate's total at most `0.88K`. `linnik_2333` is its case at `route2333` and `grid2333`; its statement is unchanged.
- *The density inputs.* `LinnikIngham73.charDensity_ingham73` (D1), `7/3 + 4ε` on `1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 5/7`, is round 524's Ingham argument at `c = 1/12`. `LinnikHuxStep.charDensity_hux73` (D3), `7/3 + 1/2000` on `16/21 ≤ σ ≤ 5/6`, is round 589's step with parameters (`LinnikHuxStep.charDensity_gen`), which also re-derives round 589's `101/50` below `11/12` (`charDensity_step'`). `CGLDensity` (D2) covers `5/7 ≤ σ ≤ 16/21`, and `LinnikStep.charDensity_step` covers `5/6` on.
- *Type II for the curve.* `SieveTypeIIGen.typeII_gen` is Proposition 3′ for a curve whose counts hold and a window whose exponents stay at most `L − 1/25000`. `SieveTypeII73.typeII_73` is its case for the curve `g73` at `L = 229/100` on `[4123/10000, 4902/10000]·L`, under `CGLDensity` (`counts_73`, `window_73`).
- *The certificate.* `SieveCert229.total_le_229`: on the grid of that window with `n = 100` cells a side, the certificate's total is at most `0.88K`, by `decide +kernel`.
- `linnik_229` is `linnik_route` at `route229` and `grid229` (`fits229`), with `typeII229` and `total_le_229`.

**What is checked.**

- `lean` was run on the 33 files from `SieveRoute` to `Linnik229` in `build.sh`'s order, with the build's `LEAN_PATH` (Mathlib at `MATHLIB_REV`) and `build.sh`'s own `lean` options, into `build/`: `SieveRoute` 810 s, `SieveCert` 112, `SieveCert229` 300, `SieveRough` 135, `SieveSep` 17, `SieveFamily` 61, `SieveBrun` 21, `SieveCount` 15, `SieveRanges` 21, `SieveLeaf` 23, `SieveTree` 14, `SieveDyadic` 15, `SieveTypeIIU` 52, `SieveRoughTuple` 21, `SieveTypeIIR` 31, `SieveDiff` 18, `SieveStops1` 17, `SieveCmp` 16, `SieveStops2` 65, `SieveProp6` 77, `SieveChain` 71, `SieveDecomp` 19, `SieveBuch` 19, `SieveLeaves` 15, `SieveQ` 31, `SieveDrop` 25, `SieveMain` 27, `LinnikCGL` 6, `LinnikIngham73` 35, `LinnikHuxStep` 57, `SieveTypeIIGen` 33, `SieveTypeII73` 20, `Linnik229` 16; 2215 s in all. ## Round 609: the stack's unconditional Linnik exponent `232/100` in Lean (`external/pnt`, six new files; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §15)

**What it is.** The owner's standing instruction of 2026-10-20, "pursue any avenue that opens up to further reduce the Linnik exponent", applied to the route of round 607 with the stack's own density arguments: `Linnik232.linnik_232` gives Linnik's theorem with exponent `232/100` and no hypothesis, below round 604's `2333/1000`.

- The density inputs are staircases of two parametric arguments the stack already has: Ingham's below `3/4`, now with the detector's `c` free (`LinnikInghamC`), and round 589's step on `[3/4, 5/6]` with round 607's parameters (`LinnikHuxStep.charDensity_gen`), twenty steps in all (`LinnikStairs`); `101/50` from `5/6` on is round 589's.
- The curve's counts and window are glued from the pieces (`SieveCurveGlue`), the window checked at the corners of each piece (`SieveTypeIIU232.window_U`).
- The certificate is at `n = 150`, in 25 kernel checks of consecutive rows (`SieveCert232`): one check of the whole grid needs more memory ~~than the machine has~~ *(Round 617: retracted, false when written: than the shell tool's memory cgroup allows, 13.36 GiB in the present container, the machine having 16; review of round 616, F1.)*.

**The theorem.** `Linnik232.linnik_232`: there is `K` such that for every `q ≥ 1` and every `a` prime to `q` there is a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` with `p ≤ K·q^{232/100}`. `#print axioms` gives `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**The proof.** SIEVE-ROUTE.md §15 gives it; each file's header states its theorems.

- *Ingham with `c` free* (`LinnikInghamC.charDensity_ingham_c`). For `0 < ε ≤ 1`, `0 ≤ c ≤ 1`, `δ₀ > 0` and `σ₂ ≤ 11/12` with `(4/3)(1 + 2c)(1/2 − σ₂) + 1 ≤ (2 + 4c)(1 − σ₂)`: the exponent `2 + 4c + 4ε` on `1/2 + δ₀ ≤ σ ≤ σ₂`. The integral class at `Y = Q^{1+2c}` is `Q^{(4/3)(1+2c)(1/2−σ)+1+ε/3}`, within the polynomial class's `Q^{(2+4c)(1−σ)}` exactly when `2 + 4c ≥ 3/(2 − σ)`, Ingham's curve; the inequality at `σ₂` gives it below `σ₂`, the two sides' difference increasing in `σ`. Round 607's `LinnikIngham73.count_middle73`, its middle range `4/7 ≤ σ ≤ 5/7`, is the case `c = 1/12`, `δ₀ = 1/14`, `σ₂ = 5/7` of `count_middle_c`; `charDensity_ingham73` adds the trivial count below `4/7` and has its own constant *(round 610: it read "`LinnikIngham73` is the case"; review of round 609, F7)*.
- *The staircases* (`LinnikStairs`). Ten equal steps from `b₀ = 2801/4801 = 1 − 1/(12/5 + 1/2000)` to `3/4`, each with the exponent `3/(2 − σ₂) + 1/2000` at its right end (`charDensity_in0` … `in9`); ten equal steps from `3/4` to `5/6`, each with `3/(3σ₁ − 1) + 1/2000` at its left end, at parameters `parHx0` … `parHx9` found by a linear program and verified exactly (`charDensity_hx0` … `hx9`). Every step is above its curve by `1/2000`, so the staircase lies within `1/2000 + (the step's rise)` of `min(3/(2 − σ), 3/(3σ − 1))`.
- *Gluing* (`SieveCurveGlue`). `RangeCounts g lo hi` and `WindowPiece g L m₁ m₂ lo hi` are `CurveCounts` and `WindowOK` on a range; both glue across a point for a curve written as nested `if`s. On a range where the curve is affine the window's inequalities hold if they hold at the corners `β ∈ {lo, hi}`, `m ∈ {m₁, 1, m₂}`, `w ∈ {0, 4·10⁻⁶}`, each side being affine in each variable separately (`windowPiece_affine`).
- *The curve and Proposition 3′* (`SieveTypeIIU232`). `gU` is `1` below `b₀`, the twenty steps, and `(101/50)(1 − σ)` from `5/6` on; `counts_U` glues the trivial count, the twenty steps and `LinnikStep.charDensity_step`; `window_U` checks twenty-two pieces at their corners by `norm_num`; `typeII_232` is `SieveTypeIIGen.typeII_gen` at `L = 232/100` on `[4045/10000, 4825/10000]·L`.
- *The certificate* (`SieveCert232`). `grid232` is the window's grid with `n = 150`. `rows a b` sums the rows `a ≤ i < b`; `total_eq_rows_of` writes the total of any grid with `n = 150` as the sum of 25 parts of consecutive rows, by `Finset.sum_Ico_consecutive`, the parts grouped by the kernel's work; `rows_0` … `rows_24` bound each part by `decide +kernel`, one at a time (`Elab.async false`), at about `0.1%` above a scratch replay's values; the bounds sum to ~~`0.8516K ≤ 0.88K`~~ below `0.8517K`, so at most `0.88K` (`total_le_232`) *(Round 633: retracted, false when written: "`0.8516K`", the sum rounded down; review of round 631, F-B.)*.
- `linnik_232` is `linnik_route` at `route232` and `grid232` (`routeOK232`, `fits232`, `typeII232`, `total_le_232`).

**What sets the number.** With these inputs the certificate's bound (scratch, crude `ω`) on the window `[4045/10000, 4825/10000]` is `0.9371` at `L = 2.32`, `n = 100`; `0.8508` at `n = 150` (the replay of the Lean's arithmetic: `0.85078K`, 4244 candidate cells, 2047 decomposed, 28853 of depth 4); `0.8136` at `n = 200`. On the windows `sieve_route_certificate.py` computes, `2.315` gives `0.8637` at `n = 200` and `2.31` `0.8953` at `n = 300`. The route's threshold `0.88K` and the kernel's memory set `232/100` at `n = 150`; on the window the certificate computes, `2.315` passes from `n = 190` on (`0.8759`; `0.8637` at `n = 200`), but that window's corners fail `WindowOK`'s margin by `4.3·10⁻⁵`, and on `[4058/10000, 4813/10000]`, whose corners pass, `n = 200` gives `0.8828` *(round 610: it read "`2.315` needs `n = 200`, about three times the kernel's work, and a window whose corners pass"; review of round 609, F5)*. A kernel check of the whole grid at `n = 150` was killed at ~~13 GB of the machine's 16~~ *(Round 616: retracted, false when written: a watcher's KiB figure converted by hand, and the limit is ~~the container's memory cgroup's (13.36 GiB in the present container)~~ *(Round 617: retracted, false when written: the shell tool's memory cgroup's (`…/claude-code-bash`, which holds `lean` and the shell's other children; the container's own cgroup is unlimited), 13.36 GiB in the present container; review of round 616, F2.)*, not the machine's; the kernel's log of that kill is no longer available; review of round 615, O1.)*, and so was a file whose parts ran together under asynchronous elaboration; one at a time, a part of 15 heavy rows took 7.4 GB, and the kernel frees a part's memory before the next, so the parts are grouped by their predicted work (scratch: a fit to two measured parts).
