## Round 612: Linnik's exponent `227/100` under Chen–Gupta–Li's estimate and Petrow–Young's bound, in Lean (`external/pnt`, six new files; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §17)

**What it is.** The first of §16's avenues, under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-20: `Linnik227.linnik_227` gives Linnik's theorem with exponent `227/100` under two displayed hypotheses, `LinnikCGL.CGLDensity` (round 607) and `LinnikWeyl.PYWeyl` (Petrow–Young's Weyl bound for every character).

- The Weyl bound empties the detector's integral class (`LinnikWeyl.class2_empty`), so round 607's step runs with the detector's height as a parameter and no fourth moment (`LinnikHuxStepY.charDensity_genY`), giving Huxley's uncapped curve `3/(3σ − 1)` above `5/6`.
- Sixty steps (`LinnikStairs7`), the glued curve and window at `L = 227/100` (`SieveTypeIIU227`), the certificate at `n = 100` (`SieveCert227`) and the assembly (`Linnik227`).
- Three scratch agents built the files from the lead's design (the emptiness lemma; the step with the height as a parameter; the numerics); the lead integrated, generated the staircase, curve, certificate and assembly files from the numerics, compiled everything, and verified the numbers it records (below).

**The theorem.** `Linnik227.linnik_227`: if `CGLDensity` and `PYWeyl` hold, there is `K` such that for every `q ≥ 1` and every `a` prime to `q` there is a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` with `p ≤ K·q^{227/100}`. `#print axioms` gives `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

- `PYWeyl` says: for every `ε > 0` there is `C ≥ 0` such that for every `q ≥ 1`, every `χ` mod `q` and every real `t`, `‖L(1/2 + it, χ)‖ ≤ C(q(1 + |t|))^{1/6+ε}`. Petrow and Young prove it for primitive characters (Duke Math. J. 172 (2023), Theorem 1.1, quoted in SIEVE-ROUTE.md §16); the extension to every character by the finite Euler product is the lead's remark in §17, standard and not formalized. It is a definition, and the theorems that use it take it as an argument; it is not an axiom.

**The proof.** SIEVE-ROUTE.md §17 gives it; each file's header states its theorems.

- *The integral class* (`LinnikWeyl`). Under the bound at one `ε ≤ 1` with constant `CL`, `‖I_χ(ρ)‖ < 1/4` for every `χ ≠ 1` with a zero `β + iγ`, `σ ≤ β < 1`, `|γ| ≤ T`, once `2·KG·CL·X·(q(T + 2))^{1/6+ε} < δY^{σ−1/2}` (`1/2 + δ ≤ σ`): `LinnikHuxley.class2_count_small`'s integral estimate with the pointwise bound in place of the convexity bound. The design said `4/(3π)`; at `ε ≤ 1` the integrated weight is `(1 + |v|)^{−23/6}`, not `(1 + |v|)^{−4}`, and the constant is `2` (the agent's correction, verified by the lead).
- *The step* (`LinnikHuxStepY`). `ParY` is `Par` with the height's parameter `cy` (`y = (1 + 2cy)/2000`); `ParY.Good` replaces `201/200 + ε ≤ lam` by `2y + ε ≤ lam` and the fourth-moment condition `h3` by `h5 : 1/6 + 2ε + 1/2000 ≤ y(lo − 1/2)`; `charDensity_genY` under `PYWeyl`. At `lo = 5/6` the conditions force `A ≥ 4y + 2ε ≥ 2.00626`, so `3/(3σ₁ − 1) + 1/2000` is attainable only from ~~`σ₁ ≈ 0.8365`~~ *(Round 613: retracted, false when written: `σ₁ ≈ 0.8362` for this exponent; `0.8365` is the crossing without the `1/2000`; review of round 612, F3.)* on (the agents' correction of §16's bookkeeping; verified by the lead).
- *The staircase* (`LinnikStairs7`): twenty Ingham steps on `[4/7, 5/7]`, twenty Huxley steps with the fourth moment on `[16/21, 5/6]` and twenty under the bound on `[5/6, 11/12]`, each `1/2000` above its curve except the first above `5/6` (`50159/25000`), at parameters found by a linear program and checked in rational arithmetic (scratch); above `11/12` at most one character is counted (the half-plane), which extends the last step to `σ ≤ 1`.
- *The curve, window and Proposition 3′* (`SieveTypeIIU227`): 62 pieces; `CGLDensity` at `ε = 1/8400` as the counts of `(7/3 + 1/2000)(1 − σ)` on `[5/7, 16/21]`; the window `[4048/10000, 4858/10000]`, 744 corners by `norm_num`; `typeII_gen`.
- *The certificate* (`SieveCert227`): `grid227` with `n = 100`, `total_le_227` by one `decide +kernel`.
- `linnik_227` is `linnik_route` at `route227` and `grid227`.

**What sets the number.** With 20 steps per staircase the certificate's bound (scratch, crude `ω`) is `0.8442` at `n = 100` (the replay of the Lean's arithmetic: ~~`0.84421K`~~ below `0.84422K` *(Round 633: retracted, false when written: "`0.84421K`", the total rounded down; review of round 631, F-B.)*, 1854 candidate cells, 877 decomposed, 6398 of depth 4) and `0.7692` at `n = 150`; the window's lower end is set by the `11/12` end (`0.40472`), its upper end by `A_max = 7/3 + 1/2000`. At `226/100` the bound is `0.8479` at `n = 200` (`0.9918` at `n = 100`): ~~the next step needs about sixteen times the kernel's work~~ *(Round 613: retracted, false when written: with these 20-step staircases; with 80 steps above `5/6` the bound is `0.8794` at `n = 150`, below `0.88`; review of round 612, F2.)*. The `16/21` and `11/12` ends tie at `L = 2.2525`.

## Round 614: Linnik's exponent `226/100` under the same two hypotheses, the certificate at `n = 200` in 49 kernel parts (`external/pnt`, nine new files; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §18)

**What it is.** Round 612's route one hundredth lower: `Linnik226.linnik_226` gives Linnik's theorem with exponent `226/100` under `LinnikCGL.CGLDensity` and `LinnikWeyl.PYWeyl`, on round 612's curve `g7` with its counts `SieveTypeIIU227.counts_7`. ## Round 618: the external build recompiles only what changed, and the certificate's definitions leave Mathlib (`external/pnt/build.sh`, `SieveCertDefs.lean`; the held cosmetics of round 617)

**Why.** The owner's direction of 2026-10-21: fix the build first, since it speeds everything after it. Two findings of the stack analysis (task 427, in progress) are build-level: `external/pnt/build.sh` recompiled all 148 modules on every run, so a run after an unchanged landing re-ran every kernel check (the 226 chain's five part files alone took 52 minutes in round 614, `SieveCert232` 14 to 20 in rounds 609 and 617); and every certificate's kernel check ran in a process that had loaded Mathlib's whole environment through `import Mathlib`, which the definitions it computes with do not need.

**What changed.**

- **The incremental rule** (`external/pnt/build.sh`, its `c`). A module is compiled only if its olean is missing or older than its source or than the olean in `build/` of a module it imports (one of the pilot's, PNT+'s or this directory's; an import with no olean under `build/`, Mathlib's, is not compared), one module at a time as before; `FORCE=1` compiles every module. This is the rule of the pilot's `build.sh` since round 217. The script prints `== M` before compiling `M` and `-- M: Ns` after, then the counts compiled and up to date, and the final check runs every time. A compile that fails now removes the module's olean and ilean, so a later run does not take a partial output for fresh. Only the modules compiled in a run are gated; the final check gates the theorems.
- **`SieveCertDefs.lean`** (new): the 28 definitions of the certificate (`DEN` … `total`; `SieveCert.lean` lines 47–153 at 182641c), round 609's `rows` (`SieveCert232.lean` lines 28–29) and the class `GridOK` (`SieveCert.lean` lines 189–195), moved verbatim (`rows` takes the section's `[Grid]` for its own binder; `GridOK`'s docstring is rewrapped and names `SieveCert.lean`). The file imports only `Mathlib.Data.Nat.Notation`, ~~which imports nothing,~~ *(Round 619: retracted, false when written: its first ~~line~~ *(round 620: import, at line 8; review of round 619, F7)* is `public import Mathlib.Init`, whose closure is 1,339 modules, loaded in about 0.9 GiB; the lead's grep for `^import` missed the `public import`; review of round 618, F1.)* for the notation `ℕ`. `SieveCert.lean` imports it and Mathlib and keeps the lemmas; `rows_eq` moves there from `SieveCert232.lean` (lines 32–34). `SieveGrid226.lean` imports `SieveCertDefs` instead of `SieveCert232`, so the five part files `SieveCert226P1` … `P5`, which import the grid and nothing else, run their kernel checks without Mathlib's environment; `SieveCert226.lean` imports `SieveCert` for `total_eq` and `rows_eq`. The lead's check that the moves are verbatim: `python3 $S/r618/verbatim_check.py` (scratch), which compares the blocks against `git show HEAD:…` line by line and confirms that every other line of `SieveCert.lean` at 182641c survives in order (its output is in `$S/r618/verbatim_check.out`).
- **What leaving Mathlib buys, measured** (scratch, `$S/r618/scr_test2.log`; peaks are the largest `ps -o rss=` sample, in KiB, converted by the script). Part 7 of the 226 certificate (`rows 28 29`, one row) checked alone in a file importing the new `SieveGrid226`: 43 s, peak 2,953,652 KiB (2.82 GiB); the same file importing the old `SieveGrid226` olean (through `SieveCert232` and Mathlib): 52 s, peak 8,651,720 KiB (8.25 GiB). ## Round 619: the certificate's loss as a parameter, so `total < K` suffices (`SieveDrop.lean`, `SieveMain.lean`; `SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §19); the sweep of round 618's review (F1–F5 minor, F6–F13 cosmetic)

**The threshold was a convention.** In `SieveMain.linnik_large` every loss but the certificate's is a parameter the proof sets to `1/100` of `X = x/log x` (`TB_ev`'s `ε`, `drop_ev`'s `ε`, the leaves' error through `η = 1/(100·C_dec·L)`, and `q ≤ X/100`), and the closing step keeps `7X/100`. The stack analysis (task 427; its three judges and the lead, who read `linnik_large` lines 213–300 and `drop_ev` 714–756 at 182641c) found the `0.88` to be slack: with `c := total/K < 1` and the losses set to shares `ε = (1 − c)/10` of `X` (five: `TB_ev`'s, `drop_ev_of`'s, two for the leaves' error, `q ≤ εX`; *round 620: "four losses" corrected, review of round 619, F6*), `(1 − c)X/2` remains. Round 619 lands that: `SieveDrop.sum_cost_div_of` and `drop_ev_of` take `total/K ≤ c` in the reals (`htot`); `SieveMain.linnik_large_of` and `linnik_route_of` take `c < 1` and set `ε = (1 − c)/10`, `η = ε/(C_dec L)`, `ev_log_le` at `ε/(C_dec L)` and `ε/L`; `SieveDrop.total_div_lt` turns `total < K` into `total/K < 1` (`div_lt_one K_pos'`, then `exact_mod_cast`; *round 620: `Nat.cast_lt` is not in the source, review of round 619, F7*); `SieveMain.linnik_route_lt` is Linnik's theorem with exponent `L` under the route's Type II estimate and `total < K`. The `0.88` forms (`sum_cost_div`, `drop_ev`, `linnik_large`, `linnik_route`) are one-line corollaries with their statements byte-identical to 9acd586's (the diff), so `linnik_2333`, `linnik_229`, `linnik_232`, `linnik_227` and `linnik_226` are untouched. `build.sh`'s final check prints `linnik_route_lt`'s axioms (443 lines). The `ring` at `SieveMain.lean:145` (`have : xq q = (q^{L/2})^2`), which fell back to `ring_nf` with a message (round 618's observation), is `ring_nf`; the build prints nothing but axiom lines. What the change opens is in §19 of SIEVE-ROUTE.md (on the lead's scratch certificates: unconditional `231/100` at `n = 200`, `2255/1000` under the two hypotheses; with the Halász–Montgomery Type II bound of the analysis, unconditional `229/100` at `n = 150`); none is landed here.

## Round 621: Linnik's exponent `230/100` with no hypothesis — the Halász–Montgomery bound per bin in Proposition 3′ (`external/pnt`, seven new files; `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §20)

**What it is.** The stack analysis of task 427 (its merged proposal M-2) found, and the lead verified before this round (`scratchpad/stack/verify_M2/`, `scratchpad/lower/lead_notes.md` §12), that Proposition 3′'s bin-wise orthogonality bound can be replaced, bin by bin, by the Halász–Montgomery bound the stack proves since round 525 (`LinnikPower.hm_duality` with the kernel bound `LinnikOffDiag.norm_offK_le`), which is the better bound where the bins are sparse, at the top of the curve, so that the `11/12` end of the curve stops binding the Type II window. On round 609's unconditional curve `gU` this moves the exponent from `232/100` (`n = 150`, 25 kernel parts) to `230/100` at `n = 100` in one kernel check, under the `0.88K` form of the route; and it opens `Linnik226` without `PYWeyl` on its landed certificate (a later round, task 432).

**The theorem.** `Linnik230.linnik_230`: there is `K` such that for every `q ≥ 1` and every `a` prime to `q` there is a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` with `p ≤ K·q^{230/100}`, with no hypothesis. `#print axioms` gives `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

**The proof.** SIEVE-ROUTE.md §20; each file's header states its theorems, and the external README's round-621 section lists them.

- *The bin bound.* For a bin `R` of characters at one height, `SieveHMBin.sum_bin_hm` is `hm_duality` at `σ = 0`, `β_χ ≡ 0`, `γ_χ ≡ h₀`, `Λ = 2P`: `(Σ_{χ∈R} |W(χ)|)² ≤ e·Σ|a|²·(|R|·2P + |R|²B)` with `B` a bound on `|K_{2P}(ψ, 0)|` for `ψ ≠ 1` (`SieveHMBins.offK_bound`, `norm_offK_le` at `δ = ε′ = 1/1000`). `SieveHMBins.sum_typeII_bins_hm` takes the smaller of this and orthogonality's `|R|^{1/2}((P + q)Σ|a|²)^{1/2}` for each bin (`binTerm`).
- *The window condition.* `SieveHMWindow.WindowOKHM g L m₁ m₂ d e`: at each `(β, m, w)` either `WindowOK`'s inequality or, for `m ≤ 1`, the two bilinear inequalities of `hmBound` (the `|R|Λ` and `|R|²B` terms' exponents, `(L − m)(β + w) + gβ/2 + m` and `(L − m)(β + w) + gβ/2 + m/2 + (gβ + 5/12 + m/12 + d(1 − m) + 2e)/2`, each at most `L − 1/25000`). Pieces glue and lift as round 609's; an affine piece holds by the branch if its inequalities hold at the corners of the box (`affine_corner_bound`, round 609's `key` as a lemma; `windowPieceHM_affine`, `windowPieceHM_affine_split`, `windowPieceHM_const_split`).
- *Proposition 3′.* `SieveTypeIIHM.bin_bound_gen_hm` bounds `Mp · binTerm` by `C′(1 + log qT)^{10} q^{L − 1/25000 + η}(V/P)^{1/2}`, `C′ = 2√3·e^{1/2}C₀C_d^{1/2} + 6e^{1/2}C₀C_dC_K^{1/2}`, in the orthogonality case by `bin_bound_pt` (round 607's `bin_bound_gen` at one point *(round 622: it read "round 609's"; review of round 621, F2)*) and in the Halász–Montgomery case by splitting the second term with `√(x + y) ≤ √x + √y`; `typeII_gen_hm` is `typeII_gen`'s statement with `WindowOKHM g L m₁ m₂ (1/1000) (1/1000)`, its proof with `sum_typeII_bins_hm`, `bin_bound_gen_hm` and `500000·C′(1 + log qT)^{10} ≤ q^{1/100000}` for large `q`.
- *The window* `[3944/10000, 4780/10000]` at `L = 230/100` (`SieveTypeIIU230.window_230`): the piece `1` and twenty of `gU`'s steps by orthogonality at their corners (round 609's tactic `corners`), the top piece `(101/50)(1 − σ)` on `[5/6, 11/12]` by `windowPieceHM_const_split` at its 24 corners (`cornersHM`), all by `norm_num`. The lead's exact-rational check of every corner (`scratchpad/r621/corners230.py`): least slack `3.98·10⁻⁵` below `L − 1/25000` on `[3/4, 91/120]` at `m = m₂`, `w = 4·10⁻⁶`; the top piece's 24 corners' slack at least `0.0158` (its 16 Halász–Montgomery inequalities' at least `0.0241`; the least is at an orthogonality corner, `m = m₂`) *(round 622: it read "the Halász–Montgomery corners' slack at least `0.0158`"; review of round 621, F3)*; at `β = 11/12`, `m = m₁` orthogonality alone fails by `0.0146`, so the branch is needed there. `typeII_230` is `typeII_gen_hm` at `gU`, `counts_U` and `window_230`.
- *The certificate*: `grid230` with `n = 100`; the replay of `SieveCert`'s arithmetic (`scratchpad/stack/land230/replay230_n100.json`) gives the total `956276356674239363 = 0.82944K` (1808 candidate cells, 821 decomposed, 5594 of depth 4); `total_le_230` is one `decide +kernel`, the file importing `SieveCertDefs` only.

This round ~~computes them in exact arithmetic with a committed script~~ computes them with a committed script, the certificates and the corners in exact arithmetic and the fits and the window's scan in floating point *(Round 627: retracted, false when written: "computes them in exact arithmetic"; review of round 626, F1.)*, and records each figure with its status in SIEVE-ROUTE.md §23. **The results** (SIEVE-ROUTE.md §23; `route_limits.jsonl`, 36 rows *(round 629: 37 since round 628; review of round 628, finding 3)*).

- *No hypothesis* (`gU`): exact certificates (window corners, grid, route and `total < K` in exact arithmetic; the kernel's run not made) at `2282/1000` (`n = 600`: `0.99177K`), `22825/10000` (`n = 600`: `0.98057K`), `2285/1000` (`n = 250`: ~~`0.98833K`~~ below `0.98834K` *(round 628: added; review of round 627, finding 5)*; `n = 300`: `0.96309K`; `n = 400`: `0.94152K`; `n = 600`: ~~`0.92021K`~~ below `0.92022K`), `229/100` (`n = 150`: ~~`0.93914K`~~ below `0.93915K`; `n = 200`: ~~`0.89776K`~~ below `0.89777K`) *(Round 633: retracted, false when written: "`0.98833K`", "`0.92021K`", "`0.93914K`" and "`0.89776K`", the totals rounded down; review of round 631, F-B.)*. **The script.** `frontier/linnik/route_limits.py` computes, for a curve, an exponent and a grid size, the window by round 621's sampled scan; its corner inequalities in exact rationals, as `windowPiece_one`, `windowPiece_const` and `windowPieceHM_const_split` state them (an end moves inward by `10⁻⁵` while a corner at it fails; no row needed a move); and `SieveCertDefs.lean`'s certificate in exact integers, with `GridOK`, `Fits` and `RouteOK`. ## Round 635: the plan for Chen–Gupta–Li's estimate in Lean (`frontier/linnik/CGL-LEAN.md`)

**The instruction.** The owner asked whether Chen–Gupta–Li's bound had been formalized in Lean by its authors or anyone else, and then, on 2026-10-22: "Formalise it in lean". Two of the lead's web searches of that day are recorded here: "Lean 4 formalization zero density estimate Dirichlet L-functions Chen Gupta Li 7/3" and "Guth Maynard large values estimate formalized Lean". Neither found a formalization of either estimate. The nearest result was D. Loeffler and M. Stoll, "Formalizing zeta and L-functions in Lean" (arXiv:2503.00959), which formalizes the basics of `ζ` and of Dirichlet `L`-functions in Mathlib, with no zero-density estimate among them.

**The plan** (`frontier/linnik/CGL-LEAN.md`, new; it records no result).

- The target is `LinnikCGL.CGLDensity`. Of it, `Linnik225C.linnik_225c` and `Linnik226C.linnik_226c` use one count, through `SieveTypeIIU227.rangeCounts_cgl` at `ε = 1/8400`: `RangeCounts (fun σ => 14003/6000·(1 − σ)) (5/7) (16/21)`.
- A dependency map of the paper's results (arXiv:2507.08296v2), with the stack's modules that prove part of each.
- Five stages:

  - **M1:** that count from a displayed large-values hypothesis, Theorem 1.1's form at `q₁ = q` for primitive characters on the line.
  - **M2:** Theorem 1.1 from Proposition 3.1.
  - **M3:** Proposition 3.1 from its sockets.
  - **M4:** Proposition 8.1.
  - **M5:** Heath-Brown's Theorem 10.1.

- **Feasibility.** The two parts read first were the paper's §8.2 (the proof of Lemma 8.2), read in full, and Heath-Brown's theorem.

  - §8.2's tools are elementary: Plancherel, Poisson summation, the Ramanujan-sum bound, lattice-point counts and Cauchy–Schwarz. The lead found no Weil or Kloosterman bound in it.
  - Heath-Brown's 1979 paper could not be obtained. B. Kerr's arXiv:1909.12075 proves its `q = 1` case in a more general form (Theorem 16, §§5–6, read), with van der Corput's B-process as its one deep input. The version with characters needs a reflection with characters in its place.

- **M1's arithmetic.** With `V ≍ N^σ` and the power trick's `(qT)^{7/9} ≤ N ≤ (qT)^{7/6}`, `parHux73`'s values, each of the four terms of Theorem 1.1 is at most `(qT)^{(7/3)(1−σ)}` on `[5/7, 16/21]`. Two terms are equal to it at `σ = 5/7`, and the first at every `σ`. So M1 needs only the existing framework's internal `ε`.

## Round 636: Chen–Gupta–Li's density step from their large-values estimate (stage M1; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLLV.lean`, `LinnikCGLStep.lean`, `LinnikCGLLinnik.lean`)

**The owner's decision** (2026-10-22): "Let's pause the convergence reviews and run one when we have a more substantial block to review. They are slowing the process too much." So no convergence review ran on rounds 634 and 635, and none runs on this round. The hostile reviews are batched: one review will cover rounds 634–636 and the stages that follow, once a substantial block is done, and those rounds are not stable until it converges. CLAUDE.md is unchanged. `frontier/linnik/CGL-LEAN.md`'s line on reviews carries a net-state marker.

**The result.** Stage M1 of `frontier/linnik/CGL-LEAN.md`:

- `LinnikCGLLV.CGLLargeValues`, a hypothesis: Chen–Gupta–Li's Theorem 1.1 (arXiv:2507.08296v2), its second bound, at one point per character. For every `ε > 0` there is `C ≥ 0` such that, for `q ≥ 1`, `T ≥ 1`, `N ≥ (qT)^{2/3}`, `V > 0` and `|a_n| ≤ 1`, at most `C(qTN)^ε B(q, T, N, V)` distinct primitive characters mod `q` have `|Σ_{N<n≤2N} a_nχ(n)n^{it_χ}| ≥ V` at a point `|t_χ| ≤ T`, where `B = N²V⁻² + (qT)^{1/2}N³V⁻⁴ + q^{4/3}TN²V⁻⁴ + qTN^{12/5}V⁻⁴`.
- `LinnikCGLStep.charDensity_cgl`: under `CGLLargeValues`, at most `C(qT)^{(7/3+1/2000)(1−σ)}(log qT)^{10}` characters mod `q` have a zero in `Re s ≥ σ`, `|Im s| ≤ T`, for `5/7 ≤ σ ≤ 16/21` and `T ≥ 2`. This is the count that `Linnik225C.linnik_225c` and `Linnik226C.linnik_226c` take from `LinnikCGL.CGLDensity` (round 635).
- `LinnikCGLLinnik.linnik_225c_lv` and `linnik_226c_lv`: Linnik's theorem with the exponents `9/4` and `226/100` under `CGLLargeValues`, through the routes, windows, grids and certificates of rounds 625 and 622.

So the two exponents rest on the paper's large-values estimate in place of `CGLDensity`, a consequence of its density estimate (Theorem 1.2). §12 opens: "The aim of this section is to establish Theorem 1.2 with the aid of our new large value estimate, Theorem 1.1." Stages M2–M5 are to derive Theorem 1.1.

**Why the paper's theorem implies the hypothesis.** Theorem 1.1 and §1.1, re-read this round in the text layer (`scratchpad/cgl/work/cgl_v2.txt`; spaces restored, the displayed formulas transcribed):

- "where χ is a primitive character modulo q and |a_n| ≤ 1. Suppose that W is a finite set of pairs (t, χ), where |t| ≤ T and for (t, χ) ≠ (t′, χ′) either χ ≠ χ′ or |t − t′| ≥ 1."
- "In all cases, we have |W| ≤ (qT)^{o(1)}(N²V⁻² + (qT)^{1/2}N³V⁻⁴ + q^{4/3}TN²V⁻⁴ + qTN^{12/5}V⁻⁴)."
- "Asymptotic quantities such as o(1) are interpreted as qT → ∞."

Distinct characters with one point each form such a `W`, since every two of its pairs differ in the character. For `qT` above a bound that depends on `ε`, the factor `(qT)^{o(1)}` is at most `(qT)^ε ≤ (qTN)^ε`. Below that bound at most `q` characters count, and `B ≥ N²V⁻² ≥ 1` once one does, since `|D_N| ≤ N` gives `V ≤ N`. The factor `(qTN)^ε` in place of `(qT)^ε` makes the hypothesis weaker; the step needs no more. `LinnikCGLLV.lean`'s header gives the argument.

**The step** (`LinnikCGLStep`). It is round 607's step (`LinnikHuxStep`) with Chen–Gupta–Li's estimate in place of Huxley's. Its block bound, `block_bin_cgl`, makes the plan's four reductions:

- to primitive characters (`LinnikCGLLV.cgl_all`): a character with conductor `d` factors through a primitive character mod `d`, with the coefficients `a_n1_{(n,q)=1}`, and the divisors of `q` cost `C(ε)q^ε`;
- to the line (`taylor_pick`, `cgl_shift`): `n^{−δ} = N^{−δ}e^{−δ log(n/N)}`, and the Taylor polynomial of degree `K − 1` leaves some `k < K` at the threshold `V/2`; the step takes `K_T = ⌈log 8Q³⌉ + 1`;
- to dyadic pieces: the power `F^m`, normalised at the bin's `σ_b`, cut into `m + 1` pieces;
- to `|a_n| ≤ 1`: the coefficients of `F^m`, at most `d(n)^{2m}`, scaled by `τ₀^{2m}`, `τ₀ = C(ε_d)Q^{2ε_d}`, `ε_d = εs/(1600M)`.

`piece_le` bounds a piece by `8CE·Q^{A_i(1−σ)}` under eight exponent conditions, the four terms of `B` at `N = Q^λ` and at `N = Q^a`, and `parCGL_good` proves them at `parHux73`'s values (`M = 1556`, `a = 7/9 + 2εs`, `λ = 7/6 + 9εs/2`, `A_i = 7/3 + 25εs`) on `[5/7, 16/21]`. In `class1_cgl` the losses of the reductions, with `cgl_shift` at `ε = εs/400`, are at most `E·Q^{εs/4}`, `E = 16(M + 1)⁴C_τ`. Below `3/4` the integral class takes `δ = 1/5` (round 607 takes `1/4`, which needs `σ ≥ 3/4`), so `ParC.Good` asks `7/10 ≤ lo`, and the polynomial class has `⌊60/εs⌋ + 1` bins of width `εs/200`. The plan's M1 text named the four reductions, left the two classes below `3/4` to be re-checked, and stated the hypothesis with `(qT)^ε`; `frontier/linnik/CGL-LEAN.md` records the stage as done.

**What is checked.**

**Why the step needs only the proposition.** Round 636's block bound applied the count at each bin's threshold `W_j/2 = N_j^{σ_b}/Z`, `σ ≤ σ_b < 1`, so `V` ran up to `N_j/Z`; `piece_le` then bounded the result by the bound at `N_j^σ/Z`, since the bound decreases in `V`. **Why the paper's proposition implies the hypothesis.** §3's opening, Proposition 3.1, the split and §1.1, re-read this round in the text layer (`scratchpad/cgl/work/cgl_v2.txt`; spaces restored, the displayed formulas transcribed):

- "Throughout the paper we fix a smooth function w : ℝ → ℝ≥0, supported on [1, 2], such that ‖w^{(j)}‖∞ = O_j(1) for all j ∈ ℕ and w(t) = 1 for t ∈ [6/5, 9/5]."

## Round 638: Chen–Gupta–Li's Proposition 3.1 from a bound on the cubic trace (stage M3, first step; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLMat.lean`)

**The result.** `LinnikCGLMat.prop31_of_third` proves `LinnikCGLLV.CGLProp31`, round 637's hypothesis, from `LinnikCGLMat.CGLThird`, a bound on the off-diagonal of the cubic trace. `linnik_225c_third` and `linnik_226c_third` give the exponents `9/4` and `226/100` under `CGLThird`.

- The matrix of the points: `A_{i,n} = w(n/N)χ_i(n)n^{it_i}` for the integers `⌈N⌉ ≤ n ≤ ⌊2N⌋`, with `w` Mathlib's `ContDiffBump` at `3/2` with radii `3/10` and `1/2`: smooth, `0` outside `(1, 2)` and `1` on `[6/5, 9/5]`, as the paper's §3 asks. `X` is the real part of `Σ G(i, j)G(j, k)G(k, i)` over the triples of `R` that are not all equal, `G = AA*`, whose diagonal is the constant `μ = Σ w(n/N)²` over the `n` prime to `q`.
- `CGLThird`: for every `ε > 0` there is `C ≥ 0` such that, for `q ≥ 1`, `T ≥ 1`, `7/10 ≤ σ ≤ 4/5`, a real `N` with `(qT)^{2/3}/2 ≤ N ≤ qT`, `S ⊆ [6N/5, 9N/5]`, `|b_n| ≤ 1` and distinct primitive characters `χ_i` mod `q` with `|Σ_{n∈S} b_nχ_i(n)n^{it_i}| ≥ N^σ/6` at points `|t_i| ≤ T`, `X ≤ C(qTN)^ε(N³ + (qT)²|R|^{3/2} + qT|R|N^{3−2σ} + qT|R|²N^{3/2−σ} + (qT)^{9/8}|R|^{29/16}N^{3/2−σ})`.
- The proof. `prop46` is the paper's Proposition 4.6 for the points: either `|R|N^{2σ} ≤ 648N²` or `(|R|N^{2σ})³ ≤ (216N)³X`, from round 537's `LinnikMoment.refined_moment_cube` (`refined_moment_points`). With `CGLThird`, `alg112` solves for `|R|` (the paper's §11.2), one case per term. Two of the cases give `|R|` at most a constant times `qTN^{9/2−7σ}` and `(qT)^{18/19}N^{(72−112σ)/19}`, terms the paper's proof shows are dominated; `dom4` and `dom5` bound each by `(qT)^{1/2}N^{3−4σ}` for `N ≥ (qT)^{5/6}` and by `(qT)^{4/3}N^{2−4σ}` for `N ≤ (qT)^{5/6}`, for every `N > 0` and `7/10 ≤ σ ≤ 4/5`. For `N > qT`, which `CGLThird` does not cover, the mean value theorem at one point per character (`mvt_case`, from `LinnikPoints.large_values_points`) gives `|R|N^{2σ} ≤ 36N²(11 + 8 log N)(2 + log²(2N))` for `N ≥ 10`, and `polylog_le` bounds the logarithms by `(11 + 24/ε)(2 + 36/ε²)N^ε` for `0 < ε ≤ 1`. For `qT < N < 10` at most `q < 10` characters count.

So stage M3's target is now `CGLThird`, the bound on `X` that the paper's Lemma 4.5 and §§5–11 give.

**Why the paper implies the hypothesis.** Re-read this round in the text layer (`scratchpad/cgl/work/cgl_v2.txt`; spaces restored, the displayed formulas transcribed):

- The proof of Lemma 4.5: "Now we take out Z, the term coming from (t₁, χ₁) = (t₂, χ₂) = (t₃, χ₃)", with "Z = |W|(N/q Σ_{m∈ℤ} Σ_{a mod q, (a,q)=1} e_q(am)ĥ₀(Nm/q))³"; "We further separate the terms with m⃗ = 0, which gives tr((MM∗)³) = Z + Z′ + Σ_{m⃗∈ℤ³∖{0}} I_m⃗"; and of Z′: "Since Σ_{a mod q} χ(a) = 0 unless χ = χ₀, we have that χ₁ = χ₂ = χ₃."
- The proof of Lemma 4.4: "tr(MM∗) = Σ_{(t,χ)∈W} Σ_{(n,q)=1} w(n/N)² = |W| Σ_{(n,q)=1} h₀(n/N)".
- (5.2): "Σ_{m⃗∈ℤ³∖{0}} I_m⃗ = S₁ + S₂ + S₃"; the proof of Proposition 5.1: "Thus we may restrict to the case χ₁ = χ₂ = χ₃."
- "Proposition 6.1 (S₂ bound). We have S₂ ⪅_ϵ qT|W|N^{3−2σ}."
- "Proposition 11.1 (S₃ bound). Let (qT)^{2/3}/2 ≤ N ≤ qT. Then we have S₃ ⪅ (qT)²|W|^{3/2} + qT|W|N^{3−2σ} + qT|W|²N^{3/2−σ} + (qT)^{9/8}|W|^{29/16}N^{3/2−σ}."
- §11.2: "|W|³N^{6σ−3} ≪_ϵ N³ + S₁ + S₂ + S₃ ⪅_ϵ N³ + (qT)²|W|^{3/2} + qT|W|N^{3−2σ} + qT|W|²N^{3/2−σ} + (qT)^{9/8}|W|^{29/16}N^{3/2−σ}."

Their matrix (4.1), `M_{(t,χ),n} = w(n/N)χ(n)n^{it}` for `n ∼ N`, is `A` up to a zero column (`n = N` when `N` is an integer, where `w(1) = 0`), so `MM*` is `G`. `Z` is the part of the trace from the triples that are all equal, `|R|μ³` by Lemma 4.4. At one point per character, `χ₁ = χ₂ = χ₃` makes the three points equal, which the triples of `Z′` and of `S₁` exclude, so `Z′ = S₁ = 0` and `X = S₂ + S₃`, which §11.2's display bounds for large `qT`. The hypothesis has `(qTN)^ε` for `(qT)^ϵ`, which is weaker since `N ≥ 1/2`, and holds for every `qT ≥ 1`: for bounded `qT`, `|R| ≤ q` and `|X| ≤ |R|³(N + 1)³` are bounded while `N³ ≥ 1/8`. `LinnikCGLMat.lean`'s header gives the argument.

**The paper's ranges.** §4 closes with "so we suppose that (qT)^{2/3} ≤ N ≤ qT (as we have already assumed that (qT)^{2/3} ≤ N)", while Propositions 3.1 and 11.1 take `N ≥ (qT)^{2/3}/2`, and §11.2 states its dominance "For (qT)^{2/3} ≤ N ≤ (qT)^{5/6}". The hypothesis follows Propositions 3.1 and 11.1. `dom4` and `dom5` hold for every `N > 0`, so the stack's form of §11.2 uses no lower bound on `N`. When M3 proves `S₂` and `S₃`, the range `[(qT)^{2/3}/2, (qT)^{2/3})` is to be checked in the proofs of Propositions 6.1 and 11.1.

## Round 639: the off-diagonal of the cubic trace as Chen–Gupta–Li's `S₂ + S₃` (stage M3, second step; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLS23.lean`)

**The result.** `LinnikCGLS23.third_of_s23` proves round 638's hypothesis `LinnikCGLMat.CGLThird` from two hypotheses, one for each of the paper's Propositions 6.1 and 11.1; `linnik_225c_s23` and `linnik_226c_s23` give the exponents `9/4` and `226/100` under the two.

- `X3_eq`: with `E` the off-diagonal part of the points' Gram matrix `G` and `μ` its constant diagonal, `X = 3μ‖E‖_F² + tr(E³)` exactly, where `‖E‖_F² = Σ_{i≠k}|G(i, k)|²` (`frobOff`) and `tr(E³)` is the real part of the sum of `G(i, j)G(j, k)G(k, i)` over the triples of distinct points (`tri3`). A triple that is not all equal has two equal points in one of three positions, where `G(i, i)G(i, k)G(k, i) = μ|G(i, k)|²` because `G` is Hermitian, or has none.
- `CGLS2`: for every `ε > 0` there is `C ≥ 0` such that, under the conditions of `CGLThird`, `‖E‖_F² ≤ C(qTN)^ε·qT|R|N^{2−2σ}`.
- `CGLS3`: likewise `S₃ ≤ C(qTN)^ε((qT)²|R|^{3/2} + qT|R|N^{3−2σ} + qT|R|²N^{3/2−σ} + (qT)^{9/8}|R|^{29/16}N^{3/2−σ})`, where `S₃ = X − 3μ₀‖E‖_F²` and `μ₀ = (φ(q)/q)N∫w²`, the integral over `[1, 2]`, outside which `w` vanishes.
- `third_of_s23`: `X = 3μ₀‖E‖_F² + S₃`, `0 ≤ μ₀ ≤ N` (`mu0_nonneg`, `mu0_le`), and `qT|R|N^{3−2σ}` is one of the four terms, so `X ≤ (3C₂ + C₃)(qTN)^ε(N³ + …)`.

**Why the paper implies the two.** Re-read this round in the text layer (`scratchpad/cgl/work/cgl_v2.txt`; spaces restored, the displayed formulas transcribed):

- The proof of Proposition 6.1, after "By symmetry and the orthogonality of characters" and the terms with `χ₁ = χ₃`: "we find that the terms with t₁ ≠ t₃ contribute O_ϵ((qT)^{−10}) in total. The condition on the sum over W now becomes (t₁, χ₁) ≠ (t₂, χ₂). At one point per character `χ₁ = χ₃` forces `t₁ = t₃`, so the terms with `t₁ ≠ t₃`, which the error term bounds, do not occur. For each pair the sum factors as `F(1, 2)F(2, 1)` with `F(1, 2) = Σ_{m≠0} Σ_a χ₁χ̄₂(a)e_q(am)ĥ_{t₁−t₂}(Nm/q)`, the right side of (6.1) at `t = t₁ − t₂`, `χ = χ₁χ̄₂` without its term `m = 0`, which vanishes for `χ₁ ≠ χ₂`. With `h_t(u) = w(u)²u^{it}`, the left side of (6.1) is `(q/N)N^{−i(t₁−t₂)}G(1, 2)`, so `F(1, 2)F(2, 1) = (q/N)²|G(1, 2)|²` and `S₂ = 3μ₀‖E‖_F²` with `μ₀ = φ(q)Nĥ₀(0)/q`, `ĥ₀(0) = ∫w²`. With round 638's `X = S₂ + S₃` at one point per character, `S₃ = X − 3μ₀‖E‖_F²`. Proposition 6.1 gives `CGLS2`, since `μ₀ ≥ (3/5)(φ(q)/q)N` (`w = 1` on `[6/5, 9/5]`) and `q/φ(q) ≪_δ q^δ` for every `δ > 0`; Proposition 11.1 gives `CGLS3`. For bounded `qT` both sides are handled as in round 638: the left sides are bounded and vanish for empty `R`, and for `R` not empty the right sides are at least a positive constant, since `N ≥ 1/2`. `LinnikCGLS23.lean`'s header gives the argument.

## Round 640: the Mellin transform of `w²`, and the Gram entries as vertical integrals (stage M3, third step; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLMellin.lean`)

**The result.** The first piece of the proof of round 639's hypothesis `CGLS2` (the bound on `‖E‖_F²`), following the route of Chen–Gupta–Li's Proposition 6.1:

- `exists_H_bound`: the Mellin transform `H(s) = ∫w(u)²u^{s−1} du` of `w²` satisfies `(1 + |t|)^{K+3}|H(σ + it)| ≤ B` for every `K ≥ 0` and `S ≥ 0`, some `B`, every real `t` and `|σ| ≤ S`.
- `differentiable_H`: `H` is entire.
- `perron_gram`: for `N > 0` and `σ > 1`, with `ψ = χ_iχ̄_k` and `τ = t_i − t_k`, `G(i, k) = N^{iτ}·(1/2π)∫ L(σ + iv, ψ)H(σ + iv + iτ)N^{σ+iv} dv`.

These are the paper's starting points for its Lemma 6.2: "Let H(s) := ∫_ℝ w(u)²u^{s−1} du be the Mellin transform of w², which is entire and satisfies (6.2) |H(s)| = |∫_0^∞ w(u)²u^{σ+it−1} du| = |∫_ℝ w(e^v)²e^{v(σ+it)} dv| ≪_{σ,j} |t|^{−j}", and, by Mellin inversion, "q/N^{1+it} Σ_{n∈ℤ} w(n/N)²χ(n)n^{it} = … = q/N^{1+it} · 1/2πi ∫_{2−i∞}^{2+i∞} H(s)N^sL(s − it, χ) ds" (re-read this round in the text layer, lines ~~1366–1412~~ 1366–1428 *(Round 647: retracted, false when written: the quotation's last display is at lines 1422–1428; review of rounds 640–644, F8.)*; spaces restored, the displays transcribed and the intermediate step elided). The stack's form is the same integral after `s ↦ s + iτ`.

**How.** The pieces were in the stack. Round 591's `SieveWeight` bounds the Mellin transform of a smooth weight on `[1/2, 2]` by the Fourier transform in `v = −log u` and its derivatives in `v`, for `0 ≤ σ ≤ 2`; the far line that `CGLS2` will need has `σ` negative, so `exists_bound_iteratedDeriv_gE` redoes the derivative bound for `e^{−σv}w(e^{−v})²` on `|σ| ≤ S`. Round 591's `SieveLemma1.perron_weight` is Perron's formula for a weight; `perron_Wt` applies it to `W_τ(u) = u^{iτ}w(u)²`, whose Mellin transform is `H(s + iτ)`, with `L(s, ψ)` for the L-series, and `gram_eq_tsum` writes `G(i, k)` as `N^{iτ}Σ_n ψ(n)W_τ(n/N)` (the conjugate of `n^{it_k}` is `n^{−it_k}`, and `n^{iτ} = (n/N)^{iτ}N^{iτ}`).

**The plan from here.** `CGLS2` follows the paper's proof of Proposition 6.1 at one point per character. The integral in `perron_gram` moves to `Re s = 1/2`; there `L(s, ψ) = E(s)L(s, ψ*)` with `ψ*` primitive and `E(s) = ∏_{p|q}(1 − ψ*(p)p^{−s})`, and round 526's `LinnikGammaRatio.LFunction_eq_reflect` gives `L(s, ψ*) = Φ(s)L(1 − s, ψ⁻¹)`, the dual series being over the imprimitive `ψ⁻¹ = χ̄_iχ_k` mod `q`. The dual series splits at `Z ≈ (qT)^{1+ε}/N`: the first `Z` terms stay on `Re s = 1/2`, where `|EΦ|` is bounded, and form a Dirichlet polynomial in the point `k` with coefficients that depend only on `i` and the height; the rest moves to a far line `Re s = −K`, where it is negligible once `K` is large in terms of `ε`, `E(s)`'s growth `q^K` there being cancelled by `N^{−K}Z^{−K}`. Keeping `E(s)` rather than expanding it over the divisors `d` of `q` keeps one truncation for all pairs: a term with `d > N` would need `Z` of size `q²T/N`. The mean value theorem with the large polynomial put back (round 526's product trick, `LinnikWeighted.huxley_core`) then bounds the sum over `k`. The far line needs a bound for the Gamma ratio there, by moving `Γ`'s argument right, as round 526's `LinnikGammaRatio.norm_Gamma_half_ratio` does by one step.

## Round 641: the reflection of the Gram entries (stage M3, fourth step; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLReflect.lean`)

**The result.** `LinnikCGLReflect.gram_reflect`: for `χ_i ≠ χ_k`, with `ψ = χ_iχ̄_k` and `τ = t_i − t_k`, every `Z ≥ 0` and `K ≥ 1`, the Gram entry `G(i, k)` is `N^{iτ}/2π` times

- `∫ H(s + iτ)N^sE(s)Φ(s)Σ_{m≤Z}ψ⁻¹(m)m^{s−1} dv` on `s = 1/2 + iv`, plus
- `∫ H(s + iτ)N^sE(s)Φ(s)Σ_{m>Z}ψ⁻¹(m)m^{s−1} dv` on `s = −K + iv`,

where `Φ` is round 526's reflection factor `f^{1/2−s}ε(ψ*)·γ_{ψ*⁻¹}(1 − s)/γ_{ψ*}(s)·∏_{p|q}(1 − ψ*⁻¹(p)p^{s−1})⁻¹` of the primitive character `ψ*` mod `f` inducing `ψ`, and `E(s) = ∏_{p|q}(1 − ψ*(p)p^{−s})`. `reflect_gram` is the identity for the integral itself, for any character `χ ≠ 1` mod `q`. On the far line `norm_Phi_le_far` gives `|Φ(s)| ≤ f^{1/2−Re s}·π·CGK(K)(1 + |Im s|)^{1/2−Re s}·EQh(q)` on `−K ≤ Re s ≤ 1/2`, `EQh(q) = ∏_{p|q}(1 − p^{−1/2})⁻¹`.

**The paper's route and the stack's.** Re-read this round in the text layer (lines 1415–1545; ~~spaces restored~~ spaces restored, the display (6.3) written on one line *(Round 647: retracted, false when written: the declaration omitted the display's transcription; review of rounds 640–644, F7.)*): their proof of Lemma 6.2 writes the smoothed sum as "q/N^{1+it} · 1/2πi ∫_{2−i∞}^{2+i∞} H(s)N^sL(s − it, χ*)∏_{p|q,p∤q*}(1 − χ*(p)/p^{s−it}) ds" (their (6.3)), shifts to `Re s = −1`, applies the functional equation of `L(s − it, χ*)` there, writes `L(1 − s + it, χ̄)` as its first `M` terms and the rest, and concludes by "shifting the contour of the integral involving terms with m ≤ M to Re(s) = 1/2, while shifting the integral involving terms with m > M to Re(s) = −2k for a large k ∈ ℕ". The stack moves the integral to `Re s = 1/2` first, where `L(s, χ) = Φ(s)L(1 − s, χ⁻¹)E(s)`; there the dual series splits into its first `Z` terms and the rest, an entire function, which moves to `Re s = −K`, where it is the tail of the series. Both are exact; the two right sides agree.

**The bounds the shifts need.** Each shift is round 472's `SmoothPerron.verticalIntegral_shift` for an integrand that is at most `M(1 + |Im s + τ|)^{−2}` on a closed strip (`shift_of_bound`). On `1/2 ≤ Re s ≤ 2` the integrand `L(s, χ)H(s + iτ)N^s` is bounded by round 254's `PsiOmega.norm_LFunction_leC`, `|L(s, χ)| ≤ (q + 1)|s|/Re s`, and the decay of `H` (round 640). On `−K ≤ Re s ≤ 1/2` the reflected integrands need `|Φ|` there: the stack's bound of round 526 covered `−5/16 ≤ Re s ≤ 13/16`, and `norm_Gamma_half_ratio_far` moves the argument `(s + a)/2` of `Γ` right by `K + 1`, `Γ(B)⁻¹ = ∏_{j≤K}(B + j)·Γ(B + K + 1)⁻¹`, before round 526's `norm_Gamma_le_ratio`. The polynomial growth of `Φ`, `E`, `L(1 − s, χ⁻¹)` and the finite sum is absorbed by `H`'s decay to the power `K + 5`.

where `I_H = ∫|H(1/2 + iu)| du`, `L(X)` is round 526's large-sieve factor `LSX`, `H_Z = Σ_{m≤Z}1/m`, `Q₀(q)` is round 642's, and `B` is round 642's tail bound at `|τ| = 2T`. `‖E‖_F²` is round 639's `frobOff`, the quantity of the displayed hypothesis `CGLS2`. With `Z` chosen so that `N′Z` is `qT` times a small power of `qTN`, the first term is `qT|R|N^{2−2σ}` times such a power when `V = N^σ/6`, which is `CGLS2`'s bound; that choice is the next step.

**The paper's route and the stack's.** Re-read this round in the text layer (lines 1645–1960; spaces restored). ## Round 644: round 639's hypothesis `CGLS2` proved (stage M3, seventh step; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLS2.lean`)

**The result.** `LinnikCGLS2.cgls2 : CGLS2`. For every `ε > 0` there is `C ≥ 0` such that, for `χ` injective on `R` *(round 647: and each `χ_i` primitive, a hypothesis of `CGLS2` that the proof does not use; review of rounds 640–644, F11, and review of rounds 634–639, item 3)*, `T ≥ 1`, `7/10 ≤ σ ≤ 4/5`, `(qT)^{2/3}/2 ≤ N ≤ qT`, `S ⊆ [6N/5, 9N/5]`, `|b_n| ≤ 1`, `|t_i| ≤ T` and `|Σ_{n∈S}b_nχ_i(n)n^{it_i}| ≥ N^σ/6` for every `i ∈ R`,

`‖E‖_F² = Σ_{i≠k}|G(i, k)|² ≤ C(qTN)^ε·qT|R|N^{2−2σ}`.

This is Chen–Gupta–Li's Proposition 6.1 at one point per character, the form round 637's `CGLProp31` uses; round 639 made it a displayed hypothesis. With it, `LinnikCGLS2.linnik_225c_s3` and `linnik_226c_s3` give Linnik's exponents `9/4` and `226/100` from `CGLS3` alone, their Proposition 11.1 at one point per character. `CGLS3` stays a displayed hypothesis.

- `H_Z ≤ Z^δ/δ` (`HZ_le`);
- `Q₀(q) ≤ π·CGK(0)·(2^{ω(q)})³` and `2^{ω(q)} ≤ C_δq^δ` (`Q0_le`, `EQh_le`, `two_pow_omega_le`, from ~~round 526's~~ round 527's *(Round 647: retracted, false when written: the lemma is round 527's, in `LinnikTwelveSizes.lean`; review of rounds 640–644, F5.)* `card_powerset_le_divisors` and the stack's divisor bound `card_divisors_le`), which also gives `τ`;
- `|R| ≪_δ P^{1+δ}N^{1−2σ}` from the large values themselves (`card_le`, round 643's `ls_points`);

## Round 645: Chen–Gupta–Li's Lemma 4.3 (1), the first step on the `S₃` side (stage M3; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLFourier.lean`)

**The result.** `LinnikCGLFourier.lemma43`: for every `K` there is `C_K ≥ 0` (`CF K`) such that for all real `τ` and `ξ`,

`(2π|ξ|)^K|ĥ_τ(ξ)| ≤ C_K(1 + |τ|)^K`,

where `h_τ(u) = w(u)²u^{iτ}` (round 640's `Wt τ`, with round 638's `w = wCGL`) and `ĥ` is Mathlib's `𝓕f(ξ) = ∫e^{−2πixξ}f(x) dx`. This is their Lemma 4.3 (1), re-read this round in the text layer (lines 955–964; spaces restored *(round 661: and the hat, the subscripts and the exponents transcribed, here and in the next quotation; review of rounds 645–651, F3(a))*): "For any integer j ≥ 0, ĥ_t(ξ) ≪_j (1 + |t|)^j/|ξ|^j". Their part (2), "ĥ_t(ξ) ≪_j (1 + |ξ|)^j/|t|^j", enters their argument through (5.1) and Lemma 4.5. Each of its uses in the text layer (lines 1172, 1241, 1284, 1695 and footnote 3 at 1822, the census of `grep` for "4.3 (2)" and "(5.1)") concerns two points of one character, so it is not needed at one point per character.

**The proof.** They write: "The proof (cf. [5, Lemma 4.3]) relies on the properties of the function w(u) and repeated applications of integration by parts." The stack makes the integrations by parts explicit. The `k`-th derivative of `h_τ` is `F_k(u) = u^{iτ}Σ_{j≤k}(iτ)^j c_{k,j}(u)` (`hasDerivAt_F`), with `c_{0,0} = w²`, `c_{k+1,0} = c′_{k,0}` and `c_{k+1,j+1} = c′_{k,j+1} + c_{k,j}/u`. The `c_{k,j}` do not depend on `τ`, are smooth, and vanish for `u ≤ 1` and `u ≥ 2` (`cf_props`). Then Mathlib's `Real.fourier_deriv`, `K` times, gives `𝓕F_K(ξ) = (2πiξ)^K ĥ_τ(ξ)` (`fourier_F`). Finally `|F_K(u)| ≤ Σ_j|τ|^j|c_{K,j}(u)|` gives `C_K = Σ_{j≤K}∫|c_{K,j}|`.

**The `S₃` side.** With `CGLS2` proved (round 644), `CGLS3` is the hypothesis left. The paper's route to it, re-read this round (§§4–5, lines 918–1260; §7, 1930–2435; §9, 4343–4613; §11, 5519–5930):

- the Poisson expansion of the Gram entries in residue classes (Lemma 4.5's method), which at one point per character makes round 639's `S3` the paper's `S₃ = Σ_{m_i≠0} I_m`: the terms of (5.2) with a zero `m_i` give `S₁ = 0` and `S₂ = 3μ₀‖E‖_F²`;
- §7's Propositions 7.1 and 7.2, which write `S₃` through `R(v, a) = Σ_{(t,χ)∈W}v^{it}χ(a)` and its smoothing `R̃`;
- §9's moments of `R` (Lemmas 9.1 and 9.2);
- §10's energy bound (Proposition 10.2 from Heath-Brown's Theorem 10.1, a displayed hypothesis until M5);
- §11's assembly (Proposition 11.1 from Proposition 8.1, a displayed hypothesis until M4).

Lemma 4.3 (1) is what the Poisson expansion and §7's truncations of the `m`-sums use.

**An avenue checked and set aside.** With `S₂` proved, a crude bound for `S₃`, `|tr(E³)| ≤ ‖E‖_op‖E‖_F²` with `‖E‖_op` at most the large-sieve factor, would give a large-values estimate `|W| ⪅ N^{2−2σ} + (qT)^{1/2}N^{3−4σ} + qT·N^{5/2−4σ}`. Its third term equals Proposition 3.1's `(qT)^{4/3}N^{2−4σ}` at `N = (qT)^{2/3}`. `scratchpad/r645/crude_density.py` computes the density exponent that the class-I scheme of their §12.3 gives from it:

- powers `D_N^k` with `N^k ∈ [(qT)^a, (qT)^{3a/2}]`, `a ≥ 2/3`;
- the smaller of the mean value theorem and the estimate at each length;
- class II at exponent `2`;
- grids of 401 values of `a` and 301 lengths.

At the seven values of `σ` it prints in `[5/7, 16/21]`, the crude estimate never beats the mean value theorem below `σ = 3/4`, and gives 2.39 and 2.38 at `0.755` and `16/21`, above the `7/3` that `CGLDensity` needs. The same model gives Proposition 3.1 2.3338 at `σ = 5/7` (the stack's `7/3 + 1/2000` there, round 636). So the crude bound does not reach `9/4`, and the route stays the paper's. This is a scoped computation of one scheme, not a barrier claim. *(round 661: the script's output is recorded in `scratchpad/r645/crude_density.out`, rerun unchanged; review of rounds 645–651, F7.)*

## Round 646: the Poisson expansion of the Gram entries in residue classes (stage M3, the `S₃` side; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLPoisson.lean`)

**The result.** `LinnikCGLPoisson.gram_poisson`: for `q ≥ 1`, `N > 0`, any points and `τ = t_i − t_k`,

`G(i, k) = N^{iτ}Σ_{a<q}χ_i(a)conj(χ_k(a))Σ_{m∈ℤ}(N/q)ĥ_τ(Nm/q)e^{2πima/q}`,

with round 638's Gram entry `G(i, k) = Σ_{n∈colsP N}A_{i,n}conj(A_{k,n})`, `A_{i,n} = w(n/N)χ_i(n)n^{it_i}`, and `h_τ(u) = w(u)²u^{iτ}`. On the way: `poisson_scaled`, Poisson summation for `x ↦ g(cx)` with `g` continuous, vanishing outside an interval, and `ξ²|ĝ(ξ)|` bounded; and `sum_colsP_residue`, the regrouping of `Σ_{n∈colsP N}ψ(n)φ(n/N)` by residue classes mod `q`.

**The paper's expansion and the stack's.** Re-read this round in the text layer (lines 965–1075; spaces restored) *(round 661: the display runs to line 1087; the quotation below drops the subscript `n₁∈ℤ` of the second sum (line 1070), and restores the conjugation bars over `χ₂`, which the PDF draws as rules, page 13, `scratchpad/r661/probe/p13_210_280.txt`; review of rounds 645–651, F3(b) and F4)*: their Lemma 4.4's proof ends "We have the result upon performing Poisson summation." Lemma 4.5's proof says "Performing Poisson summation in the n₁-sum gives", followed by a display that reads, on one line, `Σ_{n₁∈ℤ}h_{t₁−t₂}(n₁/N)χ₁χ̄₂(n₁) = Σ_{a₁ mod q}Σ_{n₁≡a₁ mod q}h_{t₁−t₂}(n₁/N)χ₁χ̄₂(n₁) = (N/q)Σ_{a₁ mod q}Σ_{m₁∈ℤ}ĥ_{t₁−t₂}(Nm₁/q)e_q(a₁m₁)χ₁χ̄₂(a₁)`. `gram_poisson` is that display for one entry, with the factor `N^{iτ}` that their display leaves out (it cancels in the cyclic products of the cubic trace). The sum over `a` runs over `0 ≤ a < q`; the terms with `(a, q) > 1` vanish because the characters do.

Their (5.2) splits `Σ_{m⃗∈ℤ³\{0}} I_{m⃗}` as `S₁ + S₂ + S₃`, where "S₁ consists of terms with exactly one nonzero m_i, S₂ consists of terms with exactly two nonzero m_i and S₃ consists of terms with all three m_i being nonzero" (the subscripts transcribed). §7 opens "Let us first recall that" `S₃ = Σ_{m₁,m₂,m₃≠0} I_{m⃗}`, where `I_{m⃗} = N³/q³ Σ_{(t₁,χ₁),(t₂,χ₂),(t₃,χ₃)∈W, not all equal} Σ_{a₁,a₂,a₃ mod q, (a₁a₂a₃,q)=1} χ₁χ̄₂(a₁)χ₂χ̄₃(a₂)χ₃χ̄₁(a₃)e_q(a⃗·m⃗) · ĥ_{t₁−t₂}(Nm₁/q)ĥ_{t₂−t₃}(Nm₂/q)ĥ_{t₃−t₁}(Nm₃/q)`. ## Round 649: the Gram diagonal against its main term, and the condition "not all equal" dropped (stage M3, the `S₃` side; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLDiag.lean`)

**The result.** `LinnikCGLDiag.muP_sub_mu0_le`: for `q ≥ 1` and `N > 0`, `|μ − μ₀| ≤ d(q)B`, where `μ = Σ_{n∈colsP N, (n,q)=1}w(n/N)²` is round 638's Gram diagonal, `μ₀ = (φ(q)/q)N∫w²` round 639's main term, `B = max(2, A₂Z₂)`, `A₂ = CF(2)/(4π²)` and ~~`Z₂ = Σ_{m∈ℤ}|m|^{−2}`~~ *(Round 661: retracted, false when written: as written its term `m = 0` is infinite; review of rounds 645–651, F8.)* `Z₂ = Σ_{m≠0}|m|^{−2}`; so `|μ − μ₀| ≤ C_δBq^δ` for `0 < δ ≤ 1` (`muP_sub_mu0_le_rpow`). And `S3_eq_all`: for `q ≥ 1`, `N > 0` and `χ` injective on `R`,

`S₃ = Re Σ_{i,j,k∈R}F(i, j)F(j, k)F(k, i) − |R|(μ − μ₀)³`,

the sum now over all triples, since `F(i, i) = μ − μ₀` (`Fm_diag`).

**The paper's `Z′` and the stack's.** Re-read this round in the text layer (lines 1990–2025; spaces restored): their §7 drops the condition "not all equal" — "This can be done by removing the terms when (t₁,χ₁) = (t₂,χ₂) = (t₃,χ₃)" — at the cost of their `Z′ = |W|((N/q)Σ_{0<|m|≤(qT)^ϵqT/N}ĥ₀(Nm/q)C_q(m))³` with the Ramanujan sum `C_q(m)`, and then "By Lemma 4.3(1), for m ≠ 0, |ĥ₀(Nm/q)| ≪ q/(N|m|). On the other hand, the arithmetic sum is the Ramanujan sum C_q(m) and |C_q(m)| ≤ (m,q)" (the fraction and subscripts transcribed). At one point per character the dropped terms are `F(i, i)³ = (μ − μ₀)³`, before any truncation in `m`. The stack bounds `μ − μ₀` without Ramanujan sums: by Möbius inversion over the divisors of `q`, `μ − μ₀ = Σ_{d|q}μ(d)(Σ_{n∈colsP N, d|n}w(n/N)² − (N/d)∫w²)`. For `d ≤ N` each bracket is `Σ_{m≠0}(N/d)ĥ₀(Nm/d)` by round 646's Poisson summation along the multiples of `d`, at most `A₂Z₂d/N` by round 645's Lemma 4.3 (1) at `K = 2`; for `d > N` at most one multiple of `d` lies in `(N, 2N)`, outside which `w(n/N) = 0`. Their bound gives `|Z′| ⪅ |W|`, and this one gives `|R|(μ − μ₀)³ ≤ |R|(C_δBq^δ)³`.

## Round 651: a product of three `ĥ`s as an integral over `(v₁, v₂)` (stage M3, the `S₃` side; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLProd.lean`)

**The result.** `LinnikCGLProd.hhat_prod`: for `τ₁ + τ₂ + τ₃ = 0` and real `ξ₁, ξ₂, ξ₃`,

`ĥ_{τ₁}(ξ₁)ĥ_{τ₂}(ξ₂)ĥ_{τ₃}(ξ₃) = ∫∫v₁^{iτ₁}v₂^{iτ₂}J(v₁, v₂, v₁ξ₁ + v₂ξ₂ + ξ₃) dv₂ dv₁`,

where `h_τ(u) = w(u)²u^{iτ}` (round 640's `Wt`), `ĥ` is Mathlib's Fourier transform `∫e^{−2πiuξ}h(u) du`, and `J(v₁, v₂, λ) = ∫e^{−2πiλu}u²w(v₁u)²w(v₂u)²w(u)² du` (`Jk`). In round 650's `I′(m⃗)` the term of a triple of points `(i, j, k)` carries `ĥ_{t_i−t_j}(Nm₁/q)ĥ_{t_j−t_k}(Nm₂/q)ĥ_{t_k−t_i}(Nm₃/q)`, whose `τ`s sum to `0`. There `J`'s argument is `(N/q)(m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ + m₃)`, and `v₁^{iτ₁}v₂^{iτ₂} = v₁^{it_i}(v₂/v₁)^{it_j}(1/v₂)^{it_k}`.

**The paper's change of variables and the stack's.** Re-read this round in the text layer (spaces restored; the hat, fractions, exponents and subscripts transcribed). Their proof of Proposition 7.1 opens: "Expanding the definition of ĥ as an integral and interchanging the order of summation and integration, one finds" (lines 2067–2068) `I′_{m⃗}` as an integral over `(u₁, u₂, u₃)`. Then "we make the change of variables v₁ = u₁/u₃, v₂ = u₂/u₃, b₁ = a₁a₃⁻¹, b₂ = a₂a₃⁻¹" (lines 2130–2138), with "du₁du₂du₃ = u₃²dv₁dv₂du₃" (lines 2162–2163), and "Since the R factors do not depend on u₃, a₃, performing the u₃ integral and the a₃ summation first yields" their (7.3) (lines 2193–2226). The stack makes the substitution in the product of the three `ĥ`s, for one triple of points, before any sum. The sums over the points and the residues are finite, so at the next step they pass through the integral by linearity, and there the phases and the characters factor. The substitution needs `u₃ > 0`; for `u₃ ≤ 0` the integrand vanishes, since `w` is supported on `[1, 2]`. Fubini is applied to a continuous integrand that vanishes outside `[1, 2] × [1/2, 2] × [1/2, 2]`, the support their remark records: "As w(u) is a smooth bump supported on [1,2], we observe that w(v₁u₃)²w(v₂u₃)²w(u₃)²u₃² vanishes unless v₁, v₂ ∈ [1/2,2]" (lines 2227–2230).

## Round 653: the Ramanujan sum's bound and the decay of `J` (stage M3, the `S₃` side; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLRam.lean`)

**The results.**

- `LinnikCGLRam.norm_Cq_le`: for `q ≥ 1` and `n ∈ ℤ/qℤ`, `|C_q(n)| ≤ d(q)·gcd(n, q)`, with `n` read as its least nonnegative residue and round 652's Ramanujan sum `C_q(n) = Σ_{a∈(ℤ/qℤ)ˣ}e(an/q)`.
- `LinnikCGLRam.Jk_decay`: for every `K` there is `C_K` with `(2π|λ|)^K|J(v₁, v₂, λ)| ≤ C_K` for all real `λ` and `|v₁|, |v₂| ≤ 2`, where `J` is round 651's kernel.
- `LinnikCGLRam.Jk_eq_zero_of`: `J(v₁, v₂, λ) = 0` unless `v₁, v₂ ∈ (1/2, 2)`.

**The paper's inputs and the stack's.** Re-read this round in the text layer (spaces restored; the exponents and subscripts transcribed). Their proof of Proposition 7.1 ends: "As w(u) is a smooth bump supported on [1,2], we observe that w(v₁u₃)²w(v₂u₃)²w(u₃)²u₃² vanishes unless v₁, v₂ ∈ [1/2,2]. Furthermore, its jth derivative with respect to u₃ is bounded by O_j(1). Thus, by repeated integration by parts, the inner integral is O_ϵ((qT)^{−300}) unless |m₁v₁+m₂v₂+m₃| ≤ (qT)^ϵq/N and v₁, v₂ ∈ [1/2,2]. On the other hand, the inner integral is O(1) trivially." It continues with "applying the triangle inequality along with the fact that |C_q(m)| ≤ (m,q)" (lines 2227–2234). `Jk_eq_zero_of` is their first sentence, and `Jk_decay` their second and third, with `K = 0` their "O(1) trivially". The stack makes the uniformity in `(v₁, v₂)` explicit. The weight is `G(v₁u, v₂u, u)` with `G(a, b, c) = c²w(a)²w(b)²w(c)²` smooth with compact support on `ℝ³`, so its `K`-th derivative in `u` is at most `sup‖D^KG‖·‖(v₁, v₂, 1)‖^K ≤ C·2^K`. For the Ramanujan sum the stack proves `d(q)(n, q)`, not `(n, q)`. By Möbius over the divisors of `q`, `C_q(n) = Σ_{d|q}μ(d)(q/d)[q/d | n]`, and each term is at most `(n, q)`. The exact bound needs the signs of `μ`. The extra `d(q) ≤ C_δq^δ` is absorbed by the factor `(qTN)^ε` of round 639's `CGLS3`.

## Round 655: the support of `J` in `v₂/v₁`, and the cyclic symmetry of `I′` (stage M3, the `S₃` side; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLSym.lean`)

**The results.**

- `LinnikCGLSym.Jk_eq_zero_of_ratio`: `J(v₁, v₂, λ) = 0` unless `v₂/v₁ ∈ (1/2, 2)`. On the support of the weight, `v₁u` and `v₂u` lie in `(1, 2)`.
- `LinnikCGLSym.Ip_le_of_bound`: round 654's proof for any majorant. ~~If `|Ψ| ≤ c₀V + E` on `[1/2, 2]²`, with `V ≥ 0` measurable and bounded there, then `|I′(m⃗)| ≤ (N/q)³(c₀∫∫V + (9/4)E)`, the integrals over `[1/2, 2]`.~~ *(Round 661: retracted, false when written: the lemma assumes `N > 0`, and for `N < 0` the right side can be negative; review of rounds 652–657, F1.)* For `N > 0`, if `|Ψ| ≤ c₀V + E` on `[1/2, 2]²`, with `V ≥ 0` measurable and bounded there, then `|I′(m⃗)| ≤ (N/q)³(c₀∫∫V + (9/4)E)`, the integrals over `[1/2, 2]`.
- `LinnikCGLSym.prop71r`: round 654's `prop71` with `W·[|m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ + m₃| ≤ Xq/N]` replaced by `W·[|m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ + m₃| ≤ Xq/N, v₂/v₁ ∈ [1/2, 2]]` (`Vr`).
- `LinnikCGLSym.Ip_cyc`: `I′(m₁, m₂, m₃) = I′(m₂, m₃, m₁)`, a renaming of the triples of points.
- `LinnikCGLSym.sum_le_three_mul`: for `f ≥ 0` with `f(a, b, c) = f(b, c, a)` and a finite `B ⊆ ℤ`, `Σ_{B³}f ≤ 3Σ_{B³}f·[|a| ≤ |b|, |c| ≤ |b|]`. At each triple, one of the three cyclic shifts puts the largest absolute value in the middle.

**The constraint `v₂/v₁ ∈ [1/2, 2]`.** Re-read this round in the text layer (spaces restored; the integral's range, the fractions, the exponents and the subscripts transcribed *(round 661: and the tildes, the integral sign and the large parentheses; review of rounds 652–657, F6)*). Their smoothed `R` is "R̃\_{M₂}(u,a) := (∫\_{u′∈[1/2,2]} (NM₂/q) ψ̃((NM₂/q)(u−u′)) |R(u′,a)|² du′)^{1/2}" (their (7.5), lines 2246–2257). The integral runs over `u′ ∈ [1/2, 2]` only. Their proof of Proposition 7.2 bounds "the inner v₂ integral" (line 2382) by Cauchy–Schwarz, and its first factor, an integral over `v₂` of `|R(v₂/v₁, b₁⁻¹b₂)|²`, by `R̃_{M₂}` at `(m₁v₁+m₃)/(−m₂v₁)`. With `u′ = v₂/v₁`, that bound holds where `v₂/v₁ ∈ [1/2, 2]`. Their Proposition 7.1, as stated, integrates over "v₁,v₂∈[1/2,2]" (lines 2041–2066) without that constraint. For `v₁ = 1/2` and `v₂` near `2`, `v₂/v₁` is near `4`, outside the range of `R̃`. The constraint holds on the support of the kernel (`Jk_eq_zero_of_ratio`), so the stack's Proposition 7.1 keeps it (`prop71r`). This is an observation about the paper's write-up, recorded here; the repair is the one line above.

**The symmetry.** "These symmetries allow us to reduce the estimation to the case |m₁| ≤ |m₃| ≤ |m₂| at the cost of a factor 6" (lines 2340–2341). Their symmetries are `I′_{m₁,m₂,m₃}` equal to the conjugate of `I′` at `(−m₂,−m₁,−m₃)`, `(−m₁,−m₃,−m₂)` and `(−m₃,−m₂,−m₁)` (lines 2336–2340, the conjugation bars read as such). This round takes only `|m₂|` largest, which their proof uses for the length of the `v₂`-interval. That comes from the cyclic symmetry, at the cost of a factor 3. Whether §11 also needs `|m₁| ≤ |m₃|` is left to its formalization.

- Their Lemma 9.2: "Let W be a finite set of pairs (t,χ), where |t| ≤ T and for (t,χ) ≠ (t′,χ′) either χ ≠ χ′ or |t−t′| ≥ (qT)^ϵ. For any M₂ > 0, we have ∫\_{v≍1} Σ\_{a mod q, (a,q)=1} |R(v,a)|⁴ dv ⪅ ϕ(q)E(W) and ∫\_{v≍1} Σ\_{a mod q, (a,q)=1} |R̃\_{M₂}(v,a)|⁴ dv ⪅\_ϵ ϕ(q)E(W)." (lines 4470–4482).
- Their majorant: "Let ψ(τ) be a smooth bump function supported on |τ| ≪ 1 such that ψ(τ/(qT)^ϵ) majorizes the range of integration." (lines 4556–4557).
- Their last step: "Due to the rapid decay of ψ̂, the summation can be restricted to |t₁+t₂−t₃−t₄| ≤ 1, incurring an error of O\_ϵ((qT)^{−100}). The proof is then completed by observing that the remaining terms contribute ⪅ ϕ(q)E(W)." (lines 4609–4612).

**An observation about their write-up.** In the display of lines 4558–4584, the majorized integral carries the Jacobian `e^τ` of `v = e^τ` (line 4571). The identity that follows, `Σ … ∫ψ(τ/(qT)^ϵ)e^{iτ(t₁+t₂−t₃−t₄)} … dτ`, has no `e^τ`. The PDF agrees: on page 39, pdfminer finds two exponentials in the row at y = 201 (superscripts `itτ` and `τ` at y = 207) and one in the row at y = 154 (superscript `iτ(t1+t2−t3−t4)` at y = 159; `scratchpad/r659/p39.txt`, from `scratchpad/r656/probe/bar.py`). Kept, `e^τ` would grow like `e^{(qT)^ϵ}` on the majorant's support. The repair costs a factor `2`: bound `e^τ ≤ 2` on the original range `|τ| ≤ log 2` before majorizing, as `lemma92` does. The conclusion of their Lemma 9.2 is unaffected. This is recorded here and in `frontier/linnik/CGL-LEAN.md`.

**At one point per character.** `energy` counts quadruples of indices. The characters of distinct indices are distinct, so `i ↦ (t_i, χ_i)` is injective on `R` and the count is their `E(W)`. `sum_norm_Rf_four` and `lemma92` need no injectivity. With `X` for their `(qT)^ϵ` and `K` large, `|R|⁴D_K/X^K` is their `O_ϵ((qT)^{−100})`. For `R̃` the stack does not use their window `|u′ − v| ≤ 4(qT)^ϵq/(M₂N)`; weighted Cauchy–Schwarz with the kernel itself, then Fubini over all `v ∈ ℝ`, gives the factor `(2X∫ψ̃₀)²`.

## Round 660: the two Cauchy–Schwarz steps of their §11 (stage M3, the `S₃` side; `external/pnt/LinnikCGLCS.lean`)

**The results.** Below, `q ≥ 1`, `L = NM₂/q ≥ 0` and `X` stands for their `(qT)^ϵ`. `B` is a finite set of triples; in use it is round 657's block `blk M k`, with `0 < |m_i| ≤ M`, `⌊log₂|m₂|⌋ = k` and `|m₁|, |m₃| ≤ |m₂|`.

- `LinnikCGLCS.sum_blk`: the triple sum of `prop72` restricted to the block `k` is the sum over `blk M k`.
- `LinnikCGLCS.cs_vb`: for nonnegative measurable `A`, `Y` bounded on `[1/2, 2]`, `∫_{[1/2,2]}Σ_bAY ≤ √(∫_{[1/2,2]}Σ_bA²)√(∫_{[1/2,2]}Σ_bY²)`, the sums over the units. It is the finite Cauchy–Schwarz inequality pointwise, then round 656's `cs_Icc`.
- `LinnikCGLCS.sum_It_eq`, `sum_It_sq_le`: `Σ_{m⃗∈B}Ĩ_{M₂}(m⃗) = ∫_{[1/2,2]}Σ_{b₁}|R(v, b₁)|Y(v, b₁) dv`, so `(Σ_{m⃗∈B}Ĩ_{M₂}(m⃗))² ≤ S₃,₁S₃,₂`. Here `Y(v, b₁) = Σ_{b₂}Σ_{m⃗∈B}R̃(c₁, b₁⁻¹b₂)R̃(c₂, b₂)(b₁m₁ − b₂m₂ + m₃, q)`, with `c₁ = (m₁v + m₃)/(m₂v)` and `c₂ = (m₁v + m₃)/m₂`, `S₃,₁ = ∫_{[1/2,2]}Σ_{b₁}|R(v, b₁)|² dv` and `S₃,₂ = ∫_{[1/2,2]}Σ_{b₁}Y² dv`.
- `LinnikCGLCS.Yb_sq_le`, `S32_le`: `Y² ≤ PQ` by Cauchy–Schwarz over `(b₂, m⃗)` with the gcd weight, so `S₃,₂ ≤ √S₃,₃·√S₃,₄`. Here `P` and `Q` are `Y` with `R̃(c₁, b₁⁻¹b₂)²` and `R̃(c₂, b₂)²` respectively in place of the product, and `S₃,₃`, `S₃,₄` are the integrals over `[1/2, 2]` of `Σ_{b₁}P²` and `Σ_{b₁}Q²`.

Then J(f⃗) ⪅ ϕ(q)M⁶(∫\_ℝ Σ\_{1≤b≤q, (b,q)=1} f_b(u) du)² + ϕ(q)²M⁴ ∫\_ℝ Σ\_{1≤b≤q, (b,q)=1} f_b(u)² du." (lines 2464–2486)

The underscores in these quotations are escaped for the renderer.

**The stack's form.** `CGLP81` makes Proposition 8.1's implicit constants explicit: the exponent `ϖ`, the support bound `A` of `|u| ≪ 1`, the constant `κ` of `|m₃| ≪ M₃`, the constants `D j` of the decay, and, for each `ε`, the constant and the threshold of their `⪅`. Read with the paper's conventions, their Proposition 8.1 implies `CGLP81`:

- the decay condition here bounds `Σ_b|f̂_b(ξ)|` by a constant times `(T/|ξ|)^jφ(q)f_{b₀}(u₀)`, and `f_{b₀}(u₀) ≤ sup f`, so it implies theirs, with `⪅_j`;
- for `j ∈ ℕ` it includes `j = 0`, and at `ξ = 0` theirs says nothing for `j ≥ 1`;
- `Jint` at any `0 < M_i < M` is at most their supremum, and the constants may depend on `ϖ`, `A`, `κ` and `D`.

The reductions take any `f` with `R̃(c, b)² ≤ f_{−b}(c)` on `[−3, 3]`; on the block, for `v ∈ [1/2, 2]`, the centre `c₂ = (m₁v + m₃)/m₂` lies in `[−3, 3]`. With `b = −b₂` the weight `(b₁m₁ − b₂m₂ + m₃, q)` is their `(b₁m₁ + bm₂ + m₃, q)`. The triples with `m₂ < 0` are the negatives of those with `m₂ > 0`, with the same centre and gcd, a factor `2`. Then `m₁` is split dyadically, `2^j ≤ |m₁| < 2^{j+1}`, which for integers is `|m₁| ∼ 2^j − 1/2`, for `j ≤ k`; likewise `m₂ ∼ 2^k − 1/2`, and `|m₃| ≤ |m₂| ≤ 2(2^k − 1/2)`, so `κ = 2`. Each block's sum is then at most their sum, whose terms are nonnegative, and Cauchy–Schwarz over the `k + 1` values of `j` gives `4(k + 1)`. For `S₃,₃`, `u = v⁻¹` maps `[1/2, 2]` onto itself with `|dv| = u⁻²du ≤ 4du` (Mathlib's `integral_image_eq_integral_abs_deriv_smul`); `b₂ = b₁b`, their unit identity, `b₁ ↦ b₁⁻¹` and the swap then give `Q` at `(u, b₁⁻¹)`.

**An observation about their write-up, for the next step.** To bound `S₃,₄` they take `f_b(v) = ψ(v)|R̃_{M₂}(v, −b)|²`, "where ψ(v) is a smooth bump function supported on v ≍ 1 and such that ψ(1) > 0" (lines 5656–5657, spaces restored). For `J(f⃗)` to bound `S₃,₄`, `f_{−b₂}` must dominate `R̃(c₂, b₂)²` wherever the centre `c₂` falls, and on the block that is all of `[−3, 3]`. A `ψ` supported on `v ≍ 1` is `0` at `c₂ = 0`. But their `ψ̃₀` is `1` on `[−1, 1]`, so `R̃(0, a)²` is at least `(NM₂/q)∫|R(u′, a)|² du′` over the `u′ ∈ [1/2, 2]` with `u′ ≤ 2(qT)^ϵq/(NM₂)`. That is positive whenever `NM₂/q < 4(qT)^ϵ` and `R(·, a)` is not zero almost everywhere there. A `ψ` equal to `1` on `[−3, 3]` and supported on `[−4, 4]` serves: it is supported on `|u| ≪ 1`, which is all Proposition 8.1 asks, and `ψ(1) = 1`. The next step takes that `ψ`. Their argument is unaffected.
